But what he cut were just two balls of shadowy mist, and in the blink of an eye, they were restored to their shadow clone forms—both of them.
“This…” Wei Donghai was stunned. Alarm bells suddenly started ringing in his heart, but it was getting harder to control his body.
Stab!
A sword pierced his chest from behind—it was a third shadow clone.
In contrast, Gu Nan himself was standing to the side, guarding against any last-ditch attacks Wei Donghai might pull if he was determined to stab the enemy behind him, even at the cost of his own injuries worsening.
As Wei Donghai’s body slowly fell down, it proved that Gu Nan’s worries were unfounded.
Almost at the same time that Wei Donghai fell, an indescribable pressure came down, and a figure appeared beside Wei Donghai.
The newcomer was a tall man with a silver mask that had a strange face painted on it.
Gu Nan recognized this pattern. In a certain ancient legend, this face represents “King.”
“To think that I was still a step too late…” The newcomer gave a small sigh with his head lowered, seemingly lamenting his inability to save his old friend.
Wei Donghai didn’t seem to be completely dead yet. Sensing the familiar presence, he opened his eyes for the final time and spoke with difficulty, “Grand Commander, avenge me…”
His voice fell. He stopped breathing before he could hear Grand Commander’s answer.
The Grand Commander reached out a hand to close Wei Donghai’s eyes, then turned to look at Gu Nan. “You still dare to openly show yourself. Aren’t you afraid that the King of the Deep Sea will strike again?”
Gu Nan knew who he was talking about but sidestepped the question. “Are you White Mist’s Grand Commander? Hand over the world mission translation method, and I can spare your lives.”
The Grand Commander shook his head lightly. “A translation method is the foundation of a reincarnator organization. How can I give it to you?”
So Gu Nan nodded and raised his hand, swinging the sword down.
The Grand Commander was a little caught off guard. He didn’t think that Gu Nan would attack without any prior warning when they were having a conversation merely seconds before.
However, such a slash wouldn’t have any impact on the Grand Commander. He slowly raised his hand, and Gu Nan’s sword actually passed right through his hand and continued traveling down.
However, his hand wasn’t injured. It was as if he had never been hit by the sword at all.
If one looked carefully, they’d find that his palm had been cut, but there was some fine yellow sand by the opening, which completely healed in the blink of an eye.
“Transforming into sand? It’s one of the nine powers of the earth…” Gu Nan’s knowledge was so vast that he recognized the other party’s roots at a glance.
Most of the powers affiliated with the earth had such characteristics—thick, heavy, solid, and extremely difficult to kill.
The Grand Commander turned part of his body into sand and easily avoided this blow, then said, “A simple swordsman like you cannot hurt me.”
His voice sounded a little distant, and it also contained an aloof feeling of looking down from above. “You humans may have unparalleled talent in comprehension and learning, but your understanding of the essence of laws is still far behind us.”
The Grand Commander was a natural–born bloodline user. True to San Wei’s words, a powerful figure like him was extremely proud of his own bloodline.
While recognizing the talents of human beings, he also mercilessly attacked their shortcomings.
As his words fell, wisps of fine sand floated up and had already surrounded Gu Nan.
The next second, the fine sand suddenly shrunk, almost crushing Gu Nan—but it’s a pity that what they crushed was just a shadow clone.
The shadow clone was crushed into a ball of black mist, but it recovered in the blink of an eye.
“Clone? Let’s see where you can run to…” The Grand Commander had an expressionless face underneath the king’s mask he wore.
Immediately after, fine sand also began to envelop Gu Nan’s other shadow clones, which suddenly tightened…
“It’s over…” Seeing the yellow sand locking Gu Nan inside and not sensing any sign of life within the sand, the Grand Commander murmured to himself.
He didn’t puzzle over how weak his opponent was. In reality, he never expected Gu Nan to be strong to begin with.
Even if the other party was a Dao Lord; even if the other party had just killed Wei Donghai easily—in the Grand Commander’s eyes, all that was just a joke.
Because he had stayed in the Dao Lord realm for too long and had accumulated experience for countless years. Although it didn’t allow him to make a successful breakthrough, it allowed his strength to accumulate indefinitely at the Dao Lord level.
With his current strength, his skill of simply crushing his opponents with sand could easily kill people at Wei Donghai’s level.
Bloodline users could improve their own strength by accumulating power over time, which was the scariest thing about them.
Although the Grand Commander told the outside world he went into secluded cultivation, in reality, he just entered a deep slumber.
The next moment, the Grand Commander turned around, but a shadow quietly appeared by his side.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: Lets Fight
chapters.content:
Shadows exist everywhere. Where there’s light, there’s shadow, and where there’s no light, shadows exist everywhere.
An ordinary shadow appeared on the dark planetary ring, and even the Grand Commander sensed nothing, not until a black sword appeared out of thin air and pierced his body.
The Grand Commander’s steps suddenly stopped as he glanced down at the black sword, an icy expression underneath his mask.
Although he was stabbed, no blood seeped out. There was only some sand blowing in the wind.
The Grand Commander slowly turned around. "Troublesome worm…"
Boom!
Before he finished that last word, Gu Nan had blasted his head apart with a punch, and his mask, hair, and facial features all turned into sand.
However, in the next second, the sand gathered together again and condensed into the Grand Commander’s head, without the mask this time.
This allowed Gu Nan to finally see his horrifying face.
This Grand Commander’s face wasn’t human, instead resembling some kind of insect. His nose and mouth were part of a single mouthpart, and his eyeballs were a pair of protruding compound eyes, reflecting Gu Nan's face in them.
"Immortality from turning into sand?" Gu Nan felt nothing upon seeing this face, but rubbed his chin and nodded in thought.
"Human, you’ve incurred my wrath!" The Grand Commander's mouthparts opened and clicked closed, making a vague sound.
He reached out a hand, which turned into a folded tentacle with fuzzy barbs, like the forelimb of some insect.
Gu Nan didn’t even glance at it as he casually sliced through that tentacle with his sword. At the same time, he switched places with a clone. The original body appeared behind the Grand Commander, stabbing a sword at the Grand Commander’s shoulder.
In addition to obtaining the skill Substitution, the power of shadows that had reached the arcana level also strengthened his existing skills.
The improved concealment effect of Hidden Shadows made him harder to find, and for Shadow Form, the number of clones that could be created greatly increased.
But correspondingly, as the number of shadow clones increased, their attack power decreased accordingly. So when conditions permitted it, Gu Nan preferred to use his original body to attack.
The Grand Commander, who had been indifferent to all of Gu Nan’s previous attacks, changed his expression slightly.
His speed was far inferior to Gu Nan's, so he could only explode his body in that instant, transforming into sand that covered the sky, then gradually reform himself nearby.
Gu Nan lifted the Observer Eyepiece on his face and gave a faint smile.
He had discovered some of the secrets behind bloodline users when he killed Qin Xuanji earlier—these fellows who relied on their bloodlines all had a source of power within their bodies. Attacking this core drastically amplified the damage dealt.
The core was the source of a bloodline user’s strength, but it was also a weakness that the enemy could exploit. Under the Observer Eyepiece, no weak spot could escape Gu Nan’s eyes.
……
In another location on the planetary ring, faint dragon roars could be heard from a place enshrouded in golden light. A group of people were rushing to White Mist’s headquarters.
"Jing’er, I can explain…" Lin Tian stood beside Fu Jing, trying to explain, while Fu Jing kept a stiff expression.
She had also heard tales of Lin Tian's romantic affairs before this, but who would’ve thought that he actually had so many women already?
‘It hasn’t even been that long since he first started cultivating!’
Lin Tian tried to explain for a while, but Fu Jing never said a word. In desperation, he could only throw a pleading look to all the women behind him.
All the women looked up at the sky, avoiding his gaze. In the end, Ling’er, the non-blood-related younger sister who grew up with Lin Tian, took the initiative to run over.
"Big Sis Fu, Big Sis Fu.” The little girl ran to Fu Jing's side and tugged on her sleeve. "Talk to me, please? If Big Bro Lin Tian did something wrong, Ling’er will beat him up for you!"
Fu Jing couldn't keep a straight face any longer after being persuaded by a little loli in such a soft and cute tone, so she could only speak up gloomily, "This playboy… you all just let him bully you like this?"
Ling’er blushed. "There's nothing we can do about it! Who let Brother Lin Tian be so powerful? There are so many big sisters who like him!"
Fu Jing felt defeated by her naivety and was unable to respond for a while.
When Lin Tian saw this, he quickly moved closer and smiled. "Jing’er, let's not discuss this for the time being. Based on the intelligence, Gu Nan should be right up ahead. We'll avenge you first!"
When this was mentioned, even the women behind Lin Tian came forward.
"That's right. That Gu Nan even dared to bully our sister. He really is tired of living…”
"Brother Lin will absolutely teach him a good lesson!"
"Exactly! We’re the only ones who can bully our sister!"
……
At White Mist’s headquarters, the Grand Commander had just reformed his body from sand for the ninth time. He no longer kept his original human appearance and had instead turned into a huge sandworm.
After Gu Nan found and attacked his core for the ninth time, the Grand Commander finally couldn't endure it anymore and revealed his bloodline transformation.
This was the last trump card of bloodline users. Each full transformation will consume a lot of energy, and they can’t stay in that form for long, so they must kill the enemy quickly.
But along with these restrictions, the form also gave them the extreme power contained within their bloodlines.
"Die!" The Grand Commander half-spoke and half-roared.
Gu Nan could barely tell what he was saying. An overwhelming sandstorm followed.
Under the Grand Commander’s control, every grain of sand contained incredible energy, and every grain of sand could smash a hole through a person’s body.
But even in such a sandstorm, Gu Nan still didn’t move.
Shadow clones couldn’t even survive inside the sandstorm and were destroyed as soon as they appeared. Such a large-scale attack really could neutralize Gu Nan's Shadow Form and Substitution skills.
"But… you’re using all your power to control the sandstorm. Just how much energy do you have left?" Gu Nan sneered as he looked at the Grand Commander, walking forward step by step.
The sandstorm scraped at his face, creating countless fine drops of blood, but couldn't stop his steps.
"Im…pos… sible…" All twelve pairs of compound eyes on the Grand Commander’s sandworm gotm stared at Gu Nan, the panic in his heart growing heavier with every step Gu Nan took toward him.
Even the strongest sandstorm couldn’t destroy this person’s body.
‘Just what is his body made of?’
"Ah!" The sandworm’s entire body rose and roared angrily at the sky. The sandstorm intensified.
Even Gu Nan’s flesh and blood began to be scraped away at this time. With every step he took, pieces of flesh fell. When he finally reached the Grand Commander, his face was almost left with nothing but bones.
But even with just a skull, the remnants of Gu Nan's lips that weren’t scraped off yet still showed a faint sneer, and his jaw opened and closed.
If his vocal cords were still there, then what he said just now was, "Come on! Let’s fight!"
His sword pierced the enemy in a single strike!
The sandworm, who was using all his power to maintain the sandstorm, couldn’t dodge. He could only take this sword head-on, letting out a wail of pain, but this was just the beginning.
The second stab, the third stab…
The sandstorm gradually stopped some time during the frenzy of attacks. There were hundreds of holes on the sandworm’s body, yet Gu Nan kept stabbing tirelessly.
Praise of Dawn began to take effect, and Gu Nan's flesh and blood gradually grew out, which felt itchy.
He stretched out his hand and scratched his face but ripped away a chunk of flesh and blood instead, then threw it aside with disdain.
The Grand Commander on the ground had already stopped moving, while Gu Nan seemed to be entirely unaware of this until a weak voice sounded beside him, "Lord, he’s already dead…"
Gu Nan suddenly turned his head and saw a slender woman standing there with a similar mask on her face.
The pattern on her mask meant "Queen."

chapters.title: Chapter 154: Red Tail
chapters.content:
The flying yellow sand had already settled onto the ground. The Grand Commander’s corpse turned back into a human again, which proved that bloodline users’ true forms were actually human, and taking on the form within their bloodline was merely a state of transformation.
Newly-grown muscles wiggled over Gu Nan’s face, and the outline of a human face could already be seen, but that just made it even more terrifying to look at.
"Looks like you don’t plan to avenge him?" Gu Nan turned his head and looked at the figure wearing the “Queen” mask. Only half of his vocal cords had regenerated, so his voice sounded very strange.
The Second Commander didn’t seem to care about that at all. She bowed down and said, "I dare not."
A hideous smile spread across Gu Nan's disfigured face.
……
"The Sand King is dead."
Above the endless void, six virtual shadows appeared in a circle, and the scholarly dressed Heavenly Mysterly Dao Lord suddenly opened his eyes and spat out those five words with a calm face.
"I originally believed the two sides would reconcile, but who would’ve expected such an outcome…" The Dragon and Phoenix Dao Lord beside him also sighed.
Each of the six Dao Lords gathered here had heard from their own information source—some slightly later than the others—but they all received news from White Mist’s headquarters.
It was extremely difficult to hide anything from Dao Lord level cultivators if they were interested in a certain place.
Swordmaster Fu Yong looked gloomy. "Why are these two so impulsive… With both of them sustaining heavy injuries, aren’t they just giving Lin Tian an opportunity to exploit?"
When the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord gave Gu Nan White Mist’s address, he simply performed a cursory check and found no obvious enmity between the two sides.
At first, they believed that even if the two sides had some minor conflicts, the chances of a major fight breaking out were still quite low. Furthermore, once Gu Nan joined White Mist, then Lin Tian’s enemy would become even more powerful.
But who could’ve imagined that it would end like this?
White Mist’s Grand Commander was an opponent that none of the six present here would dare to say they can win with absolute certainty. Even if Gu Nan could kill him, the injuries he sustained from that must be quite heavy as well…
...Could this be Lin Tian’s fortune at work again, playing a mysterious role in creating the most advantageous outcome for him?
As the originators of the practice of creating children of destiny, these six had witnessed similar situations many times. A child of destiny would somehow break their way out of a situation that was supposed to lead to certain death.
After all, fate and destiny couldn’t be completely controlled by human beings, so they were also quite helpless in the face of that.
The six were silent for a while.
Finally, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord spoke up, "Let’s divert Lin Tian’s attention from Gu Nan for the time being… I'll meet with Gu Nan again. We finally found a good target for the child of destiny to focus on; we can’t let him die so easily."
……
At White Mist’s headquarters, very few buildings remained intact after the raging sandstorm brought about by the Grand Commander's sandworm form, and there was rubble everywhere.
Members of White Mist began to come out one after another, cleaning up the broken tiles and ruins and beginning the reconstruction of the headquarters.
Gu Nan sat on a high throne in a palace deep within the headquarters, overlooking the people below.
At this time, his body had completely returned to normal, as if he hadn't gone through that great battle. Two people stood beneath him—one of them was naturally the Second Commander, the one with the Queen mask, while the other was Elder Qin.
Never in his dreams did Elder Qin think it would end like this.
He bowed his head and glanced at the back of the Second Commander out of the corner of his eyes, unable to dispel the doubts in his heart.
Gu Nan suddenly slaughtered his way to their front steps, and the Grand Commander just happened to be in secluded cultivation inside the headquarters when that happened. This was supposed to be a good thing, but who could’ve imagined that the Grand Commander would be killed by the other party?
‘The Second Commander was clearly the one who appeared back then and ordered us to stop cooperating with Gu Nan, so how come she’s cooperating with him now…’
‘And the Second Commander is usually never at headquarters, so how come she just happened to appear right now? Plus, if she was already here, then why didn’t she show up earlier to help the Grand Commander…’
Elder Qin hurriedly withdrew his gaze, trying to stop himself from thinking about it, but his thoughts ran wild against his will.
"Elder Qin, tell our subordinates that no one is allowed to divulge anything about today's events to outsiders."
The Second Commander’s voice successfully called back Elder Qin’s attention, pulling him from his thoughts. He quickly straightened up and replied, "Yes ..."
He looked up but saw that neither the Second Commander nor Gu Nan, who was sitting high on the throne, even spared him a glance, so he turned and left.
When Elder Qin’s figure disappeared completely, a mysterious smile appeared on Gu Nan’s face.
"I should have thought of it earlier. The timing of San Wei’s appearance was too coincidental, and the woman called Liu Wei at the Bloodline Alliance’s branch office seemed to be acting strangely as well… So you were the mastermind controlling them."
Gu Nan has always had a good memory.
At the beginning, his meeting with San Wei was just an accident, while the latter offered to be his maid in order to join White Mist.
Although the logic behind her request was slightly far-fetched, Gu Nan didn't ponder it too deeply at that time. But now that he was looking back, he realized something was off.
Even the woman called Liu Wei, who appeared in the Bloodline Alliance’s branch office, had a strange attitude. Her words at that time seemed to resemble a deliberate provocation rather than an attempt at peaceful conflict resolution.
Now, when he thought about San Wei and Liu Wei’s similar names
[1]
and their aura, which resembled that of the Second Commander in front of him, certain things became clear.
"As expected, I can’t keep it from Lord," the Second Commander said with a smile, then stretched out her hand and took off the mask on her face.
Underneath the mask was a beautiful face, which was somewhat similar to Lin Yunyun's.
Gu Nan raised his eyebrows slightly and asked, "Lin Yunyun is…?"
"My daughter," the Second Commander answered bluntly.
Gu Nan immediately became amused. They had conversed for quite a while, but he finally realized that Lin Yunyun was the other party’s ultimate goal. Perhaps the Second Commander had worked out this series of plans from the moment San Wei first discovered Lin Yunyun.
“You people always like to complicate things." Gu Nan waved his hand a few times. "Why didn’t you just tell me to use Lin Yunyun and that sandworm’s head to exchange for the world mission translation method?"
That’s right. The reason Gu Nan and the Second Commander could sit down and have a genial discussion was because the latter promised to hand over what Gu Nan needed.
The Second Commander just smiled without saying anything.
Only those with absolute power could use such a straightforward method. Other people could only use their brains.
But the outcome was the same as Gu Nan’s words. As part of the deal, she received Lin Yunyun and a White Mist that no longer had the Grand Commander, while Gu Nan would get the translation method he wanted.
Gu Nan didn't give this more thought. He slowly stood up and said, "It's your turn to honor your promise…"
The Second Commander nodded lightly as she turned and walked towards the door. "Please follow me."
When Gu Nan and the Second Commander came to the door, he suddenly asked, "Third Tail and Sixth Tail are both your doppelgangers? So how many tails are you?"
"It's more appropriate to say that they’re my reincarnations. Everyone in our clan is like this, but Third Tail and Sixth Tail are both entirely unaware of their connection to me." The Second Commander replied with a chuckle, "As for me…"
She leaned in slightly with a charming smile. "Lord can call me Red Tail."
Gu Nan turned his head to see a red fox tail swaying up and down behind her, so he nodded expressionlessly. "Then you’re Big Tail."
"Where did you get that from?" The Second Commander paused in confusion.
"From the Calabash Brothers
[2]
."
T/N:
[1]
Names:
San Wei = Third Tail
Liu Wei = Sixth Tail
Red Tail = Red Tail
Please excuse the inconsistency. San Wei and Liu Wei don’t show up that often after this, and gonna use Red Tail instead of the pinyin “Hong Wei” because her name is pretty literal.
[2] Calabash Brothers:
Pretty old Chinese animation:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabash_Brothers
The main characters are the seven calabash brothers, and their names are translated as Big Brother, Second Brother, Third Brother, etc., so as the leader of her doppelgängers/clones, Red Tail would be named “Big Tail” going by that naming convention. Also by that convention, San Wei would actually be Third Tail, and Liu Wei would be Sixth Tail.
Index

chapters.title: Chapter 155: Translation Method—Mirror of White Mist
chapters.content:
A golden radiance was still flying forward over the planetary ring. Lin Tian and his harem would soon arrive at the headquarters of White Mist.
At this time, however, one of the girls suddenly frowned and hurriedly asked Lin Tian to stop.
"Bingyu, what's wrong?" Lin Tian looked back strangely at the woman who opened her mouth.
He Bingyu was one of Lin Tian's confidantes. At the same time, she was also a disciple of Heavenly Mystery Dao Hall and could be considered one of the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s disciples, so she originally held a high position in Heavenly Mystery Dao Hall.
"My Dao Hall just received new information. Gu Nan fought White Mist’s Sand King. Both sides suffered heavy injuries, and Gu Nan has already left White Mist."
He Bingyu's face was frosty, as if there would never be any expression on her face. Only when she looked at Lin Tianshi would her expression contain a little tenderness.
"It’s a good thing that Sister Yu is here, or else we would’ve made another trip in vain!" Ling’er patted her little chest and laughed again. "It probably never occurred to them that we’d have an insider like Sister Yu inside their Dao Hall."
Because of He Bingyu's existence, they could receive immediate updates on Gu Nan’s whereabouts and all kinds of latest information on the continent.
And He Bingyu sincerely loved Lin Tian, so she’d never deceive them.
But it never occurred to them that although He Bingyu might be trustworthy, the information she obtained might not be.
……
"The process of reading the wills of various worlds and clearly writing out the goals they want us to accomplish is called translation."
"By carrying out a world’s will, that world’s origin will repay us—in many cases, that will be a direct demonstration of certain laws, which is of great benefit to us."
Red Tail’s sweet voice continuously echoed, while Gu Nan read the files in his hands and listened to her explanation.
"Who do you mean by 'us’?" Gu Nan suddenly interrupted her.
"Of course it's people like us, who are only a step away from Void Cutter Realm." Red Tail gave Gu Nan an odd look, not understanding why he’d ask this question.
In her eyes, Gu Nan was merely half a step away from that realm. ‘How can he not understand how beneficial a direct demonstration of laws is?’
Gu Nan sensed her surprise but could only secretly roll his eyes—he relied on Evil Value to level up. Since when did he have to comprehend the laws by himself?
After combining Red Tail’s words, as well as the documents in his hands, Gu Nan also gained a general understanding of a world’s will.
It wasn’t strange to receive a present after carrying out the world’s will. In fact, the expression "carrying out justice on heaven’s behalf" appeared a long time ago.
Some cultivators in ancient times actually received gifts from the Dao of Heaven because their actions just happened to agree with heaven’s will. As a result, their cultivation levels soared, and they were considered people who had contributed great merits to heaven and earth.
In the eyes of modern cultivators, the theory of merit was of course nonexistent, but the existence of the world’s will wasn’t a lie.
To put it bluntly, “translating” the world’s will meant being the first to seize the opportunity—as the translator of the world’s will, no matter who completes the mission after that, the world’s will would always reward the translator.
In game terms, Gu Nan understood this as the world missions existing in a mission hall, while translators seek and accept missions here.
There might be a large number of missions inside the mission hall, so translators usually tell others about missions and hire people to help them with it.
"People who translate the will of the world are called prophets and heavenly masters in some planes, but in most places, they have a unified name…" Red Tail looked up and said, "Heavenly Emissaries."
Those who fulfill the will of heaven were Heavenly Emissaries.
Gu Nan nodded, "What’s your translation method? Take it out."
Gu Nan was purely treating the earlier explanation as part of the story plot, but what he really cared about was the translation method.
Without further delay, Red Tail handed another document to Gu Nan while saying, "As for how to become a Heavenly Emissary, the information itself isn’t valuable, but the hard part is experience and… power."
Gu Nan looked up at her, then continued reading the file, because the first page of this document already pointed that out clearly.
If someone wanted to become a Heavenly Emissary, they must at least be an experienced Dao Lord and have a preliminary understanding of their own exclusive law. It would be even better if they were actually a Void Cutter Realm cultivator.
Because no matter the translation method, cultivators essentially had to use their understanding of laws to interact with and comprehend the world’s will, so as to translate world missions.
The translation method owned by White Mist was called "Mirror of White Mist." By creating a mirror covered with white mist, the world’s will be projected onto it, and cultivators can then explore and search through the missions list bit by bit.
"Mirror of White Mist" was a high-grade translation method, and even the organization’s name—White Mist—was derived from it.
"Interesting… Do you have a finished mirror?" After reading through the entire document, Gu smiled with great interest and asked Red Tail.
"Yes." Red Tail was already prepared and immediately nodded. Originally, White Mist only had two Heavenly Emissaries—the Sand King and her, so naturally they had extra mirrors lying around.
Red Tail took out a palm-sized mirror and handed it to Gu Nan. The mirror was obscured by a thick white mist, which made it impossible for people to see its true appearance.
At the same time, Red Tail also took out another mirror, where only a small portion was obscured by white mist. This was the mirror Red Tail used.
In the areas where the mist had been dispersed, a resplendent starry sky appeared on the mirror, so deep that people could lose themselves in it.
Red Tail brushed the mirror with one hand and explained, "By gradually eroding the mist with the power of your own laws, you can… eh?"
Halfway through her explanation, she saw Gu Nan raise the mirror expressionlessly, the power of shadows pouring out crazily from his hand and messily sweeping away the mist surrounding the mirror.
Although some "die-hard" areas were still covered with white mist, all of a sudden, more than 80% of the mist was washed away by Gu Nan.
"This…" Red Tail’s eyes almost popped out. It's not that she hadn’t seen other Heavenly Emissaries, and she had even seen people translate at a faster speed than Gu Nan, but those were all Void Cutter powerhouses!
She couldn't help glancing up at Gu Nan.
‘This young man, who was seriously injured by the King of the Deep Sea not long ago, is now merely an inch away from Void Cutter Realm?’
Gu Nan didn't care about her thoughts. He was busy scanning the surface of the mist mirror quickly, and sure enough, world missions were displayed one after another.
Some were tedious, some were simple; some came from famous large planes, while some planes were names he’d never heard of… But in sum, hundreds of missions were displayed in front of Gu Nan.
Gu Nan heaved out a mouthful of turbid air. He had been looking for ways to translate the world missions ever since meeting Lu Zhanyu on Ruby Fish Star.
Finally achieving his goal after scheming for a long time…
Even with Gu Nan's composure, at this time, he couldn’t help revealing a joyous expression.
He was a player. He could ignore the joy, anger, and sorrows of NPCs and the life and death of monsters, but he couldn’t ignore leveling up and clearing missions.
In a sense, this was the purpose of Gu Nan's existence as a player.

chapters.title: Chapter 156: On How to Identify a Mysterious Expert
chapters.content:
The reason top players are top players is because they won’t be carried away by excitement; they always keep a clear mind.
"How are mirrors made?" Gu Nan didn't even take a deeper look at the translated missions and asked directly.
The missions were already there, so they wouldn’t run away. What Gu Nan needed the most right now was how to create these mirrors—this was the only missing link in this whole translation process.
"The Mirror of White Mist is a vessel for the world's will, and different translation methods have different vessel production methods," Red Tail started introducing the production process Gu Nan.
With her explanation, Gu Nan also learned how to make the mirrors.
It was actually related to the children of destiny on Heaven and Earth Star—the main ingredient for these mirrors was the fate accumulated by a child of destiny.
The basic principle behind the mist mirrors was to use the fortuitous fate to make contact with world wills, then engrave that onto the mirror made of special materials.
"So you guys are the ones behind those children of destiny?" Gu Nan asked with some amusement.
"Of course not." Red Tail shook her head violently. "A child of destiny’s fortune and fate are the foundation of these mirrors, so we naturally want to hide it. How can we do this right in front of our own doorstep?"
Gu Nan also nodded when he heard this. For reincarnators like them, it was really easy to find a random small plane and start collecting the fortune and fate from there. Why would they carry this out on their home planet and risk others discovering their goals?
"However, the fortune and fate in Star Realm is far thicker than that of smaller worlds, which is why that group of people couldn’t resist the temptation and started to experiment right on Heaven and Earth Star…"
When she said this, Red Tail's face showed some mockery. She then added, "Lord can read more about this matter and the required materials in the document."
……
An hour later, Red Tail left to oversee the ongoing reconstruction of the headquarters, while Gu Nan stood alone inside the archives room of White Mist, leafing through the files that had been sorted out.
Actually, it wasn’t quite accurate to say he’s alone, because someone else was helping him sort out the information, and she was also a familiar face.
Perhaps because Gu Nan already knew her, Red Tail sent San Wei over.
This was a girl who was clearly pure in temperament yet insisted on dressing herself up to be extremely bewitching on Heavenly Enterprise Star. However, she wasn’t wearing any makeup right now and looked like a girl next door.
"My Lord, this is the information you wanted…" San Wei’s forehead was full of sweat, as if she was standing on a stove, and she dared not stop walking for even a second, trying to find tasks to do.
"Mm." Gu Nan took the file in passing, then said with a chuckle, "Stop swaying around. Sit down. I’m almost done reading it."
San Wei’s face turned white, and she sat down while trembling, not even daring to glance at Gu Nan.
She was indeed fearful to the extreme. After all, she had witnessed Gu Nan's brutality first-hand and just happened to run into him again in White Mist. There was nothing more terrifying than this.
When they were both in Heavenly Enterprise Star, she was the one who betrayed him and left with Lin Yunyun back when rumors of his supposed death were spreading!
But at that time, she never could’ve imagined that this person would actually slaughter his way to White Mist’s headquarters and kill the Grand Commander!
‘And it looks like he’s going to rule White Mist from now on…’
At the thought of this, San Wei felt her head go blank, and her future seemed to plunge directly into purgatory.
Gu Nan looked at her with some amusement.
According to Red Tail, San Wei was one of her reincarnated clones, and their souls were connected, so Red Tail could easily influence San Wei's actions.
But looking at San Wei’s behavior, it was obvious that San Wei herself was entirely unaware of this. She believed that she was her own person.
Such a technique was truly terrifying.
But Gu Nan didn’t care about that. Be it San Wei or Lin Yunyun, neither their identities nor their so-called betrayals meant anything to Gu Nan.
Gu Nan would never help an NPC of his own volition. He would only ever do so because of missions, so the relationship between him and anyone else in this world was always a business transaction to the satisfaction of both parties. Gu Nan won’t consider other people’s feelings, but at the same time, he won’t demand anyone’s loyalty either. After all, in the game world, players have long gotten accustomed to this kind of event—an NPC they saved after much difficulty would someday randomly drop out of their party just because the plot demanded it.
San Wei was a trivial matter. Gu Nan was most concerned about the child of destiny.
White Mist’s archives clearly documented this event. The method of collecting someone’s fortune and fate was leaked in an accident fifty years ago.
An important member of White Mist died outside the organization in the middle of a mission. That person just happened to be returning to headquarters with all of the collected fate, and the member’s body was discovered by the six nearby Dao Lords.
After that, children of destiny gradually began to appear in Heaven and Earth Star.
It was clear that those six Dao Lords started experimenting with the information they stumbled across.
White Mist’s files also recorded information on all six Dao Lords, as well as when and where they created their children of destiny.
And among the various test subjects they created, the two most typical ones were naturally listed in the data.
"Ye Chen? Lin Tian?" Gu Nan almost had the urge to laugh when he saw those two stereotypical names.
It seemed that no matter the world, the main characters would always be similar—only the side characters were different.
"U-Uncle," a faltering voice came over. Lin Yunyun was standing at the door with her head down. "The Second Commander asked you to come over…"
Gu Nan nodded and stood up. He also wanted to ask Red Tail something face to face.
When he walked past Lin Yunyun, he reached a hand out and rubbed her hair with a smile, looking at her like she was a long-lost puppy who had finally found her way back home.
……
When he returned to the throne room that the Sand King built for himself, Red Tail was already waiting there.
The first sentence she spoke upon seeing Gu Nan surprised the latter, "The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord is here."
"Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord? If I recall correctly, he’s among those six Dao Lords, right? Yet he still dared to visit?" Gu Nan asked, as if laughing at the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s foolishness.
Red Tail, however, said seriously, "Of those six Dao Lords, the other five are all worthless trash who have lived comfortably for far too long and lost their edge. Only the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord cannot be underestimated."
"Oh?" Gu raised his eyebrows and recalled his meeting with the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord but didn't recall seeing anything special.
Besides practically writing the words “mysterious expert” on his face, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord didn’t seem too clever in his actions.
As if guessing Gu Nan's thoughts, Red Tail said, "What’s written on his face might not necessarily be true, and his actions might not necessarily be genuine either. If my other clone didn’t infiltrate that side, then I wouldn’t have known this either."
When she said that side, she naturally meant the six Dao Lords’ side.
This made Gu Nan pause slightly. He then nodded seriously as well. "That’s true… Looks like we’ll have to test him to see if he really is a mysterious expert."
"How can we test him?" Red Tail frowned.
The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord never left an opening for anyone to exploit. If he didn’t want to reveal his true power, then who would be able to test him? She had made similar attempts herself, all of which failed.
Gu Nan didn't explain much and just asked directly, "Where's the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord? Just let him in."
Moments later, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord walked into the throne room leisurely, still dressed like a scholar. His expression looked mysterious.
Red Tail didn't look at him; instead, she turned to Gu Nan. She was curious how Gu Nan planned to test the other party.
Gu Nan just smiled faintly, his thoughts indiscernible.
When the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord walked to the foot of the throne, he gently opened his fan and was about to speak, but he saw Gu Nan suddenly disappear from the throne, while a crimson blade sliced through the air.
Gu Nan already had Blade of the Sanguine King in his hand and had just slashed downwards!
"If he can be killed by this, then he’s definitely not a mysterious expert." Gu Nan used the simplest identification method.

chapters.title: Chapter 157: Law of Causality
chapters.content:
In the throne room deep inside White Mist’s headquarters, the sudden flash of bloody light not only dumbfounded the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord, but it also left Red Tail stupefied.
No matter how you looked at it, both Red Tail and the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord could be considered smart people.
But the smarter they were, the more they’d overthink things, and the less they’d be able to understand the thoughts of a lunatic like Gu Nan.
But they understood at least one thing: Gu Nan really did intend to kill the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord just now and didn’t hold back in that attack.
When the blade fell, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord seemed to be standing in place motionlessly, but as the blade was about to touch him, the slash suddenly missed, striking the spot to his left.
Red Tail looked at him with a grave expression. She had never seen the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord in battle before, so she was secretly on the alert when the strike missed.
As White Mist’s distinguished Second Commander and a bloodline user who had lived for several hundred years, Red Tail's knowledge was by no means shallow.
However, she was unable to see through the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s move just now.
"He didn’t dodge or manipulate space. It wasn’t an illusion, and he didn’t switch places with a clone…" Red Tail muttered to herself as she fixed the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord with a stare, her mind full of confusion.
Gu Nan’s simple slash couldn’t be dodged at all, yet the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord used unknown means to force this strike to miss.
The feeling he gave off was as if… he’d been there all along.
The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s expression remained unchanged, but there was a hint of a smile deep within his eyes— ‘If my skills can be seen through so easily, then wouldn’t it be too cheap to call myself Heavenly Mystery?’
"A causality skill?" Gu Nan, however, stopped his action and spat out three words, looking a little surprised.
Causality skills were a special law that reversed cause and effect. Its absolute strength wasn’t high, but its application was very clever.
For example, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord proclaimed that this strike wouldn’t hit him, so no matter how Gu Nan aimed that slash, it would never hit him.
But the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord almost tripped and fell when he heard Gu Nan. He looked at Gu Nan like he was looking at a ghost, too speechless to speak for a while.
Gu Nan put away his blade and nodded encouragingly. "To be able to awaken the law of causality—you’re certainly qualified to act mysterious."
"How… How did you know…" The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord had never seen someone guess his law correctly simply by seeing one skill before.
Gu Nan just smiled and shook his head.
If he had to say the one thing he was most knowledgeable about in this world, it wouldn’t be the dungeons in his previous life or the various gods’ secrets. It would be the power system here, which closely resembled the one inside the game.
Starting from Tier 3—Prodigious Realm—understanding the various laws and building their own exclusive laws were all things that players had researched inside-out.
The law of causality might sound incredible, but in the game, it was merely average—any law had its advantages and disadvantages, and causality was no exception.
However, this type of skill really was suitable for acting mysterious, so Gu Nan recognized the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s right to pretend to be a mysterious expert.
Unable to get an answer, the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord asked Gu Nan another question after seeing Gu Nan put his weapon away, "Mr. Gu doesn't want to kill this poor Daoist anymore?"
Gu Nan didn't care about his odd form of self-address. Instead, he looked at the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord strangely. "There’s no enmity between us. Why would I want to kill you?"
Even someone as calculating and shameless as the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord choked upon hearing those self-confident words.
‘Bastard, now you know there’s no enmity between us?’
Gu Nan, however, ignored his attitude and bluntly said, "I'll just call you Heavenly Mystery… Forget it, that’s not very civilized. What do you want to see me about?"
The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord gave him a deep look, collected his emotions, and resumed his indifferent and calm expression. "Lin Tian is an old acquaintance of Fu Jing’s."
……
The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord quickly left.
The owner of the law of causality seemed like he came here just to get attacked, tell Gu Nan an insignificant piece of news, and then leave mysteriously.
"It’s difficult to confirm the outcome of Lord’s battle with the Sand King. Perhaps the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord paid a visit to see if you’re injured,” Red Tail immediately thought of this.
"Perhaps." Gu Nan smiled, seeming unconcerned. "Help me pick up someone. Her name is Lan Si… You should be able to find her, right?"
Red Tail smiled. "Of course. We’ve known Lord’s whereabouts ever since you set foot on this planet."
"That's good." Gu Nan stood up and was about to leave the throne room, but after thinking about it, he sat down again. "I'll live here in the future. You can leave."
This throne room reminded him of the empty Evil God Temple, and suddenly he wanted to stay here for a long time.
Red Tail looked at him curiously but didn’t say another word. She had seen too many powerful figures’ strange hobbies back when she was still a young fox.
But just as she was about to leave the throne room, she suddenly turned around and asked, "My Lord, what is the law of causality?"
"To specify a law and assign it the highest priority—this is the law of causality," Gu Nan explained casually. Then, as if afraid that Red Tail wouldn't understand, he added, "For example, if you put on a pair of black-rimmed glasses and red clothes, then one minute will only have 59 seconds."
……
Gu Nan didn’t give the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord and the law of causality too much thought.
After reading the archives carefully and fully understanding how to create a mirror, he finally took out the mirror eagerly and studied the missions on it.
This mirror was the one that Red Tail gave him, and he had dispersed most of the mist with the power of shadows.
The Evil God Temple was a very straightforward game system. Once his Evil Value reached the requirement, the system would give him the most standard realm and power corresponding to that level, without fail.
His Evil Value was currently at 300, which was the arcana level. That was the equivalent of a full EXP bar at Tier 3, so no one could be closer to Tier 4 than him.
Because of this, the mist on the mirror in front of him seemed so weak.
Gu Nan used his mind to slowly examine each mission on the mirror. At the same time, his hand continuously jotted down the mission content and requirements.
Unlike ordinary Heavenly Emissaries, others usually looked for easy missions first to give to their subordinates or complete themselves, but Gu Nan only looked for missions from large planes.
Small missions that gave only a couple Evil Value couldn’t even enter Gu Nan’s eyes anymore. The mission planes he wanted had to be at least as large as Immortal Demon World.
Gu Nan probably cleared away 90% of the mist on this mirror, but there were only a few dozen missions in it.
According to this estimate, an entire mirror would probably have around 50 missions.
Gu Nan spent another hour removing all of the remaining mist, then translated the mission information and listed them on a piece of paper.
"A total of 52 missions. If sorted and screened according to the mission plane… There you are!"
Gu Nan checked the mission planes’ information one by one and finally found a suitable target.
The Morningstar Plane was a mid- to large-sized plane with many powerful Dao Lords. Not only did the scale meet Gu Nan's requirements, but the power level was also just right…
Just as Gu Nan was about to check the mission content, a figure suddenly broke into the hall. It was precisely Red Tail.
She rushed in without even a greeting, and her expression didn't look very good. As soon as she arrived, she said, "My Lord, the situation has changed…"
Gu Nan slowly put away the paper and calmly asked, "Is it Lan Si’s situation?"
"Yes." Red Tail gave a small nod. "When our people got there, there were already people making a scene at the Tang family residence…"

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Harem of Corpses
chapters.content:
On Heaven and Earth Star, Tang family residence.
"Young Master Lin, this woman named Lan Si was brought in by one of our family’s juniors. I’m also unaware of her specific origin!" An elder in brocade clothes was standing in front of Lin Tian, complaining.
This person was the head of the Tang family, Tang Bo. Lan Si sat next to him and Lin Tian, her face full of innocence.
Before Lin Tian even spoke, the dozen or so women behind him had already surrounded them.
"How can you allow a woman of unknown origin inside your home?"
"You might not know her, but what about Tang Xuan? Have her come out and confront us!"
"That's right! If Gu Nan doesn't return, you can apologize to our Sister Jing in his place!"
"Apologize! Apologize!"
Faced with the siege of over a dozen beautiful girls, Tang Bo could only respond with a bitter smile as he tried to placate each one. While apologizing, his heart also felt extremely stifled.
He was the distinguished patriarch of the Tang family. Since when has he ever experienced something like this?
Speaking of which, it was quite strange. He’d always managed his family rather strictly, so his family’s servants rarely used their status to bully others.
But today, two foolish servants actually taunted Lin Tian right in front of their front gates… How could such a thing happen?
Tang Bo wouldn't even have believed it if he hadn't seen it with his own eyes.
But the damage was already done, and his family inexplicably offended a Dao Lord powerhouse.
Fortunately, Tang Bo responded quickly. After understanding the situation, he immediately ordered Tang Xuan to hide while he took Lan Si along, trying to resolve the situation.
"Alright, alright. Don’t bully the Tang family head." Finally, Lin Tian clapped and motioned for the women to step down, preventing the Tang residence from turning into a chatty street market.
It's just that after such an uproar, Fu Jing's relationship with the other women improved greatly, and she even started calling them sisters.
Even Fu Jing herself didn’t know why she, someone who used to be firmly against harems, seemed to accept the dozen women for no reason…
Lin Tian went to Tang Bo and said, "Patriarch Tang, I know this matter has nothing to do with you. I'm only here to find Gu Nan."
Tang Bo seemed to heave a sigh of relief and said gratefully, "Young Master Lin, thank you for your understanding…"
At this time, Lan Si cut in, "If you’re just looking for him, then this also has nothing to do with me, right?"
"How can it have nothing to do with you?" When Fu Jing heard this, she immediately walked over angrily. "You and Gu Nan are on the same side!"
Fu Jing had seen Lan Si and Gu Nan traveling together on the starship.
"Jing’er, listen to me." Lin Tian, however, said firmly, "We only punish the evil leader. We must not hurt the innocent… Although I have no respect for heaven and earth in this life, all I seek is a clear conscience!"
When Lin Tian said this, the illusory forms of nine golden dragons circled him, as if roaring, and his figure suddenly seemed much more majestic.
And in the eyes of everyone present, a faint golden radiance seemed to be emanating from him. He didn’t resemble a mortal at all, as if he was an immortal or a Buddha.
"Big Brother Lin Tian…"
"Elder Brother Lin…"
All the women stared at him with eyes full of yearning. Even Fu Jing was immersed in this atmosphere, and her original goodwill towards Lin Tian gradually turned into an inexplicable feeling of admiration and worship.
Next to them, Tang Bo was also secretly frightened. In his perception, Lin Tian's image was elevated yet again, turning from someone he couldn’t offend to someone he absolutely must establish friendly relations with.
Only Lan Si wasn’t affected. After all, she possessed a Godhead. She just stared at Lin Tian curiously.
However, just when everyone’s attention was drawn to Lin Tian’s majestic aura, a figure leisurely walked in, completely ignoring all this, and stopped before Lan Si.
"Let's go,” the person said thus to Lan Si, not even sparing Lin Tian a glance.
His movements were so natural that Lin Tian and his party didn't even react in time.
It wasn’t until Lan Si obediently stood up and started walking outside that Fu Jing exclaimed, "He… He’s Gu Nan!"
"Him?" Lin Tian stared blankly, a bit confused as he studied this ordinary-looking youth.
He’d long gotten used to his opponents always being tall and handsome geniuses. All of them were arrogant jerks just asking for a beating.
But he couldn’t muster even an ounce of competitive spirit against this bland-looking fellow!
"He doesn't look very strong!" Among the women, a tall woman chuckled, "Sister Jing, your Big Sis will teach him a lesson!”
Then she actually shouted to Gu Nan, "Hey, you there! Gu something—you bullied our Sister Jing. I’ll forgive you if you can survive my throwing knife, how about it?"
Fu Jing was worried when she heard this, but Ling’er smiled reassuringly beside her. "Sister Jing need not worry. Sister Pearl comes from a family that uses throwing knives. Even Prodigious cultivators are wary of their throwing knives…"
As if to confirm her words, Pearl didn't bother waiting for Gu Nan’s response. She raised her hand and threw the blade.
This knife was as quick as lightning, heading straight for Gu Nan, who didn’t make any movements to dodge.
A smile had already appeared on Pearl’s face, but her expression suddenly changed in the next second.
There was a flash of white light, and the throwing knife flew back towards her at several times its original speed!
"Look out!" Lin Tian’s voice boomed, but speed wasn’t his forte. When he flew to Pearl, it was already too late…
The throwing knife was embedded in Pearl’s forehead, and the girl who was originally smiling like a flower had died with her eyes wide open.
"No!" Lin Tian’s eyes widened, almost shedding tears of blood as he held Pearl in his arms and screamed up at the sky.
"Sister Pearl!"
"Elder Sister Pearl! ！”
The women also wailed in sorrow. Ling’er, who was the first to follow Lin Tian and also had the closest relationship with everyone, had already burst into tears.
Gu Nan looked like he suddenly remembered something when he saw this and asked Lan Si beside him, "Is that Lin Tian?"
"Yes." Lan Si nodded, then took two steps back, sensing that a large battle was about to break out.
Gu Nan finally understood. ‘So this is that child of destiny, the one who can be used to create over half of a mirror.’
The gaze with which he looked at Lin Tian immediately changed.
Lin Tian gently placed Pearl's corpse down with trembling hands and stood up.
He glared at Gu Nan, the veins bulging out on his face, and slowly enumerated every word, "You will pay…"
But before his words finished, Gu Nan's Blade of the Sanguine King had already arrived, and the crimson arc drawn by the blade sent him flying, crashing straight through three of the Tang family’s high-rise buildings.
"Brother Lin Tian…" Tears fell straight down from Ling’er’s round eyes, and she ran at Gu Nan. "You… I’m gonna kill you!"
What greeted her was naturally a slash of the blade, so the lovely little Ling’er fell down, dead on the spot.
"Ling’er!" He Bingyu shouted sorrowfully and jumped into the air, crazily circulating the internal energy in her body.
She raised both of her hands, and two huge Yin Yang fish appeared above her head, circling each other swiftly. "Heavenly Mystery Art, Last Style—Forbidden Technique · Reversing Heav–”
Swish!
Blade of the Sanguine King swung down, cutting both her and the fish in half—this brilliant student of the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord didn’t have the chance to finish shouting the name of her move.
Besides Ling’er and He Bingyu, Lin Tian’s dozen or so women all exploded with potential when they realized that Lin Tian's life and death were uncertain, taking out their trump cards one after another.
Hidden weapons, poison, firearms, illusions… All kinds of skills dazzled the eyes.
Lin Tian’s harem covered almost 80% of the skills on the continent, but it's a pity that these skills were useless in front of Gu Nan.
No matter how many tricks they tried, no one could block a single strike from that blade.
In just a few seconds, the corpses of over a dozen beautiful girls were sprawled all over the floor. Except for Pearl, the first one to die from the throwing knife, none of them had intact corpses.
Among the ones who died by Gu Nan’s blade, the lightest injuries were severed arms and decapitated heads, while the majority were directly sliced in half.
Of the group of beautiful women, only Fu Jing remained. She joined the harem the latest and had the deepest fear of Gu Nan, so she didn't have the courage to attack him.
She just looked as pale as paper as she watched Gu Nan approach her step by step. Her legs went weak, and she suddenly crumpled to the ground.
Lin Tian, who had been sent flying, managed to regain his senses only now. He stared at the long gash on his chest and rushed back to the battleground, but what he saw was a scene that made him want to tear his eyes out.
His dozen or so women had turned into chopped bodies…
"Ahhh!" Lin Tian roared at the sky in agony. He rushed at Gu Nan like a crazed demon and threw a punch with all his power.
His Nine Dragons Body Tempering Art was used to the extreme, and his physical strength almost reached the limit of Prodigious Realm. The power of this one punch could practically kill Dao Lords.
However, his opponent was Gu Nan. Gu Nan doesn’t need almost—he is the limit.
Gu Nan’s blade drew a gentle arc, and Lin Tian's right arm was cut off directly; blood gushed out.
But Lin Tian wasn’t dismayed in the slightest. Instead, he laughed wildly. "Die! Die for me!"
It turned out that his severed right arm didn't stop. It swooped down with unparalleled ferocity, the nine dragons coiled around it.
He traded an arm for a chance to hit Gu Nan!
Thwack!
This punch hit Gu Nan on the shoulder, making a dull noise. Time seemed to have stopped at this moment.
Lin Tian stared at Gu Nan intensely, but the latter still didn’t fall, so the grin on his face gradually froze.
After a while, Lin Tian's severed arm had already fallen to the ground. Only then did Gu Nan reach out and rub the spot where he’d been hit while muttering, "Protagonist halos really are powerful. Even I feel some pain from this."
As he spoke, the force of shadows poured out around him and completely wrapped around the stunned Lin Tian, directly dispersing all the internal energy in his body and sealing his five senses in passing.
Gu Nan still wanted to take him back to White Mist and use his fate to create a mist mirror, so of course he couldn’t let Lin Tian die.
But at this moment, a voice came from mid-air, "Mr. Gu, please wait… We’ve been hunting Lin Tian for a long time. Is it possible for Mr. Gu to give him to us?"
At the same time six new figures appeared—they were precisely the six great Dao Lords. Fu Yong the swordmaster was the one who spoke up.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: One Slash, Six Attacks
chapters.content:
Fu Yong's face was full of smugness. Although it wasn’t his idea to make Gu Nan and Lin Tian fight each other, he still felt quite proud right now.
He also witnessed Lin Tian’s final blow. ‘No matter how strong Gu Nan is, how can he not be hurt after taking that punch?’
They only needed three Dao Lords to defeat peak-strength Lin Tian, so now that an injured Gu Nan was facing all six of them, how could he resist at all?
Fu Jing, who had collapsed to the side, seemed like she saw her savior and immediately rushed over. "Daddy… Daddy, I’ll definitely listen to you from now on…"
She hugged Fu Yong's arm. Her face was full of joy from the new lease on life she’d just gotten.
"Hmph, you unruly girl… Now you remember to look for your father?" Fu Yong snorted softly. Although his words were harsh, his hand pushed her behind him protectively.
After all, she was still his daughter, and Fu Yong couldn’t bear to see anything happen to her.
At this time, Gu Nan had already given Lin Tian’s severed arm and his completely sealed body to Lan Si, while he himself walked forward, holding a bloody blade.
His destination was naturally the six great Dao Lords.
Fu Yong’s expression couldn’t help darkening when he saw Gu Nan approach slowly with a blade that still glowed crimson.
"Does Mr. Gu truly intend to make an enemy of us?" Fu Yong asked in a low voice. He mistakenly believed that Gu Nan didn't understand his situation yet. "Forget it. Let this old man give some introductions to Mr. Gu. This one is the Dragon Phoenix Dao Lord, and this is…"
As soon as Fu Yong pointed to the Dragon Phoenix Dao Lord, Gu Nan suddenly raised his blade and split into six shadowy figures, each making the same slashing motion.
"You…" Fu Yong glared angrily, but he wasn’t known as a swordmaster for nothing. At this critical juncture, he drew his sword from his waist and tried to block the attack.
But he never could’ve imagined that Gu Nan would have an unparalleled advantage in fighting Dao Lords like him who specialized in frontal assaults.
The max Tier 3 experience bar from the Evil God Temple gave him strength that was at the very peak of Tier 3, while Blade of the Sanguine King also brought him extremely high attack power.
Although it might be hard to kill experts with strange abilities like the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord in one blow, people like Lin Tian and Fu Yong were Gu Nan’s favorite type of enemies.
Under the scarlet glow, Fu Yong's sword broke cleanly into two pieces, only managing to block Blade of the Sanguine King for a single instant.
Fu Yong, this distinguished swordmaster, didn’t even have time to grunt in pain as both his sword and his body were cut in half.
A split second later, Gu Nan's figure turned pitch-black, while the shadow doppelganger next to him turned into Gu Nan—this process was repeated many times until all six slashes were made by Gu Nan himself.
After the dazzling "six attacks with one slash", Gu Nan stood still again, but he didn't feel any mental strain from carrying out the attack.
‘Is it because my soul was also strengthened in this world, which in turn strengthened my mind? After all, it was just a virtual reality game in my past life, so the players’ minds were merely at the level of ordinary people.’
Gu Nan rubbed his chin thoughtfully as five bisected corpses slowly fell onto the ground in front of him.
Among the six Dao Lords, only the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord remained standing in his original spot. His face didn’t even show any surprise, as if everything was within his expectations.
Gu Nan didn't even look at the five corpses—precisely as Red Tail said, with the exception of the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord, the rest of the six great Dao Lords were worthless.
They had grown complacent after being immersed in a comfortable environment for too long. Except for Fu Yong, the rest of them weren’t even able to react to Gu Nan's strike.
Even Fu Yong was barely able to draw his sword, so he couldn't escape the fate of dying either.
This was also one of the reasons why agility-type Evil Gods pursued ultimate speed. No matter how strong someone was or how high their realm was, they might still be killed in a single blow as soon as they let down their guard.
Clap…Clap…Clap
The Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord clapped his hands lightly, the folding fan making a distinctive sound as it hit his hand.
"You’re able to slaughter Dao Lords as easily as butchering pigs at the tender age of 19. Looks like it won't be long before the Starry Ocean Pavilion sends you a star seal," he said thus to Gu Nan.
Gu Nan had heard of the Starry Ocean Pavilion’s star seal before.
As the largest public organization in the Central Region, not only did the Starry Ocean Pavilion control the Star Ranking, it also sent membership invitations to all Void Cutter cultivators in Star Realm.
And their invitation letter was precisely a star seal made of special materials.
Gu Nan was too lazy to continue this conversation. It was obvious that the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord paid him a visit because he wanted to send the five other Dao Lords to their deaths, and Gu Nan also didn't mind giving them the fatal blow.
"Let’s go." He patted Lan Si on the shoulder, and Lan Si, who looked like she’d just woken from a dream, hurriedly followed him.
"Wait…" A low voice rang out—it was Fu Jing, whose face was ashen.
She walked a few steps up to Gu Nan, her expression changing several times. Finally, she said through gritted teeth, "You killed Lin Tian and my father, so why didn’t you also kill m—"
Crimson light flashed. Gu Nan casually swung Blade of the Sanguine King, which he hadn’t put away yet, and sent Fu Jing’s head flying.
Naturally, Gu Nan didn’t mind respecting the wishes of NPCs begging to die.
……
Deep inside White Mist, Gu Nan stood quietly in the throne room, watching the scene below with great interest.
It had been three days since Lin Tian’s capture. Gu Nan had been making preparations as soon as he returned to White Mist and also learned how to create the mist mirrors.
As for how the five Dao Lords’ deaths caused an uproar on the continent or what the Heavenly Mystery Dao Lord’s true purpose was, Gu Nan didn’t want to care about any of that.
NPCs’ goals were never something players had to care about; they only needed to care about their own missions.
Lin Tian was still enveloped in shadows, and the nine golden dragons in his body could only crouch in a corner obediently, not daring to move in the face of Gu Nan’s law of shadows.
"This is the array used to sacrifice a child of destiny’s accumulated fate," Red Tail drew a very tedious array, then wiped her forehead and explained.
Things related to fate and destiny were indeed extremely complex. Not only was the array itself complicated, but it also required a large amount of supporting ingredients.
Fortunately, they were doing this inside White Mist. Otherwise, it would’ve been a hassle for Gu Nan to collect all the materials himself.
Perhaps Red Tail also wanted to take this opportunity to show Gu Nan the value of White Mist and herself. Otherwise, based on her understanding of Gu Nan, he might just abandon White Mist at any time.
And Red Tail actually guessed right. It was precisely the tedious process of making the mirrors and the difficulty of collecting and processing raw materials that made Gu Nan determined to completely control White Mist and operate it as his organization.
"Starting tomorrow, set up a shell organization on the mainland. This will be White Mist’s public front," Gu Nan said to Red Tail beside him. "Don't put too many of our own people in there. If necessary, this shell organization can be discarded like a disposable glove."
"Yes, my Lord." Red Tail looked at Lin Tian, who was lying quietly inside the array, and smiled.
Gu Nan then told Lan Si, "You will be the leader of the shell organization."
"Ah?! I… I've never done such a thing…" Lan Si suddenly couldn't even speak coherently. She didn't expect that there would be a task for her.
"You’ll be the one handling all such matters in the future." Gu Nan was all smiles as he patted her on the head.
As an apostle, she’d have to learn to be sanctimonious and dignified sooner or later, so she might as well get used to this earlier.

chapters.title: Chapter 160: Morningstar Plane
chapters.content:
Lin Tian's fate was extracted and successfully made into a new mirror. There weren’t too many accidents during this process.
Gu Nan, who obtained the new mirror, wasn’t in a hurry to translate it. Instead, he started preparing to reincarnate.
That’s right. After a long period of recuperation, Gu Nan was finally ready to reincarnate again.
Although Lan Si had been cultivating diligently, causing Gu Nan’s Evil Value to rise continuously until it reached 325, there was no limit to human greed.
He used to dream about continuously earning Evil Value while lying around all day, but now, he felt that this speed was too slow, so he was determined to go out and clear a dungeon mission.
Of course, in order to save enough points to buy the Tier 4 advancement, reincarnation was inevitable.
If there was no delay from dealing with Lin Tian, then Gu Nan should’ve already started the next reincarnation a few days ago, because he’d already found a rather suitable mission on the first mirror’s mission list.
The reincarnation array on the ground slowly shone, and Gu Nan stepped inside it. His body was stored in the void, while his soul was gradually drawn out and thrown into another world.
……
｢Integrating external mission｣
｢Mission objective: Kill the moon thrall’s child｣
｢Mission reward: Medium｣
The mission notification that hadn’t appeared for a long time slowly emerged from the Evil God Temple. The corners of Gu Nan’s mouth stretched into a small smile. This mission was practically tailor-made for him.
The Morningstar Plane where the mission was located was slightly smaller than Immortal Demon World, but its power level was much higher, and there were even Dao Lord-level figures here.
The scale of the plane meant that the reward wouldn’t be small, and assassination missions were also Gu Nan's favorite missions.
He wouldn’t have to waste too much time on clear-cut missions like killing people or seizing certain treasures. At least it would be much better than the previous Immortal Demon World.
If it was a large-scale mission such as the war between the righteous and demonic factions, it would inevitably take a lot of energy to complete.
This time, Morningstar Plane’s mission was very good, but the only bad thing was…
"O noble Heroic Spirit who slumbers in the river of time, please answer my call…"
After a series of long incantations, a blue door appeared in front of Gu Nan, which he stepped through.
The next moment, he appeared in a school classroom. At his feet was a magic circle with strange lines, and in front of him was a girl with a wooden expression.
According to Gu Nan's understanding of the Morningstar Plane, this girl was probably his host.
The Morningstar Plane was a very strange plane, and the reincarnation rules here differed from rules elsewhere. Reincarnators wouldn’t possess a host’s body upon entry. Instead, reincarnators would exist in the form of Heroic Spirits.
This seemed to be a natural defense mechanism the plane used to protect its natives so that not only would reincarnators not kill their hosts, they would also have to protect them.
Because once the host dies, the reincarnator’s Heroic Spirit form will dissipate, and the reincarnation will immediately terminate.
Not long after Gu Nan appeared, the magic circle at his feet began to shine, and the pillar of light next to him turned from red to blue, then finally turned white, searing the eyes with its harsh light.
"Oh dear! Lin Duo, you summoned a King Level Heroic Spirit!"
"Ahhh! It’s actually a King Level one? As expected of Miss Lin Duo. I’ll have to redouble my efforts as well!"
"Duoduo, since you and I have such a good relationship… Can I touch your Heroic Spirit?"
The meaning represented by the harsh white light made everyone in the classroom suddenly burst into exclamations, while the girl in front of Gu Nan was swarmed by several companions tugging on her arms.
As the person who summoned Gu Nan, Lin Duo herself never imagined that she would summon a King Level Heroic Spirit.
This was an honest-to-god Tier 3 bigshot!
This girl with a slightly round face and some freckles felt at a loss for a moment and didn't know what to do.
Gu Nan had learned the rules of this plane from White Mist’s archives long ago, so he expressionlessly proclaimed, "My name is Gu Nan."
As soon as Gu Nan’s voice fell, the students surrounding him suddenly burst into exclamations again.
"Wow! It’s actually a sentient Heroic Spirit. As expected of a King Level existence!"
"Yeah! It looks so handsome!"
"I also really want a Heroic Spirit like this…"
In fact, Gu Nan still kept his original appearance. No matter which angle you looked, his ordinary-looking face couldn’t be said to be handsome at all. But this plane’s style was simply like this. Everyone in this world had Eighth Grade Syndrome—Gu Nan had already heard about that.
Finally, a teacher-like person appeared next to him and clapped his hands to signal everyone to be quiet, then turned to Lin Duo. "Lin Duo, don't be nervous. Just do what we practiced in class."
Lin Duo, who received the teacher’s encouragement, gritted her teeth and said, "M-Mister Gu Nan, it’s nice to meet you…"
Gu Nan just nodded indifferently. He needed to play the role of a cold and aloof Heroic Spirit, which would make his future mission clearing more convenient.
The classroom began to quiet down. Everyone was watching Lin Duo and Gu Nan with curiosity in their eyes, even the teacher.
This was a King Level Heroic Spirit. Not even those Tier 2 powerhouses were guaranteed to summon one. Nobody expected a high school student to summon such a Heroic Spirit on her first try…
But the teacher wasn’t too surprised. The power level of a summoned Heroic Spirit was completely up to chance, so it wasn’t like similar events had never happened before.
Everyone's gaze made Lin Duo more nervous. She even started stuttering, "Mr. Gu Nan, m-my name is Lin Duo. I'm a student of the capital’s No.4 High School, and my hobby is…"
"I'm just a Heroic Spirit. I don't care about your hobbies," Gu Nan interrupted with a slight frown.
“Ah… I’m sorry!" Lin Duo's little face suddenly flushed red with embarrassment, and there were bursts of low laughter around her.
Gu Nan shook his head slightly and walked out of the circle. The outline of his body gradually turned solid, no longer resembling a pure white spirit, and the world even automatically put a formal suit on him.
‘It's truly a considerate law…’ Gu Nan couldn't help muttering.
The current Gu Nan had inherited a part of his original body’s strength, speed, and laws. He looked no different from human beings.
The term “Heroic Spirit” was local to this plane. Its essence was more like an individual directly created by laws. Like all elemental life forms, it was a creature created by laws.
This was different from Gu Nan's previous understanding of the term Heroic Spirit. Here, it didn’t mean the souls of dead people; instead, Heroic Spirits were a special existence between reality and fantasy.
When ordinary Heroic Spirits answered summonings, they often had a strong obsession and needed the summoner to help them fulfill their wishes.
Gu Nan's eyes swept across the classroom. Some people bowed their heads, while others looked at him curiously, but they were none of his business.
His eyes finally settled on Lin Duo, the girl who summoned him. At least for this period of time, he had to keep her alive.
"I will stay here for a year at most to obtain what I desire." Gu Nan said calmly, "But before that… You seem to have encountered some trouble."
T/N:
This is not the Fate universe
