chapters.title: Chapter 167: Heroic Spirit Temple
chapters.content:
An old man slowly opened his eyes in a quiet mountain hut on the outskirts of the northern city. His hair and beard were all white, yet he radiated health and vigor. There was a brilliance in his eyes that made people dare not meet his gaze.
This old man was Han Jun.
Those who could recognize him would be greatly surprised if they saw this. To think that the true ruler of the Heavenly King Corporation and a Tier 3 powerhouse would actually live in seclusion in a place like this.
With his status and position, it was entirely possible to enjoy all the glory and splendor in the world, but he was actually willing to live in this remote mountain cottage like an ascetic.
"Master." A faint figure floated into appearance behind Han Jun and whispered, "Han Yuntian and Han Feng… are dead."
Han Yuntian was Han Feng's father. He was the Boss Han who just died by Gu Nan’s sword, as well as this old man’s third child.
However, Han Jun’s expression remained indifferent when he heard the news, as if the ones who died weren’t his son and grandson.
"How did they die?" The old man asked calmly.
The blurry shadow behind Han Jun gradually became clear, and it turned out to be a humanoid with a wolf’s head. He didn’t speak and instead handed some documents to Han Jun.
Han Jun’s gaze quickly swept through the report, reading ten lines at once, but his brows wrinkled.
Han Yuntian was found dead inside his own house. No clues of the culprit could be found, but judging from the lingering energy on the corpse, it was most likely a Tier 3 existence…
"I've confirmed it myself. It may be the work of a Heroic Spirit," the werewolf saw Han Jun's expression and added.
"A Tier 3 Heroic Spirit?" The suspicion on Han Jun's face grew stronger—a Heroic Spirit of this level was even rarer than a Tier 3 human.
Even for King Level Heroic Spirits, it wasn’t easy to grow to Tier 3 without dying. On the other hand, it was comparatively easier for Heroic Spirit summoners to reach this level with the help of multiple Heroic Spirits.
"The culprit can kill people inside the city, so it’s definitely not a naturally formed Heroic Spirit… How could those two useless things provoke an expert of that level?" Han Jun said with an icy expression.
He had many children in his lifetime and even more grandchildren, so the death of one or two of them didn’t give him any distress.
But if his useless descendants got the family into big trouble that couldn’t be easily resolved, then not even death would be enough to make up for their stupidity.
‘A Heroic Spirit wouldn’t kill so purposefully. There must be someone behind this Heroic Spirit, giving the orders… If the Heroic Spirits under this mastermind’s control are already this strong, then how strong would the summoner have to be?’
Although there were also cases of particularly powerful Heroic Spirits with weak summoners, Han Jun didn’t want to take any risks.
"Investigate this matter," he coldly ordered the werewolf. "I'll pay a visit to the Heroic Spirit Temple. If a King Level Heroic Spirit really did appear in the world, then it won’t be able to hide from the Heroic Spirit Mirror."
……
"The moon thrall is a King Level Heroic Spirit. If a moon thrall really did appear in the world, then My Lord will know as soon as you look at the Heroic Spirit Mirror,” the bearded old man explained with a fawning smile as he floated beside Gu Nan.
There was a Heroic Spirit Mirror inside the Heroic Spirit Temple. Gu Nan hadn’t known this information before; the old man was the one who told him.
The Heroic Spirit Temple was a special kind of existence that was basically the Heroic Spirit association. Even the textbooks Lin Duo studied at school were mostly written by the Heroic Spirit Temple.
The Heroic Spirit Temple could be said to be the absolute authority on all Heroic Spirit-related matters and commanded a very high status on the continent.
The Heroic Spirit Mirror, on the other hand, was a special treasure. A rather hefty cost had to be paid for each usage, but its function was also quite remarkable—it could be used to detect the location of a designated Heroic Spirit.
The Heroic Spirit Mirror was originally a product of the warring years. In the Heroic Spirit Continent, it was the equivalent of “radar.” Now, it was mainly used to investigate Heroic Spirit-related crimes.
After understanding the mirror’s function, Gu Nan was also satisfied.
Despite having a limited range, the Heroic Spirit Mirror was indeed what he needed right now.
If he found the moon thrall’s location, then it wouldn’t be long before he found the moon thrall’s child as well.
Looking at the old man whose body was about to turn into an illusory shadow and whose soul was about to scatter, Gu Nan smiled. "In that case, I'll take you to the Heroic Spirit Temple… You can repair your body there, right?"
The old man was overjoyed and nodded repeatedly. He suggested this course of action for Gu Nan precisely because his current situation wasn’t optimistic, and only the Heroic Spirit Temple could save him.
……
It was lively as usual when Han Jun arrived at the Heroic Spirit Temple. This was the gathering place of Heroic Spirit summoners.
Heroic Spirits that would rarely ever be seen in daily life appeared in the temple one after another.
However, someone of Han Jun’s status naturally didn’t need to mingle with those people.
Not long after he reached the Heroic Spirit Temple, someone came out to welcome him.
"Elder Han, Temple Master Dongfang has been waiting for you for a long time," the person who greeted Han Jun said.
This world didn’t only have one Heroic Spirit Temple. The person in charge of each temple was called the Temple Master. The Temple Master here was called Dongfang Qi, an old friend of Han Jun’s.
Han Jun first paused slightly in surprise, then reacted and shook his head with a chuckle. He didn't ask anything and just followed the person inside, where he saw a gray-haired old man in the inner temple. It was precisely Dongfang Qi.
Dongfang Qi waved for the greeter to leave and immediately said to Han Jun, "I knew you’d pay the temple a visit as soon as I heard that something happened to your family!"
"Why? Did you confirm that it’s the work of a Heroic Spirit?" Han Jun didn't care about the death of one of his sons at all. Rather, he was much more concerned about the enemy’s identity.
Dongfang Qi's expression gradually became serious. "Yes, and it's a Heroic Spirit I've never seen before…"
There weren’t any clues from Han Feng's death, but Han Yuntian had died inside his own house. Naturally, people from the Heroic Spirit Temple assisted in the investigation.
While Gu Nan's lingering energy at the crime scene might just give the werewolf mere suspicion that a Heroic Spirit caused it, in the eyes of the expert investigators from the Heroic Spirit Temple, it was indisputable proof.
"Have you used the Heroic Spirit Mirror to investigate yet?" Han Jun couldn’t help but ask.
"Not yet." Dongfang Qi shook his head. "We’ll be able to track it using the Heroic Spirit Mirror when the temple investigators finish extracting the energy left behind at the crime scene."
Han Jun frowned a little, but he also knew that a brand-new Heroic Spirit could only be tracked like this, so he had to sit through it and wait.
The process didn't take long, but before they even turned on the Heroic Spirit Mirror, there was a noise outside.
"What happened?" Dongfang Qi frowned as he asked a worker outside.
The temple attendant who was stopped by Dongfang Qi quickly bowed and replied, "Answering the Temple Master, a person came here to heal an injured Heroic Spirit. It’s a rare guardian Heroic Spirit…"
Dongfang Qi was even more confused. "Isn't that normal? What's there to make a fuss about?"
While it was true that guardian Heroic Spirits were rare, this was the gathering place for all the rare and precious Heroic Spirits in the whole city, so it wasn’t surprising for bizarre Heroic Spirits to appear here.
The worker replied with a bitter smile, "That person is really… His Heroic Spirit is clearly dying, but he doesn't care about it at all. For someone like him to have a guardian Heroic Spirit is simply a waste of a precious treasure."
Hearing this, Dongfang Qi and Han Jun exchanged a glance and gently shook their heads at the same time.
There were all kinds of people in the world, and there were also many fellows who didn’t cherish their own Heroic Spirits, but such people were bound to be spurned by Heroic Spirits.
"Temple Master, the mirror is ready," another voice said behind the two men.
Faced with a more pressing matter, Dongfang Qi was too lazy to care about some guardian Heroic Spirit. He immediately ordered someone to activate the Heroic Spirit Mirror to track down the culprit’s whereabouts from the lingering energy on Han Yuntian’s corpse.
However, the result surprised him greatly. He looked like he’d seen a ghost.
"Dongfang, where is that Heroic Spirit?" Han Jun couldn't understand the symbols on the Heroic Spirit Mirror, so he could only ask Dongfang Qi.
Dongfang Qi was silent for a moment, and after a long time, he slowly spat out four words, "Right inside this temple…"

chapters.title: Chapter 168: Reputation
chapters.content:
Inside the Heroic Spirit Temple’s main hall, Gu Nan asked a staff member under the gaze of all the onlookers, "His injuries can be treated if I just put him in there?"
Gu Nan was naturally referring to the guardian of the Sun Moon Enchanted Box—the old man with the white beard.
Gu Nan was asking a girl with a ponytail. Although she was very dissatisfied with this fellow who didn't respect Heroic Spirits, she kept telling herself that she couldn't be rude in front of everyone.
But she still didn’t have a good attitude when facing Gu Nan. She replied stiffly, "That's right!"
There was a small man-made hot spring in front of Gu Nan that many Heroic Spirits were soaking in. It could cure Heroic Spirits’ injuries and restore their strength.
Gu Nan nodded, casually grabbed the old man by the collar, and threw him in—his action immediately drew a buzz.
"You’re really… too crude! How can you treat a Heroic Spirit like this?"
"A fellow like this with no respect for Heroic Spirits—even if he becomes a Heroic Spirit after he dies, no one will want him!"
"Too excessive…"
Gu Nan completely ignored this discussion, while the bearded old man didn't have time to respond to these sympathetic people. He was comfortably soaking in the Heroic Spirit Temple’s hot spring and quickly recovering from his injury.
Perhaps because the old man's injury was strange, or maybe because he was strong, the originally rainbow-colored spring water faded at a speed visible to the naked eye after he entered.
A short while later, the spring water had turned completely transparent, and all the other Heroic Spirits healing inside the hot spring could only stare at this with stunned eyes.
And the old man's figure also solidified again. He suddenly opened his eyes, a flash of divine light in his eyes. His entire aura also turned imposing.
"This one, Gu Zhaoyue, has returned once again!" Excited, the old man even reported his real name. He laughed and looked at Gu Nan, looking like his schemes had succeeded.
"Didn’t expect this, did you now? This one has been imprisoned by the Sun Moon Enchanted Box for thousands of years. I’ve been waiting for this day… Speaking of which, I really need to thank you, little friend!"
As Gu Zhaoyue spoke, he laughed at Gu Nan. At the same time, power exploded from his whole body, showing that he was actually at the Prodigious Realm, and his level within the realm was also quite high.
"If you didn’t destroy the moon box, this old man wouldn’t have had the chance to escape! Don't worry, since this one is now free, our previous… Huh?"
A black sword ran through his chest and continued into the spring water behind him, piercing him clean through.
Gu Nan stood in front of Gu Zhaoyue expressionlessly, holding a black sword in his hand, while Gu Zhaoyue was stupefied and speechless. He was rapidly losing strength along with his injury.
"Where is the Heroic Spirit Mirror?" Gu Nan turned to ask the female staff next to him.
The girl didn't immediately come to her senses because of the sudden changes. She subconsciously pointed behind her. "It’s there… Hey, wait! You haven't paid yet!"
‘No matter what the relationship is between this fellow and his Heroic Spirit, they used up an entire hot spring!’
Gu Nan stopped. He stared at the girl who spoke, then at the people around him, and muttered, "This is really troublesome…"
Before the girl understood what he meant, a sword of shadow had already pierced her heart.
……
Just as the sentence "Right inside this temple" fell, a loud noise came from outside.
"What happened? !” Dongfang Qi asked loudly. He couldn’t imagine that anyone would dare to make trouble inside the Heroic Spirit Temple.
‘Does that person want to make enemies of the entire continent’s Heroic Spirits?’
Han Jun's eyes narrowed slightly; he had a bad feeling in his heart.
Crash!
A corpse smashed the ground in front of them. It turned out to be the person whom Dongfang Qi was just speaking to. Unable to bear it any longer, Temple Master Dongfang rushed to the front hall to check the situation.
But the scene that greeted him left him flabbergasted.
The originally lively yet orderly Heroic Spirit Temple now had blood and bodies strewn everywhere, and countless figures were carrying out the slaughter in the hall.
There were indeed countless figures; each one was a black faceless shadow. They ran around crazily, killing every creature in sight.
In the middle of the hall stood a young man in a gray suit, with a bearded old man beside him.
"My Lord…" Gu Zhaoyue floated near Gu Nan, still smiling, as if everything minutes ago was just a dream.
He was a Heroic Spirit, so he didn’t have any so-called vital organs. Besides a bloody gash on his chest, he looked no different from before.
"Can you use the Heroic Spirit Mirror," Gu Nan asked flatly, so flat that it hardly sounded like a question.
Gu Zhaoyue, however, felt his heart freeze slightly and hurriedly replied, "Yes! Back in the holy war, this old man controlled the Heroic Spirit Mirror to assist the army…"
Gu Nan nodded wordlessly, and Gu Zhaoyue finally sighed in relief.
He figured out some of Gu Nan’s thoughts—this lord cared about neither loyalty nor betrayal; he only paid attention to who was useful and who was useless.
If you were useful, then you could stay no matter what you did, but if you were useless, then you’d never enter his eyes, no matter how loyal you were.
On the other side, Dongfang Qi roared furiously, "Who are you?! You dared to attack the Heroic Spirit Temple. Aren’t you afraid that… Wait, you’re that Heroic Spirit!”
Dongfang Qi was in the middle of his sentence when he came to a sudden realization. The result from the Heroic Spirit Mirror was still fresh in his mind. If Dongfang Qi still couldn't connect the dots, then the time he spent as a Temple Master would’ve been in vain.
Gu Nan coldly cast a glance at him, then looked around him.
Under the ravages of his shadow dopplegangers, there were no living humans left in the Heroic Spirit Temple. In the silence, only the strong scent of blood permeated the building.
Han Jun also appeared beside Dongfang Qi, staring at Gu Nan. "Sir, who on earth are you? Why attack my Han family?"
Neither of them received an answer, because what answered them was only a sword as quick as lightning.
The dark sword sliced through the air. Han Jun and Dongfang Qi were both stunned. At the same time, a huge shadow also appeared in front of them, blocking the way.
"Roar!"
This was a giant chimpanzee, which was Dongfang Qi’s main Heroic Spirit. Gu Nan's sword sank into its body but didn't cause too much damage.
Dongfang Qi wasn’t a summoner who cultivated his physical body. He had already broken out into a cold sweat and immediately shouted, "Black Star, kill him!"
The chimpanzee roared three times, and its huge palm slammed down.
However, no one expected Gu Nan to not make any move to dodge. He just raised his left hand casually. The chimpanzee’s palm strike was actually blocked by one hand.
Even the chimpanzee froze. It tried to pull its hand back, only to find that it couldn’t move…
It roared again. The next second, its roar turned into one of horror. Gu Nan lifted the chimpanzee's huge body with one hand and threw it directly into the hall behind him.
Boom!
The chimpanzee crashed into a pillar, actually smashing the pillar to pieces and causing dust to fly all over the place. Dongfang Qi was decapitated before he could even utter a sound, dying instantly.
At this critical juncture, Han Jun's head suddenly turned into a wolf's head, and his entire body jumped up into the sky. He broke through the ceiling and fled.
"It’s a type of Heroic Spirit that possesses the summoner," Gu Zhaoyue made a judgment and looked at Gu Nan flatteringly. "My Lord, do you want this old man to hunt that person down?"
Gu Nan waved his hand. "I have no grudge against him. Do I look like someone who randomly murders people?"
Even someone as shrewd and shameless as Gu Zhaoyue was choked up by this sentence. He hesitated for a long time before asking tentatively, "Then My Lord, you killed the people here because…?"
"She asked me for money." Gu Nan pointed to the ground at the female staff who had been cut into pieces.
"If you buy things from NPCs without paying, you’ll lose reputation. If people find out about this, no one will do business with me anymore," Gu Nan explained earnestly, "so I had to kill them all."

chapters.title: Chapter 169: Moon Thralls Trail
chapters.content:
The floor of the Heroic Spirit Temple was littered with corpses, and only Gu Nan and Gu Zhaoyue walked forward slowly. Gu Nan stepped in the pool of blood but didn’t create any splashes. This was because he’d wrapped shadows around himself—there was no deep meaning behind this; he simply didn’t want to get his shoes dirty.
This was still a habit from back when Gu Nan played the game. The Evil God game’s simulation was too realistic. Bloodstains wouldn’t automatically disappear, so players had to find their own ways to deal with it.
Players were such contradictory creatures. On one hand, they reaped lives like they reaped the harvest, while on the other hand, they detested slaughter and bloodshed—they didn’t simply pretend to go through the motions of disgust; they truly detested it.
Gu Nan walked out of the silence and came to a stop in front of the Heroic Spirit Mirror. Without another word, Gu Zhaoyue had already walked up to it and began to fiddle with it.
It wasn’t much trouble to activate the mirror, but it cost quite a lot of resources. Even during the war, the mirror still couldn’t be used frequently.
But Gu Nan didn’t care. In any case, the mirror wasn’t spending Gu Nan’s money, and he also didn’t care about money.
The Heroic Spirit Mirror quickly responded, and an image composed of countless lines gradually appeared in front of Gu Nan.
"My Lord, the moon thrall is indeed here!" Gu Zhaoyue exclaimed in surprise. He didn't expect for such a rare ancient Heroic Spirit like the moon thrall to actually appear in this world.
"Where is it?" Gu Nan didn’t show any excitement and calmly asked. His goal was the moon thrall’s child, not the moon thrall.
Gu Zhaoyue compared the mirror’s patterns with a map and gave Gu Nan an address, but the latter frowned slightly.
Because he recognized this address. It was Lin Duo's No.4 High School in the capital…
‘Why would the moon thrall appear in a high school?’
Just as Gu Nan's expression darkened slightly, Gu Zhaoyue's eyes widened as they stared at the Heroic Spirit Mirror. "My Lord… There isn’t just one moon thrall… There’s a lot of them…"
……
In the capital’s No.4 High School, Lin Duo was walking on the school’s field, holding hands with a boy and girl carved from jade.
The charm of the sun and moon spirits was too great. As a result, parading around the school while holding hands with these two porcelain dolls made a crowd of people surround Lin Duo, pestering her wherever she went.
Lin Duo's face was full of helplessness. She didn't expect this ending either, but these two little brats refused to stay at home no matter how she tried to convince them.
The sun spirit merely gave a pout and stared at Lin Duo with his big dark eyes, and Classmate Lin Duo immediately surrendered.
"Lin Duo! Who… Who are they?!” A shrill scream came from the rear. This was Tian Tian, Lin Duo's classmate and best friend. She was staring at Lin Duo's left and right sides, her eyes turning into hearts.
"They are my Heroic Spirits…" Lin Duo said weakly, having explained herself countless times.
"Ah? Isn't your Heroic Spirit that stiff-faced person?" Tian Tian was also in yesterday's classroom and naturally remembered the sensational King Level Heroic Spirit.
"Nonsense! Mr. Gu Nan isn’t… Hmph, mind your own business!" Lin Duo wanted to defend her Heroic Spirit, but she could only let it go after some thought.
Tian Tian laughed, and Lin Duo became angry from embarrassment. She simply took the two porcelain dolls and walked away briskly.
Today was the opening of the Heroic Spirit Tournament. Although the official tournament wouldn’t start until tomorrow, there was an opening ceremony and an exhibition match between two famous seniors today.
Tian Tian hurriedly ran up to apologize when she saw that Lin Duo was really annoyed, while the sun and moon spirits lagged behind them.
No one noticed that the two innocent-looking children were huddled together at this time, whispering about some appalling things.
"As expected, the Moon Thrall Calamity will originate from here,” although the sun spirit had a cool expression, his indifferent tone lowered the surrounding temperature slightly.
The moon spirit, who often played the role of an ignorant loli, looked similarly indifferent. "This calamity is inevitable… We just need to protect our contractor."
The sun spirit nodded in silence.
Seeing him like this, the moon spirit’s mouth raised slightly, and she recovered her usual charm. "When the time comes, I'll be in charge of killing enemies. I’ll leave our contractor to you, Little Brother."
The sun spirit didn't remain silent this time. He glared back without hesitation. "I am your older brother!"
……
In the principal’s office of No.4 High School, two uniformed police officers, a man and a woman, were standing in front of the principal.
"Principal Xue, we are members of the Special Incidents Team of the capital police department." The policewoman showed her ID to the principal and introduced herself, "My name is Jiang Xue, and this is my colleague Jiang Tian."
After checking the two’s IDs, Principal Xue didn’t doubt their identities but was a little confused. "Hello. Officers, what do you wish to investigate? Is there anything we need to cooperate with?"
Jiang Xue and Jiang Tian exchanged a glance, and Jiang Xue spoke up, "We want to secretly search all the research labs in the school."
"Research labs?" Principal Xue became more and more bewildered. It was impossible for high school laboratories like theirs to have any high-end research. How did they attract the police?
However, Jiang Xue answered with a deep voice, "Yes. We have received a report that some people are conducting highly dangerous Heroic Spirit research here."
……
In a research lab deep within No.4 High School, several staff members in white coats were running around quickly, transmitting experiment data to the center.
In the center of the laboratory was a middle-aged man with gold-rimmed glasses. His head was slightly raised as he quietly studied the pod in front of him.
The pod was filled with light blue culture fluid that surrounded an odd-looking humanoid creature.
This creature was roughly as tall as ordinary humans, but it had sharp claws on its hands and no hair on its head. Only a pair of pointed ears grew on its bald head.
And there were fifty such pods in this modest-sized laboratory.
"Professor Tian, the 50th moon thrall is also in an active state, ready to be awakened at any time," a staff member stood beside Tian Yuan and reported in a low voice.
Professor Tian Yuan gently lifted his glasses and nodded. "Then let’s start."
"Yes." The man clearly understood what he meant by "start” and immediately responded, turning around to give orders.
Tian Yuan's gaze never moved from the pod, quietly watching the moon thrall inside. An indescribable expression gradually appeared on his face.
Anticipation, longing, fanaticism…
With the operation of the laboratory staff, the 50 incubation pods lit up simultaneously. Under strong external stimulation, the moon thralls began to open their eyes one by one.
But before they could move, they were all pushed into a cramped secret room.
"It’s been fifteen years. This day has finally arrived." Tian Yuan looked at the moon thralls who had fallen into a heap, and a strange smile appeared on his face.
"A child of the moon thrall—is there really such a thing in this world?" Tian Yuan murmured to himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Infection
chapters.content:
Jiang Xue and Jiang Tian hurriedly passed through the northern section of the school, where most of the research labs were. They checked the rooms one by one but didn’t find anything suspicious yet.
"Sister, we can’t just keep on searching like this." Jiang Tian suggested with a frown, "Why don't we inform them and have the people in these labs come out by themselves?"
Jiang Tian had a baby face and looked like a newly graduated college student, but he was already a veteran police officer of several years.
He knew they were short on time for this assignment, and it was also inconvenient to send lots of officers into the school, so the police could only rely on the two of them to covertly investigate.
His older sister, Jiang Xue, joined the police force a year earlier than he did, so she had more experience. At this time, she shook her head. "No, we can't accidentally startle the target."
She knew more about the story behind this mission. "This incident isn’t simple. Once the target gets away, there may never be a chance to catch him again."
Jiang Tian couldn't help being curious. "Sister, what exactly is the mission this time? The captain didn't even tell me…"
Jiang Xue frowned slightly, but since the mission was right in front of their eyes, there was nothing to hide now. She immediately asked, "Have you ever heard of the Full Moon Cult?"
"That evil cult?!” Jiang Tian immediately exclaimed. He knew all too clearly about the Full Moon Cult’s fierce reputation.
Jiang Xue nodded darkly without another word. And once Jiang Tian learned that this mission was actually related to an evil cult with a fierce reputation, he immediately lost interest in asking more questions.
The two sped up their pace, but right then, a startling energy fluctuation originated from not far ahead.
……
In Tian Yuan's lab, 50 moon thralls were squeezed into a cramped space together, and a red mist was slowly released into that space.
Under the influence of the red fog, the moon thralls’ gazes turned ferocious and cruel, and the vicious nature in their hearts was thoroughly aroused.
With a loud growl, the moon thralls started fighting each other.
The space for their activities was too narrow, so most of the moon thralls were crowded together. Rather than fighting, crazily tearing into each other was a more apt description.
They used their teeth, claws, and all the weapons in their disposal to hurt and kill their own kind.
Tian Yuan watched all this dispassionately, and when only half of the moon thralls remained, he waved indifferently. "Start pouring the Heroic Spirit origin fluid."
The Heroic Spirit origin fluid was the same as the rainbow-colored spring water inside the Heroic Spirit Temple used to heal injured Heroic Spirits.
This kind of fluid had a superb recovery effect on Heroic Spirits and was very expensive. It was usually diluted, yet Tian Yuan had used ultra-high concentration fluid right now.
The rainbow-colored sticky fluid began to permeate the small room and soon covered the ground in the enclosed space.
The fighting among the moon thralls turned even more desperate. As soon as they received a wound on their bodies, it would quickly close up from the effects of the healing fluid. Just like this, they ripped into each other endlessly.
Fresh blood continuously flowed down, mixing with the Heroic Spirit origin fluid on the ground to form a sticky mixture that reeked of blood.
……
"Sister, hurry up! It’s just ahead!" Jiang Tian took the lead, practically flying through the experimental area, and soon came to a stop in front of Tian Yuan’s lab.
He had already used the power of a Heroic Spirit to reach an amazing speed. However, Jiang Xue's Heroic Spirit wasn’t a speed type, so she could only lag behind, gasping for breath as she tried to catch up.
But Jiang Xue didn’t have time to complain now. She caught up to her younger brother while panting. "Hurry! Smash the door open!"
Jiang Tian nodded heavily. He mobilized all the power of the Heroic Spirit possessing him and gave the lab door a heavy kick.
Boom!
"Ahhh! It hurts…"
A loud impact echoed throughout the research building. Three seconds later, Jiang Tian cried in pain as he held his foot, but the door didn’t budge.
Jiang Xue's face darkened. She pushed him aside and grunted angrily, "You’re so useless. Watch how your sister does it!"
Jiang Xue's Heroic Spirit was also the possession type, but her realm was obviously higher. When she used her full power, the illusory form of a grizzly bear even appeared behind her.
A bear’s roar seemed to travel through the air, and the young girl slammed her palm onto the door with all her power.
They heard an even more oppressive noise, but the door still refused to budge. Jiang Tian looked at it all in disbelief.
"This door really is strong," Jiang Xue said nonchalantly as she silently withdrew her hand, but Jiang Tian clearly saw that her right hand was trembling.
At that moment, two figures appeared in front of them—a young man in a gray suit and an old man with a long white beard.
The two police officers didn't know how they could appear out of thin air like that and immediately became alert. Jiang Xue frowned and asked, "You two are…"
However, the two newcomers ignored her. The old man continued explaining, "My Lord, this door is made through a secret technique and is connected to the entire laboratory. Destroying it through brute force will also destroy the lab.”
"Oh, I see…" Jiang Tian exclaimed from the side but immediately shut his mouth upon an angry glare from his sister.
It's just that both police officers felt their hearts sink. It was fine if the door was simply strong; there would always be a way to break it open. But if it was connected to the lab…
Wouldn’t destroying the whole lab give the people inside a chance to take advantage of the chaos to escape?
The young man’s expression remained unchanged. He said indifferently, "Let’s enter and take a look."
The two officers who heard him looked at him simultaneously with strange expressions.
‘Did this person not hear that old man just say that the door can’t be smashed open?’
But they saw the young man step sideways, walk past the door, and directly punch the wall right next to the door.
Boom!
A noise far louder than the previous sounds came, and the lab’s outer wall was directly blown away, leaving a huge hole…
By the time the two police officers came back to their senses, the two newcomers’ figures had already disappeared, and without thinking too much, the officers quickly got up and rushed into the lab.
What greeted them was the bloody scene taking place inside a small transparent room.
With a face full of excitement, the last surviving moon thrall was crazily sucking up the contents inside its kin’s skull, eating even the brain and rapidly swallowing the food.
After swallowing all of its kind, the skin of this moon thrall gradually reddened, and its body also showed a strange bloody color.
Jiang Tian, who had never seen such bloodshed before, almost threw up.
Jiang Xue's face twitched slightly, but she still choked back her disgust and shouted, "Tian Yuan! Stop the experiment immediately, or else we won’t be polite!"
Tian Yuan, who was standing in the middle of the lab, smiled faintly and shook his head. "Too late…"
Bang!
The transparent glass was directly smashed by the blood-colored moon thrall, and it jumped out and immediately pounced on the surrounding staff.
One of them couldn't dodge in time. The moon thrall bit his neck, and the researcher collapsed weakly.
"Professor Tian, what… what the hell is going on?" A researcher stood behind Tian Yuan, gaping at this scene, which was completely different from the results they expected.
"Moon thralls are a type of extremely pure Heroic Spirit. Their individual differences are so small that they can even devour each other for genetic evolution."
Tian Yuan was like a victorious general, calmly explaining his achievement, "The devouring order I gave them isn’t self-regeneration like you all believe, but instead, it’s…"
Tian Yuan dragged out his tone, his hollow eyes falling onto that researcher without a trace of emotion, "Infection."

chapters.title: Chapter 171: The Continents Sinner
chapters.content:
Tian Yuan's voice was calm and indifferent. The lab seemed to fall into a strange silence. The only sounds were Tian Yuan’s words echoing quietly and crisp chewing sounds as the moon thrall munched on a researcher.
After it tackled that staff member, it bit off his neck immediately, then ripped his scalp apart piece by piece and ate his entire brain.
Jiang Tian was walking over, covering his mouth and suppressing the discomfort in his stomach, when he saw this and finally threw up.
The even more bizarre thing was that after that researcher’s brain was completely eaten, his corpse actually stood up slowly.
Some blue liquid began to ooze out of the remaining half of his head, eventually forming a twisted new head—a moon thrall’s head.
"To think that a human will actually turn into a moon thrall once bitten…" Jiang Xue murmured incredulously. This completely overturned her understanding of the world.
On the Heroic Spirit Continent, it was common knowledge that humans were humans, and Heroic Spirits were Heroic Spirits. It was impossible for one to turn into the other. However, the present scene overturned this commonly-held belief.
"The moon thrall infected his soul and transformed him into a Heroic Spirit. His body is just a shell to hold the Heroic Spirit… What a genius idea!"
Gu Zhaoyue's voice also contained disbelief, but at the same time, it was also full of breathless amazement.
Tian Yuan gave Heroic Spirits the ability to infect humans. Like a virus, they would continuously spread throughout the world… If it succeeds, this enormous storm will sweep across the entire continent!
It will be a war between Heroic Spirits and humans!
This was a turning point for the progress of civilization on the entire continent!
When Gu Zhaoyue realized what all this meant, a string seemed to be plucked in his heart, and some ideas sprouted involuntarily like weeds.
No matter everyone’s thoughts, the moon thralls wouldn’t stop.
In a short time, the number of moon thralls had multiplied from one to two, then two to four… In the blink of an eye, they had already infected over half of the researchers into their kind.
"Professor Tian…" Tian Yuan's deputy stood behind him. He was just an ordinary researcher. Faced with such a bloody scene, his legs were weak and he couldn't walk.
But his mind was still clear, and his train of thought remained uninterrupted. "Professor Tian, what can you gain from any of this? If the moon thralls spread across the entire continent, it’s not like you won’t be affected…"
He stopped when a moon thrall jumped onto Tian Yuan’s back.
However, the moon thrall didn’t have any intention of biting down. After smelling Tian Yuan, it suddenly jumped from his shoulder and onto that deputy, then bit down with great force.
Everything happened so fast. Only until he felt the pain from his neck did the deputy’s pupils contract, fixing Tian Yuan with a death glare.
"You’re a… Heroic Spirit…"
Tian Yuan burst out laughing at this moment as his entire body began to burn with power, an indescribable wave originating from him. It was extremely similar to the moon thralls’ powers.
Affected by this wave, the moon thralls who were still scurrying around began to get down on one knee, paying respect to Tian Yuan.
Jiang Xue's face changed slightly and she blurted out, "The Full Moon Cult! No wonder the Full Moon Cult was always so elusive, and we couldn’t find any trace of it… It turns out that the members are all moon thralls!"
If all the members of the Full Moon Cult were moon thralls, then of course they wouldn’t be able to locate them using the tracking methods effective on human beings!
What made Jiang Xue pale even further was that if she guessed correctly, then it would mean that… this batch in front of them wasn’t even the first batch of moon thralls.
‘So there are currently countless such mutant monsters lurking all over the continent?!’
As if to confirm her guess, Tian Yuan slowly stepped down, a victorious smile on his face.
"I’ve been waiting for this day ever since I woke up from a deep slumber fifteen years ago." The smile on his face looked slightly deranged. "You two puny police officers really thought I didn't know you were here?"
Tian Yuan snorted coldly. "To tell you the truth, your chief superintendent had long been aware of my existence, but unless you can wipe out all of my children, no one will dare to kill me. Once I lose control over them… huh?"
Professor Tian felt a sudden pain in his chest while saying those bold words. A pitch-black longsword had already stabbed him through.
Gu Nan's expressionless face was placed in front of him, which made Tian Yuan’s jaw drop.
"You… You dare to kill me?" When he said this, his tone was the same as that of Gu Zhaoyue upon seeing the moon thralls.
"Aren't you afraid of plunging the world into chaos?!”
Tian Yuan had built up an enterprise through 15 years of painstaking efforts. It wasn’t like he had never been in a hopeless situation before, but ultimately, hia enemies didn't dare to push him into a corner for fear of all the moon thralls losing control and rampaging after his death. This was his greatest reliance.
But Gu Nan alone didn’t care. How many people would die in the Morningstar Plane had nothing to do with him.
Gu Nan knew that Tian Yuan, a Heroic Spirit, couldn’t be killed by a mere sword through the heart, so black light shone from the sword, and the power of shadows poured out crazily.
This extremely high-ranking law dealt fatal damage to Tian Yuan.
Tian Yuan roared in anger, trying to break free from Gu Nan's hand, but his own strength was too weak; he was almost instantly overwhelmed by the power of shadows.
Tian Yuan's sight began to darken, and his thoughts also became clogged up, but a soft inquiry traveled into his ear.
"Do you know about the moon thrall’s child?"
Tian Yuan’s mind didn’t process this at all. He subconsciously replied, "A living person who still manages to retain their sense of self after being infected by a moon thrall is the moon thrall’s child…"
"Many thanks," Gu Nan nodded and thanked him earnestly. Then the power of shadows erupted, completely destroying Tian Yuan’s vitality.
The instant Tian Yuan's life force completely disappeared, the lab seemed to quiet down for a second, then utter chaos broke out.
The crimson moon thrall seemed to have gone a little berserk, frantically rushing towards Gu Nan, while other moon thralls ran out desperately. In the blink of an eye, they were gone. The Jiang siblings couldn’t even stop them.
The moon thrall who pounced on Gu Nan was naturally sliced in half, but nobody could catch up to the ones that ran away.
Moments later, the lab was silent again, but Jiang Xue rushed to Gu Nan with a furious scowl and asked, "Do you know what you’ve done?!”
"There are at least 32 cities on the continent, all of which have the Full Moon Cult’s moon thralls lurking within them. Once they start rampaging, can you take this responsibility?"
Gu Nan didn't even look at her. He was busy rummaging through Tian Yuan's personal belongings.
Looting corpses was a good habit, and he actually found something valuable—Tian Yuan's research notes.
Beside him, Gu Zhaoyue gave a soft cough. "Officer, it’s clear that Tian Yuan had already completed his plan. Even if we didn’t kill him, he would still have given the order to attack."
"Then you could’ve arrested him. You guys are powerful enough to do that!" Jiang Xue growled at Gu Nan, "You… You two are the sinners of the entire continent!"
Gu Nan, who was squatting on the ground, stood up at this time, surprised by the anger of the female police officer.
The next moment, Gu Nan scratched his head in confusion, then absentmindedly sent a sword flying over.
The female police officer couldn’t even utter a sound before she was cut in half.

chapters.title: Chapter 172: So this was an apocalypse dungeon
chapters.content:
There was no shortage of blood in Tian Yuan's lab to begin with, so Jiang Xue's bisected corpse didn’t add any new color to this place.
"You… You…" Jiang Tian stared at Gu Nan in shock. Then his eyes turned red. "I'll kill you!"
So the sword flashed as it made another arc, and Officer Jiang Tian followed in his sister's footsteps.
Gu Nan, on the other hand, seemed like he’d just swatted two flies and said to Gu Zhaoyue beside him, "Let's go."
"My Lord, where are we going next?" Gu Zhaoyue floated closer to Gu Nan fawningly.
"It's time to set up a camp for survivors. The creation of the moon thrall’s child requires experiments on living people," Gu Nan said, then muttered to himself, "I didn’t expect this to be a zombie apocalypse dungeon."
"Oh, that's right, this continent needs to completely fall into chaos first."
……
The capital’s No.4 High School was already a mess at this time.
After the mutant moon thralls escaped from the lab, they were like a virus that entered the human body and received the most abundant nutrients, spreading wildly.
Every human they bit to death would become a new moon thrall and join in spreading the infection.
Fortunately, the moon thralls’ infection characteristic couldn’t affect Heroic Spirits, or else the unrest would be even more serious.
But considering that such unrest happened simultaneously in the continent’s 32 major cities, the severity of the incident was quite terrifying.
"Big Sister, let's go!" The moon spirit pulled on Lin Duo’s hand and urged urgently.
"Okay, okay… What the hell is that?" Lin Duo naturally had no objections to running away, especially since everyone else was doing the same, but she was quite curious about the scary monster behind her.
"That's a moon thrall," a somewhat cold voice answered. The sun spirit had just spoken.
Lin Duo looked at him in surprise. Her expression seemed to say, "So you weren’t mute after all," while the sun spirit just shook his head coolly.
The moon spirit interrupted their conversation, "We need to leave now before it’s too late.”
As if to confirm her words, a moon thrall suddenly lunged at them but was kicked aside by the moon spirit, crashing to the side.
Lin Duo swallowed and hurriedly agreed, "Yeah, let’s leave…"
……
Inside the imperial capital’s city hall, the president slammed his hand down on the table, roaring at the people below, "Just yesterday, an alarming incident occurred at a Heroic Spirit Temple, and today, over 30 cities—including the capital here—simultaneously reported riots… Can anyone tell me what the hell these monsters are?!”
The president’s anger was conveyed clearly to his subordinates, one of whom stood up and said, "Sir, according to expert analysis, those monsters should be a kind of ancient Heroic Spirit—the moon thrall."
"You think I’ve never seen a moon thrall before?" Veins jumped out on the president's forehead, and he asked with an icy expression, "Since when did moon thralls attack humans without provocation and even turn the bitten into moon thralls?"
Back in ancient times, the moon thrall was merely a normal type of Heroic Spirit. At most, they were rare creatures. They didn’t have the ability to turn infected humans into other moon thralls.
In fact, Tian Yuan was the one who endowed them with both an irrational aggression and the ability to infect humans.
In a sense, the moon thralls currently terrorizing the world could be considered a completely new type of Heroic Spirit.
The official who got up could only wipe away some sweat. The outbreak of moon thralls was too sudden; they really didn't have time to obtain more information.
Seeing the official’s speechless expression, the president could only say with a cold face, "Continue investigating the cause behind the monsters’ appearance, but the most important matter right now is to organize the people and have them take emergency refuge. At the same time, we must gather Heroic Spirit summoners to kill those monsters.”
As the ruler of a country, the president naturally wasn’t incompetent. He took the best course of action in this situation.
No matter why those monsters appeared, the government must not panic at this time. As long as they prevented the monsters from attacking ordinary citizens, the number of moon thralls wouldn’t increase any further, and they would all be eliminated sooner or later.
As the president's orders were issued one by one, his subordinates’ pens moved nonstop, writing down his instructions. The relevant policies were quickly decided upon.
"Alright…" The president let out a light sigh. "Everyone, act according to this temporary order. Let’s bring the situation under control first… Why are you all staring at me?"
Mid-sentence, the president saw everyone present stare at a spot behind him, looking like they’d seen a ghost.
Chills suddenly emerged in his heart. He subconsciously looked back, only to see an entirely dark figure standing behind him holding a longsword in its hand.
The president himself wasn’t a powerful fighter and was directly beheaded before he even had a chance to react.
The moment his head landed on the ground, he saw the overall situation at the meeting hall for the final time—a black shadow stood behind each of the twenty-plus people in this room, making the exact same decapitating motion with their swords.
‘Everything’s over…’ This was the president’s last thought.
The simultaneous beheading of all the top government officials was enough to throw the imperial government into complete chaos and render it defenseless against the oncoming crisis.
And after doing all this, Gu Nan leisurely dispelled all the shadow clones and left before the government’s powerhouses arrived on the scene.
……
Near the capital’s No.4 High School, Gu Nan and Gu Zhaoyue were standing on top of a tall building, overlooking the chaos and fighting below.
The sudden doomsday scenario exposed many people’s true natures.
Greed, tyranny, bloodthirst—the darkest sides of human nature were revealed in just a few hours.
Of course, all this had nothing to do with Gu Nan. It wasn’t any of his concern who had humanity and who didn’t. He just came to check on Lin Duo.
Gu Nan didn't want anything to happen to Lin Duo in such a chaotic situation. If his reincarnation was forcibly terminated because of her death, then he’d really suffer a loss.
On the other hand, he didn't want to reveal his presence either, so he only sent a shadow doppelganger to tail her in secret, while he himself watched everything from the top of the building.
Gu Zhaoyue looked into the distance, watching the chaos and confusion coming from the direction of the government buildings. He was vaguely aware of what Gu Nan had left to do just now.
"My Lord, the government…"
Gu Nan nodded. "Although moon thralls are highly contagious, they’re actually quite weak. The humans can’t be allowed to fight them in an organized manner.”
At best, the moon thralls were at peak Innate Realm. In terms of this world’s power level, they weren’t even considered Tier 2.
At this level, the moon thralls would be quickly encircled and killed once humanity’s strongest leaders finally reacted.
Gu Nan wanted to create a child of the moon thrall, so of course he couldn’t sit back and watch the moon thralls be wiped out.
So he killed off humanity’s top-level officials. As long as the government descended into chaos, it would give the moon thralls some time to mutate and strengthen themselves.
The scene of fifty ordinary moon thralls devouring each other to gather energy still remained in Gu Nan's mind.
Gu Zhaoyue was silent for a long time. He roughly understood what Gu Nan went to do, but he still couldn't figure out the goal behind those actions.
‘Don’t tell me that there really is such a thing as an antisocial personality in this world?’
But he absolutely didn't dare to ask more questions. A moody person like Gu Nan might just cut him down as soon as he opened his big mouth.
"The capital won't be in chaos for long. I’ll clean up the top military officials," Gu Nan said flatly. "Within half a month, I want to see a survivor camp with more than 2,000 people."
"Yes, My Lord." Gu Zhaoyue didn't even ask the reason and just bowed obediently.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: Apocalyptic Catastrophe
chapters.content:
The appearance of moon thralls plunged the world into great chaos.
Thanks to Professor Tian Yuan's efforts, moon thrall outbreaks appeared simultaneously in the imperial capital and the continent’s 32 other cities, catching people on the Heroic Spirit Continent by surprise.
The mutated moon thralls had characteristics that ordinary people couldn’t imagine.
They lacked all rationality and were ferocious, unafraid of death. They were Heroic Spirits and thus hard to destroy. They also had the ability to infect humans, and on top of that, this ability was constantly evolving…
In the blink of an eye, almost 20 days had passed since the start of the moon thrall outbreak.
Because of a certain someone’s outstanding contributions, the Heroic Spirit Continent’s government had hardly mustered any effective response when doomsday came.
By the time humanity’s top officials came back to their senses, the moon thralls had already destroyed the communication lines around the country, so each region could only fight its own battles.
Hidden in the very center of a man-made survivor camp in the middle of the capital was a research lab completely sealed off from the outside world.
All was silent around the lab, but if someone put their ear to the wall, they’d still be able to faintly discern the miserable shrieks from inside.
Those pained screams came from human beings. The screams emerged sporadically and sounded quite terrifying.
Gu Nan stood in the lab expressionlessly. A man was tied up in front of him. The man watched as a moon thrall was released and started nibbling on his head.
Throughout this process, the man was injected with psychotropic drugs to ensure that he stayed conscious the entire time.
After a series of blood-curdling screams, the man was turned into a moon thrall and beheaded by Gu Nan's sword shortly after.
"Still a failure… What exactly went wrong?" The headless body slowly fell down in front of Gu Nan, but he frowned and didn't seem relaxed at all.
According to Tian Yuan, the moon thrall’s child was a human who could still retain their rationality even after being infected, but what sounded so simple was actually extremely difficult to do.
In the beginning, moon thralls had to eat all of a human’s brain in order to infect the human’s soul.
But a mere half a month later, the moon thralls’ infectious powers had improved greatly, and they could turn humans with just an ordinary scratch.
"But even so, humans still die completely the instant they turn into a moon thrall…" Gu Nan rubbed his forehead, feeling some headache.
In just half a month, he had conducted at least hundreds of experiments, but not a single one succeeded.
Every time, the subjects would lose their consciousness before they were completely infected, and when they woke up next time, they would’ve already become mindless moon thralls.
Gu Nan couldn't even ask anyone about this situation—through the notes left by Tian Yuan, he was afraid that he was already the person who knew the mutant moon thralls the best in the world.
Compared with the normal moon thralls in ancient times, the biggest characteristic of mutant moon thralls was their infection ability and lack of reason.
These two were symptoms from the same source—according to Tian Yuan, it was precisely the moon thralls’ mutated infection ability that made them unable to think, turning into mindless monsters that could only fight.
Originally, in Tian Yuan's plan, he could leverage his own advantage as their kin to control the mindless mutant moon thralls.
He originally wanted to instigate a war between humans and Heroic Spirits in order to control the entire continent.
But who could’ve expected Professor Tian to die in Gu Nan’s hands before he could complete his plan? This triggered great turmoil throughout the continent.
In this sense, it was no exaggeration to say that Gu Nan single-handedly caused the apocalypse.
Not even Tian Yuan ever intended for the moon thralls to go berserk, because this wouldn’t benefit him at all.
Gu Nan was the only person who needed the apocalypse to happen so that even if his own experiments failed, with a large number of specimens outside, the moon thrall’s child would still appear sooner or later.
"Tian Yuan wanted an intelligent existence to awaken among the countless moon thralls and command them to counterattack mankind?" The corners of Gu Nan’s mouth lifted.
……
In the capital’s central area, Lin Duo slowly dragged her exhausted body into the camp.
This was her former high school, but now it was called the Star & Moon Camp, which was one of the largest survivor camps in the capital.
"Your Excellency Lin Duo, welcome back." The night guards around the camp hurriedly saluted after seeing Lin Duo.
Lin Duo nodded at them with a smile and entered the settlement, leaving a lot of buzz behind her.
"Hey, did you see that?! Lin Duo smiled at me!"
"Nonsense, she clearly smiled at me…"
Lin Duo’s steps didn’t slow upon hearing these conversations. A small smile involuntarily appeared, but she quickly stopped smiling.
Although it had only been half a month since the apocalypse started, the law of the jungle in which power meant everything had already permeated every corner of life.
Only the strong could get more food, resources, better living conditions, and respect from others.
Conversely, the weak may even be deprived of their own lives at the whims of the strong.
Lin Duo still didn’t have a deep understanding of such an environment yet, but she enjoyed the respect from others and was proud to fight in order to protect the weak.
But she was also very aware that the reason people treated her with such respect was all because of those two little fellows……
The twin sun and moon Heroic Spirits revealed power on par with Tier 3 Heroic Spirits in the fight against the moon thralls.
And since they were her contracted Heroic Spirits, these contributions were naturally counted as Lin Duo’s achievements.
"Big Sister, I'm back."
When she walked into her home inside the camp—the high school dormitory was converted into homes—Lin Duo shouted inside.
Her older sister, Lin Ke, poked her head out from the inside and saw Lin Duo’s slightly tired face. Lin Ke said with a chuckle, "Go and get ready. We have chicken soup tonight!"
"Wow!" Classmate Lin Duo, the famed expert, suddenly lost her dignified image and cried out in excitement.
The current world wasn’t like the time before the apocalypse. Meat, which seemed ordinary at that time, was extremely precious now. Even with Lin Duo's high status in the camp, she still hadn’t tasted meat for several days.
A moment later, Lin Ke came out with hot chicken soup and said, "I heard this was because our camp’s reconnaissance team found an uninfected chicken farm…"
"But the fact that we were rationed two whole chickens is all thanks to a bigshot like you!" Lin Ke put down the chicken soup and rubbed Lin Duo's head.
"No… It's all due to Little Ming and Little Yue," Lin Duo said with embarrassment while the figures of the sun and moon twin Heroic Spirits also emerged behind her.
After getting along for a long time, Lin Duo had given them names
[1]
—originally they were called Little Ri and Little Yue, but the former was so strange that it was changed to Little Ming.
"Little Ming, do you want to drink chicken soup?" While Lin Duo was feasting, she didn't forget her little friends.
The sun spirit rolled his eyes wordlessly. Beside him, the moon spirit laughed while covering her mouth. "Stupid Big Sister, we can’t taste anything…"
Heroic Spirits didn’t have taste buds.
Lin Duo's family spent their evening laughing at Lin Duo. During this time, Lin Ke casually mentioned, "By the way, Little Duo, your classmate Tian Tian came to look for you several times in the past two days…"
T/N:
[1]
Ming = bright/radiance; Yue = Moon; Ri = Sun
