chapters.title: Chapter 351: Little Zhong Dies Hobby
chapters.content:
Vampire Maiden Shana was a famous quest chain in his past life. It was a chance for players to take full control of the Raymond clan and even control the Capital of Blood as long as it was completed well.
In the game, almost every single large territory would have such and such clues to pique the player’s interest in slowly progressing through the quest chains.
If the game didn’t design these sorts of plot-relevant clues that contained plotlines, players would probably all choose to slaughter the city and be done with it.
And now, this design originally intended to increase the player's interest in the city worked in Gu Nan’s favor.
Among the missions available in the Capital of Blood, Shana’s quest chain was the easiest way for players to take control of the vampire clan, but it wasn’t very useful if one wanted to intervene in the overall situation of the Capital of Blood.
But Gu Nan's goal was none other than to control the Raymond clan; he wasn’t interested in the Capital of Blood to begin with.
As long as the player helped Shana through the following trials and let her embark on a training pilgrimage outside, then in just two months, she would become a Legend Rank powerhouse in one fell swoop.
By then, Classmate Shana would be returning with honor, but she’d still need the player’s help to truly control the Raymond clan.
After all, Legend Rank powerhouses couldn’t be considered invincible yet. There were over ten Legend Rank princes sitting within just one vampire clan.
‘After sending Shana off, I can go pick up that item…’ Gu Nan walked down the streets of the Capital of Blood, planning out the itinerary in his mind.
Returning to the World of Gods gave Gu Nan a feeling of having everything under control, because all the people and things here were recorded in his mind… Wait a minute.
Gu Nan suddenly realized something was wrong when he walked past a building and paused.
In front of him stood an antique pavilion made entirely of mahogany that was full of classic oriental beauty. The plaque even had the words "Qinghe Pavilion" on it.
Gu Nan wasn’t an immortal—he naturally couldn’t recall the name of the building that should originally have been here, but he was certain it wasn’t something like Qinghe Pavilion.
Or rather, there should be no such thing in the game. This architectural style was clearly the style of the Myriad Heavens Universe!
"Big Brother Gu Nan!" A pleasantly surprised shout came from ahead.
Gu Nan glanced up and saw Zhong Die standing outside Qinghe Pavilion, followed by Du Ke.
As Lu Xinhuan’s charge, Zhong Die also traveled all the way to the World of Gods with Gu Nan’s group, so they were considered acquaintances. Thus, Gu Nan nodded and asked, "Why are you guys here?"
"I came to see the Ceremony of Blood!" Zhong Die said excitedly. When she saw Gu Nan’s gaze fall on the building behind her, she explained, "You mean this? This is my family's business!"
Gu Nan suddenly understood when he heard that.
Qinghe Realm, Zhong Qinghe, Qinghe Pavilion… Zhong Qinghe, this first-generation Star Ruler of Qinghe Realm, had always liked to name his properties after himself. Not even his astral world was spared.
That meant Qinghe Pavilion was this Star Ruler’s business. His reach extended all the way to the World of Gods.
Gu Nan finally realized how this world was different from the world inside his past life’s game.
The existence of the Myriad Heavens Universe made an inherent difference. The two worlds weren’t completely isolated from each other. Skills, knowledge, and even power systems—there may be situations where information about them could be exchanged between the two worlds.
Especially in the case of a business-oriented astral world like Qinghe Realm, it was all too normal for its forces to spread across the World of Gods.
On the other hand, the fact that the two worlds knew about each other's existence would also affect the decisions made by their respective middle and upper echelons.
The gods frequently fought with each other in the game, but now that an outsider called the Myriad Heavens Universe existed, the internal fighting between the gods might not be as intense anymore.
All in all, the Myriad Heavens Universe was an oversized butterfly. Through the butterfly effect it brought about, it was entirely possible that the World of Gods became something completely different from the one Gu Nan was familiar with.
‘I can't trust the game’s history too much, but some knowledge won’t be affected.’ Gu Nan immediately made a judgment in his mind, adjusting his train of thought for this trip.
If he still based everything off of the game’s exact history, then his plans might go wrong at some point.
Zhong Die was still rambling incoherently to Gu Nan. Her train of thought was very jumpy; she could go from talking about disgusting zombie soldiers to delicious blood drinks all of a sudden.
That's right, delicious blood drinks.
It would be too naive to truly believe Zhong Die to be a sweet, innocent girl.
Bai Qiaozhen, who was also the daughter of a Star Ruler, already had the experience of ruling an entire realm. Even if Zhong Die wasn’t really interested in management, it was still impossible for her to be a naive, innocent girl.
But it wasn’t like she was the sort of person who hid her true nature and feelings behind layers of masks either. Rather, she was purely passionate about her hobbies—passionate to the point of obsession.
"Big Brother Gu Nan, let's go to the gladiator arena. I want to see them get killed!" Zhong Die tugged at Gu Nan's sleeve while saying some astonishing things.
Du Ke, who was listening from the side, sweated profusely. Originally, he was quite happy to act as a guide for the eldest miss at Lu Xinhuan’s behest. Of course he’d obtain a lot of benefits if he could be on good terms with the daughter of a Star Ruler.
But after truly coming into contact with this eldest miss, he realized the terrifying thing about Zhong Die.
"Do you like blood a lot?" Gu Nan couldn’t help asking while looking at Zhong Die, who was gulping down the Capital of Blood’s unique “blood drink” at an insane pace.
This blood drink really did use the fresh blood of various creatures as raw materials and was concocted by mixing them together. No other race besides vampires would like it.
Even after processing it so that the drink no longer had the pungent smell of blood and the taste was exactly the same as normal drinks, non-vampires still didn’t like it.
"Yeah!" When talking about this topic, Zhong Die inexplicably looked excited again. Of course, she’d been exuberant ever since she reached the Capital of Blood.
"I've liked blood ever since I was very young! But bleeding hurts so much… that’s why watching others bleed is the best!" Zhong Die said with an innocent smile on her face.
She said this with complete sincerity—she believed this from the bottom of her heart.
A blood fetishist who doesn’t want to bleed because of the pain, so she likes to watch others bleed instead—Gu Nan characterized her as such in his mind.
Setting aside the unique fetish of liking blood, Zhong Die was indeed a young girl quite inexperienced with the ways of the world. She wasn’t even too wary of strangers.
Since he also had to wait for the Ceremony of Blood to start and wait until Shana left to get that item, Gu Nan was strolling around idly for the time being. Thus, he didn’t mind going along with Zhong Die for now.
On the other hand, he was also eager to see what kind of changes would occur when visitors from the Myriad Heavens Universe entered the game’s original plotline.
And the Capital of Blood’s gladiator arena had just the right mission that could be triggered.
"Okay." So Gu Nan nodded.
Zhong Die grinned so wide that her eyes curved into crescents. Just because she was naive didn't mean she was ignorant of power—she was equally happy to get closer to a super powerful big brother like Gu Nan.
What's more, whether her trip to the World of Gods would end successfully depended on him.
Zhong Die's gaze shifted to Du Ke, who understood her meaning and hurriedly said, "When it comes to gladiator arenas—"
"Let's go to the Central Gladiator Arena," Gu Nan cut him off.

chapters.title: Chapter 352: Central Gladiator Arena
chapters.content:
From its name, the Central Gladiator Arena should be the centermost gladiator arena, but in reality, it was merely one of three large gladiator arenas in the Capital of Blood.
Due to poor management, the Central Gladiator Arena had already entered a state of decline. It was in constant danger of being surpassed by the two new arenas and might be tossed out of the ranks of the "Big Three" at any time.
However, it was precisely because of this that the Central Gladiator Arena began to prepare programs with lower and lower bottom lines in order to attract more customers, and the level of bloodshed here far exceeded that of its peers.
Over time, the Central Gladiator Arena really did create a new path.
Nowadays, not only were the onstage arena matches filled with all kinds of bloodshed and violence, but even the spectators came to blows.
But the arena’s officials deliberately ignored such fights and tacitly allowed this behavior. They even secretly influenced public opinion, describing their own gladiator arena as the "men's battlefield."
The three of them had just arrived at the arena entrance when a burly man crashed down onto the ground in front of them, blood gushing out from a big gash in his abdomen.
"Is it interesting?" Gu Nan’s expression didn’t even change. Instead, he turned and asked Zhong Die.
Zhong Die shook her head with a disgusted look. "I only like pretty big sisters, preferably virgins."
"Oh, then this hobby of yours is indeed a bit like the vampire race." Gu Nan nodded. Disdaining men and only preferring the blood of young virgins was one of the characteristics of vampires.
Gu Nan unhurriedly stepped over the burly man while several people rushed out from the arena’s entrance and pointed behind Gu Nan, shouting, "There! Cut him down!"
These men each carried an ax in their hands and had ferocious expressions on their faces. The ax blades still had obvious bloodstains on them.
Zhong Die and Du Ke, who’d fallen a step behind, were right next to the burly man at this time. Du Ke was so scared that his face paled, while little Zhong Die was watching with interest.
"Let's go," Gu Nan's calm voice rang out as he waved to the two, signaling for them to continue on their way.
"But…" Du Ke looked at the fierce ax wielders coming towards them, afraid that if he continued to move forward, they’d cut down him and Zhong Die as well.
However, what surprised him was that the group passed by him without even raising their heads and started hacking at the burly man on the ground.
When the burly man was mutilated to a bloody pulp and practically cut into mincemeat, these people finally jerked up and bowed in unison at Gu Nan and his companions. "Welcome to the Central Gladiator Arena!"
Du Ke was stunned, but Gu Nan went back and patted little Zhong Die's head. "This is a show unique to the Central Gladiator Arena. It’s performed dozens of times every day."
"Ah, so it's a show," Du Ke let out a relieved sigh and said with a smile.
Although he came to the Undead Kingdom over ten years ago, this was actually his first time visiting the Capital of Blood. He usually worked in Skeleton City.
"But it’s so realistic." Little Zhong Die studied the bloody mincemeat on the ground and even poked it twice with a tree branch.
"Of course it's realistic." Gu Nan burst into loud laughter. "Because this person was actually hacked to death!"
……
The realistic performance at the entrance to the Central Gladiator Arena probably scared poor Du Ke, who had a pale expression as he followed Zhong Die listlessly.
Little Zhong Die, however, seemed completely oblivious to this. She couldn’t care less about violence and bloodshed and held no empathy for the loss of life.
"What are you doing here in the Capital of Blood?"
"To join the Ceremony of Blood, of course."
"Oh, do you want to be bitten and turned into a vampire?"
"Yes!" Zhong Die grinned so wide that her eyes curved into crescents. "That way, I’ll have the perfect excuse to drink blood… I heard that sucking blood feels very comfortable to them, is it true?"
"It’s true." Gu Nan nodded very earnestly.
Little Zhong Die smiled even more joyfully and didn’t even ask Gu Nan how he knew. She just looked at the gladiator arena below with a smile.
A werewolf and a human were currently fighting to the death in the arena. Half of the werewolf's head was already split open, but he was still fighting to the end.
The human opponent, on the other hand, kept toying with him. Slash after slash, he left gashes all over the werewolf’s body.
While attacking his opponent, the human was even waving his other hand at the spectators—he was mainly putting on a gory show for the audience patrons.
"They're too ugly." However the blood-splattered scene didn’t seem to pique Zhong Die’s interest too much.
"There are vampire gladiators here too, as long as you can afford to pay," Gu Nan said with a smile.
Zhong Die's eyes suddenly lit up, and her head swung around with a
swish
to look at Du Ke pleadingly, while a troubled smile began to appear on the latter's face.
……
Outside the city gates of the Capital of Blood, a black-robed man slowly appeared and walked to a shady corner.
"The target is in the Central Gladiator Arena," the black-robed man's voice seemed to echo far away when it reached the corner.
A long time later, a response traveled out from the shadowy corner, "There’s a Legend Rank powerhouse in the Central Gladiator Arena. There’s a change in plans. We will switch to assassination."
"Yes." The black-robed man was silent for a while, then asked, "My Lord, dare I ask which faction the Legend Rank powerhouse is from?"
"An outsider."
……
Inside the Central Gladiator Arena, two graceful vampires, one male and one female, were standing on the arena. They gazed at each other with clear worry in their eyes.
"Hurry up and fight! Hurry up and fight!"
"You damned vampires, hurry up and fight!"
"Blood-sucking monsters, you guys really are slow!"
The two stood across from each other in the arena, yet neither attacked. This already caused the audience below the stage to shout with great dissatisfaction.
"That’s right! Fight now!" Little Zhong Die was also screaming with a frenzied look on her face, just like the most obsessive fan.
Only, no celebrity would be happy with a fan like her—this was a fan who wanted the celebrity’s life.
But the excited Zhong Die didn’t realize that a man and a woman were quickly walking over.
"Zhong Die, is this what you meant by liking vampires?" Lu Xinhuan's cold voice traveled over, while the person herself was already standing in front of Zhong Die.
Du Ke hurriedly stood up, looking like a great weight was lifted off his mind. "Miss Lu, you're finally here."
He wasn’t faking his emotions. During this tortuous time, he was almost driven crazy by Gu Nan and Zhong Die.
It was precisely because of this that he secretly contacted Lu Xinhuan, hoping she would come over and handle things here.
Zhong Die's voice came to an abrupt halt, as if a good girl had come out to visit a bar one day and was caught red-handed when she suddenly ran into her family.
She somewhat sheepishly put her hands behind her back and mumbled, "I just like to watch vampires fight is all… Big Brother Gu Nan, save me!"
As soon as she said that, she quickly ran behind Gu Nan and only peeked her head out, making a face at Lu Xinhuan.
Lu Xinhuan was absolutely furious. After connecting the dots with Zhong Die’s actions over the past few days, how could she still not realize she’d been tricked all along!
‘Romance novels, wanting to see handsome vampire boys and beautiful vampire girls… Yeah right!’
"Lord Gu Nan, please hand Miss Zhong over to us." Lu Xinhuan took a deep breath and tried to calm herself down.
Zhong Die looked up nervously, glancing at Gu Nan's profile. This was already the best chance she could think of to break away from Lu Xinhuan's control.
Gu Nan smiled as he patted little Zhong Die's head. "Nope."
He didn’t give any reason, nor did he offer any exchange or compensation. A no was a no.
The corners of Lu Xinhuan's mouth twitched slightly. She, who was fully aware of Gu Nan's power, didn’t know what to say for a while.
On the contrary, the middle-aged man who came along with her but never spoke until now revealed a smile.
"Miss Lu, do you require this humble one’s help?" The middle-aged man smiled and said, "I can have these two companions of yours temporarily leave the Central Gladiator Arena."
"On what grounds? Who are you!" Zhong Die instantly exploded. She was still waiting to watch the fight between the vampires below!
The middle-aged man looked at Zhong Die as his smile grew wider. "One of the three owners of this gladiator arena. My name is No—"
His expression suddenly froze as a hand of shadow gripped his neck and slammed him hard onto the arena.
"You'll be dead soon, Classmate Noken." Gu Nan said with a smile, "As a sacrifice to start off the quest."

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Origin Blood
chapters.content:
Night Elf Baron Noken, one of the three owners of the Central Gladiator Arena, had a notable reputation in the Capital of Blood, but in Gu Nan's eyes, he was just a key used to trigger the mission.
The quest chain at the Central Gladiator Arena was quite simple.
There were two forces that both wanted to kill this Noken. One of them chose to do it themselves, while the other side arranged for two vampire assassins to go undercover.
These two vampire assassins were the same two currently standing in the arena.
In fact, these two were a vampire couple, but they weren’t from the Capital of Blood, much less the Raymond clan, which was why they fell to such dire straits and were coerced to come here as gladiators in order to find an opportunity to assassinate their target.
Originally, in this mission, the player would get a clue like "the two rare vampire gladiators seem to be related to this matter,” then uncover the identity of the assassination target from the two vampires.
The next step was simple: send Noken to the vampire couple so that they could kill him before the other faction assassinated Noken.
The reward was a promise from the two vampires to do one thing for the player, as long as it was within their power.
This "within their power" really did mean anything within their power and weren’t just fanciful words protagonists threw out.
As long as they could do it, they wouldn’t hesitate at all. The player could even have the female vampire sleep with them, or they could order the two vampires to kill each other—they would still immediately attack each other.
Of course, the two would stop before the final blow because neither could bear to kill the other, and the promise would become void.
However, the correct use of this reward was to have the two vampires each contribute a part of their origin blood.
They were from a special clan. When their origin blood was mixed together, it could turn a normal vampire into an extraordinarily talented first-generation Vampire Ancestor, which was a benefit designed for vampire players.
And this was exactly what Gu Nan wanted.
Since Zhong Die intended to accept the siring and become a vampire, Gu Nan didn't mind helping her out again.
Of course, his help wasn’t without purpose. If Zhong Die could fill the role of a "player" and participate in the storyline events, then she’d have a higher chance of eventually taking control of the Raymond clan than Shana.
Ever since he discovered that forces from the Myriad Heavens Universe would also affect the World of Gods, Gu Nan no longer completely trusted his own memories and must prepare some more backup plans.
On the other hand, something very interesting will happen at the end to players taking the vampire route…
Endless thoughts swirled through Gu Nan's mind, while the present situation was in the midst of a sudden change.
Unfortunately for little Zhong Die, she wouldn’t be able to see two vampires fight to the death anymore, because the pair that was still distressed seconds ago suddenly saw a present fall from the sky as Noken appeared directly in front of them. How could they still hold back when the target was right before their eyes?
The two figures simultaneously pounced on Noken. Their hands turned into crimson light that directly shot into Noken’s chest with astonishing power.
All this happened so fast that Noken himself still had a stunned look on his face, as if he couldn't believe that he’d die like this.
In the audience seats below the arena, a black-robed man let out a low roar of anger and slapped the wall of the arena with his palm, almost slapping a hole in the wall.
He had come under the order of "change of plan, assassinate the target," but Noken had already died in front of him before the new plan could even be carried out!
His eyes shifted to the arena, glaring fixedly at Lu Xinhuan’s back.
"Qing! He! Pavilion!" The black-robed man hatefully repeated this name that had a somewhat odd pronunciation. They wouldn’t have needed to change their plans if not for the sudden appearance of this Legend Rank powerhouse.
With Noken dead, the two vampires didn't hesitate anymore and immediately spread open wings of blood, flying into the sky.
"Follow me," Gu Nan's voice sounded in Zhong Die's ears.
……
After night fell, two figures traversed through the forest. Their footsteps were a bit hurried, one might even say disorderly, but they also contained some inexplicable lightheartedness.
"We’re free, Natasha! We're free at last!" The man's voice echoed through the forest, startling a few birds in the curtain of night.
"Yes, we… are free." Natasha's voice was just a little more mellow, but all the same, the excitement in it couldn’t be hidden, "After we leave—"
"I'm very sorry, both of you," a voice came from the small wooden cabin in front of them, causing the two to look up in shock.
The two of them personally built this cabin when they first came to the Capital of Blood. Not even the people who coerced them knew about it, so how could someone be lurking here?
Gu Nan's figure slowly appeared, followed by the curious Zhong Die and the silent Lu Xinhuan.
"The two of you might not have gained your freedom yet." Gu Nan stared at them with a calm gaze and said indifferently, "I was the one who delivered Noken to you. According to your clan’s precepts, you guys must pay the corresponding price."
The vampire clans’ precepts were very strict rules imprinted in their bloodlines. The price for breaking it was unimaginable.
A skeptical player with a vampire character once tried… and then he deleted his account.
Natasha’s beautiful face had already lost all color, while the male vampire could only grit his teeth and say, "Don’t even think about using this to threaten us. Even if the clan precepts exist, we only need to—"
"Shut up, I want both of your origin blood," Gu Nan rudely interrupted.
The vampire couple’s faces stiffened slightly as they involuntarily exchanged a glance. The price of their origin blood wasn’t completely unacceptable. It was also extremely precious, but compared to their freedom…
"Alright." Natasha was the first to nod.
……
A few moments later, the two vampires had left, while Gu Nan had an additional bottle of pale golden liquid in his hand.
"Is this bottle of blood useful?" Zhong Die stared at the medicine bottle Gu Nan shook around and revealed a "simple and honest" smile. "Why don’t you let me drink it? I’m so thirsty…"
Gu Nan’s face had a mysterious smile. "If you can successfully accept the siring, I will give it to you as a present."
"Deal!" Zhong Die hurriedly agreed. The purpose of her trip was precisely to enter the Ceremony of Blood and receive the siring, so this was practically a gift with no strings attached!
"Absolutely not!" Lu Xinhuan, however, shouted from behind the two.
Gu Nan slowly turned his head and studied at her with an interested gaze, but he also had no intention of attacking.
His gaze caused a slight chill in Lu Xinhuan's heart, but she still insisted, "Zhong Die, you’re the daughter of a respected Star Ruler. How can you just turn into a vampire?!"
She originally thought Zhong Die was just curious and wanted to come here to see what vampires looked like and witness the Ceremony of Blood in passing… but who would’ve thought that her true goal was to turn herself into a vampire all along!
"What's wrong being a vampire?" Zhong Die argued.
Lu Xinhuan’s expression darkened. After a while, she finally replied, "Nonhuman races will not have humanity’s best interests at heart! Lord Gu Nan, you are also a human…"
"I’m not though?" Gu Nan’s expression said
don’t look at me, this has nothing to do with me
.

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Bringing Umbrellas
chapters.content:
Gu Nan's blunt reply made Lu Xinhuan freeze for a moment.
Only then did she recall rumors that the one in front of her was the reincarnation of a Heavenly Demon—could it be true?
But she quickly shook her head. Now wasn’t the time to wonder about Gu Nan's identity. Instead, she had to change Zhong Die’s mind— ‘A lowly foreign race like vampires…’
Outside the wooden cabin, Gu Nan just watched the two women argue without any intention of intervening or “mediating” by force.
He wanted to see if Zhong Die's will was firm and if she had enough willpower to complete his plan and forge a new path for him.
His arrangement for Zhong Die wasn’t related to the mission itself. It was a backup plan he prepared for the mission, and at the same time, it was also an experiment.
He wanted to test what would happen if an NPC who didn’t originally exist in the game filled the role of the player and continued on that path.
To do this, the three views of the NPC itself mustn’t be too close to normal. It was clearly impossible to find a real player, so someone so purehearted to the point of obsession like Zhong Die was already quite good.
……
Inside the sanctuary handling the Ceremony of Blood, a man whose skin was pale to the point of appearing sickly reassured someone with a faint smile, "You can rest assured, Miss Lu."
After a pause, the man gently took a sip of the red liquid in his cup. "Since you’ve already talked to us, the person you named will never pass the test."
"Then we leave it in your hands, Mr. Stanton." Lu Xinhuan likewise revealed a smile and sighed with relief. "As for our reward, rest assured that we won’t let you down."
Lu Xinhuan hadn't been in the World of Gods for long and wasn't quite used to the way of speaking here.
However, the results of her multiple inquiries showed that Stanton had a rather good reputation.
Although greedy, he wouldn’t break his promise after accepting the money. And for Qinghe Pavilion, any problem that could be settled with money wasn’t a problem at all.
The two had an amicable discussion, but the Ceremony of Blood had yet to start, so Lu Xinhuan didn’t stay for long and quickly left.
Du Ke was already waiting by the door. "Miss Lu, we can rest a bit easier now with Stanton pulling the strings from within."
Stanton was one of the preliminary examiners for this test. Although it was hard for him to guarantee with 100% certainty that a candidate would pass, it wasn’t hard for him to disqualify someone.
"It's still not enough." But Lu Xinhuan shook her head. "We need to have a backup plan."
……
In a flash, it was nearly half a month later, marking the start of the Ceremony of Blood. It was the day the Raymond clan openly recruited new descendants.
But today was also a special day for the Raymond clansmen who were already vampires, because today, some of them would be erased from the Raymond clan registry and lose the right to use the Raymond surname.
For a clan, the number of clansmen with that surname was always fixed. Every year, the number of people who joined the clan was equal to the number of people being kicked out.
Of course these new recruits also had the risk of being erased from the clan registry, and vampires who lost their surnames would suffer even worse fates. They would never be able to restore their identity again.
Vampires stripped of their surnames basically lost their “political authority” and could no longer hold any position within the clan, nor would they have access to any resources ever again.
Shana sat in front of a round table. Her long blonde hair was a bit disheveled and she looked haggard. She seemed very troubled.
Of course she was troubled, because she was on the list of clan members who were about to have their surnames erased today.
She was considered to have tarnished the glory of the clan and was found unworthy of being a vampire descendant because the fact that she secretly went out to act as a blood slave for money was discovered.
"What should I do?" These four words kept echoing in Shana's head. In fact, she still had a last resort, but she just didn’t want to consider it—leave the Capital of Blood and become a wandering rogue vampire.
Losing her dignity and status as a noble and becoming a wanderer—something that normally seemed unimaginable now had a chance of happening.
Compared to losing even her surname, there was at least a chance of turning things around if she became a wanderer.
"But you’ve gotta be able to escape this place first," Gu Nan's voice sounded directly in Shana's ears, as if he completely saw through her thoughts. His remark was cutting.
"It's you!" Shana stood up fiercely and dashed up to Gu Nan.
She would never forget that face of his. She wouldn't have been discovered by the clan if it wasn't for him, let alone end up in this situation!
"You still don’t understand?" Gu Nan smiled and explained, "Your dear brother has been watching you for a long time. As long as you receive a client even once, no matter what the result is, your secret will definitely be exposed."
Shana’s quest chain was triggered through "buying flowers." If the player didn’t try to buy flowers, then she wouldn’t be bought by anyone.
The reason was very simple. Besides players who had nothing better to do, absolutely nobody would ask a girl selling flowers on the street whether she had any high quality goods like “deathly crimson safflowers” in stock.
This was just as unreliable as someone asking you "Mister, want to play?" on the streets, and getting the answer "How much is Big Sis Chi Ling
[1]
?"
Shana's delicate face turned deathly pale. After a long silence, she finally asked, "How can you help me, and what price do I need to pay?"
Her train of thought was very clear. Perhaps there were people in this world who would help her for free, but the one in front of her was clearly not such a person.
"I can give you power." Gu Nan's expression remained tranquil. "In exchange, your life will belong to me."
A trace of helplessness and desperation flashed through Shana's dark green eyes, but in the end, she nodded.
A moment later, the extremely obscure law of shadows turned into a jet black dagger that sunk into Shana's chest, circling around her heart.
"Go on now, don't disappoint me." Gu Nan revealed a strange smile.
……
The Capital of Blood's much-anticipated Ceremony of Blood finally started, and on this day, vampires slowly walked out, one after another.
The men were handsome while the women were beautiful. Just from appearances alone, vampires were indeed one of the races blessed by heaven.
"Ladies and gentlemen." A male vampire stood on the high platform and said to the audience below, "In this year’s Ceremony of Blood, ten lucky people will have the honor of joining the noble Raymond clan…"
"Oh, apologies," he said after a pause.
"This humble one just received word that a despicable clan member has chosen to defect and fled. Before we kill her and take back her surname, the number of lucky people this time… will only be nine."
"Only nine, huh." Zhong Die stood beside Gu Nan and glanced around her.
Around a hundred people were lined by her side. Most of them were her competitors.
"Big Sis Lu will surely think of ways to stop me, right?" She looked up at the stage again.
"Of course," Gu Nan offhandedly replied. "But it doesn't matter. The only thing she can use is money. Sometimes, money isn’t all-powerful. By the way, did you bring the umbrella I asked you to bring?"
"I brought it." Zhong Die nodded honestly.
"Mm… There are a few other lucky fellows as well." Gu Nan glanced into the crowd of examinees, a few of whom also brought umbrellas.
Then Zhong Die saw him wave his hand, and a fine black rain began to fall from the sky.
……
The vampire on the stage was still speaking with assurance and composure, while Stanton was sitting inside the sanctuary, looking at the list in his hand.
He easily found Zhong Die’s name with little effort. After all, it had such an odd pronunciation.
A smile appeared on Stanton's face as he gently scratched a mark next to Zhong Die's name, then handed the list to the companion next to him.
"Please don't let this person pass the qualifying round."
"Piece of cake." Bernoulli, who was also an examiner, didn't even raise his head and casually agreed after casting a cursory glance at the name.
They’d done countless similar things every single year, so of course he wouldn’t refuse to give his companion face.
Stanton smiled faintly without saying anything else.
The examination to become a vampire descendant involved too many factors, so the examiners’ subjectiveness held great sway as a deciding factor. This also gave the examiners room to pull some strings if bribed.
Relatively speaking, preliminary examiners like Stanton and the others were still not too corrupt—the final selection at the end was the real lucrative job.
"They should’ve finished giving that stupid speech by now, right? How come no one has come in yet?" Stanton looked up with some dissatisfaction and raised his voice.
A servant soon hurried over and reported while sweating profusely, "My Lords, it's raining outside!"
"Raining?" Bernoulli looked up in confusion. "What does rain have to do with our examination?"
"I-It’s the Rain of Corrosion. We don't know why it rained. It's not supposed to appear at this time of year," the servant stammered.
"The living beings hit by the rain all turned into white bones… Of our examinees, only four survived."
Stanton's mind went blank with a boom. He subconsciously asked, "Why were those four able to survive?"
"Because… they brought umbrellas."

chapters.title: Chapter 355: Blood Diet
chapters.content:
Nobody expected the Rain of Corrosion to suddenly start falling in the sky above the Capital of Blood.
The Rain of Corrosion was a special natural phenomenon whose effects were completely aimed at living creatures. Creatures without flesh and blood like plants or dead things like walls wouldn’t be affected.
When living creatures came in contact with this rain, their souls would rot along with their flesh and blood, while undead creatures like skeleton soldiers were completely immune.
But it was extremely unfortunate that the people who would come to the Ceremony of Blood today hoping to become vampires naturally wouldn’t be undead!
The Rain of Corrosion wasn’t an unusual phenomenon in the Undead Kingdom. Many flying undead creatures could trigger this sort of disaster.
If one was unlucky, even a simple sneeze from a bone dragon that just happened to be flying over their head may trigger a Rain of Corrosion.
Of course, it was likely that even ordinary people would be able to withstand that degree of corrosion. The body’s self-regulation ability would be enough to resist the corrosion.
But today’s Rain of Corrosion even annihilated many powerful Tier 3 creatures as soon as a droplet touched them… This was clearly a spell cast by a Legend Rank powerhouse at full strength!
"Bring in the remaining four candidates," Bernoulli ordered with a dark expression as he stared at the mess outside.
The four "lucky ones," including Zhong Die, were quickly brought into the sanctuary hosting the Ceremony of Blood.
And this time, two more examiners—a man and a woman—had also joined Stanton and Bernoulli. They were none other than the examiners in charge of the final selection, but they also had ashen expressions.
Since this fiasco suddenly happened, their selection was no longer necessary. Now that less than nine candidates were left, of course all of them automatically advanced.
"All four of you have been selected. Come with me," Bernoulli sighed and spoke up.
Stanton's gaze fell on Zhong Die. Of course he recognized Zhong Die's face, but in the end, he didn’t say anything and allowed Bernoulli to lead her away.
……
"I don’t want the money anymore. I'll pretend I've never seen you guys before. Now hurry up and get lost!" Stanton glared at Lu Xinhuan resentfully and said fiercely.
Lu Xinhuan argued coldly, "Mr. Stanton, isn’t this quite immoral of you? You’ll have less than nine people no matter what you do, so it won’t be a big deal for you to insist on disqualifying Zhong Die!"
She wasn’t actually being unreasonable. Compared to the original plan of nine people, having only four or three remaining made no difference.
As long as Stanton insisted on it back then, Zhong Die could still be kicked out of the ranks of the inductees.
But the question was, why would Stanton do that?
"Are you crazy? That Rain of Corrosion was the work of a Legend Rank expert! Legend Rank, do you understand!?" Stanton's voice rose even higher.
A clear calculation went through his mind.
That rain was clearly the work of a mysterious expert attacking in secret. He’d still have justification if he kicked Zhong Die out before the rain, but if he mentioned kicking Zhong Die out right to her face, then wasn’t that the same as exposing his ulterior motives?
Once Zhong Die held a grudge against him and convinced the Legend Rank powerhouse behind her to kill him, the clan wouldn’t be able to protect him.
Of course, Stanton never could’ve imagined that Lu Xinhuan, who was standing in front of him right now, was also one of those Legend Rank experts he feared.
As for Lu Xinhuan, she didn’t know whether to laugh or cry. She didn’t expect this to be the deciding factor for Stanton.
Had she known this, she wouldn’t have concealed her own power.
In fact, she didn’t deliberately hide her power. It’s just that Qinghe Realm established itself in the Myriad Heavens Universe through business, so Lu Xinhuan had long gotten accustomed to using money to solve all problems. The thought of using her own power to oppress people never even crossed her mind.
According to the norms that people in Qinghe Realm believed in, strength was only used for self-defense. Only a win-win situation achieved through commerce would be considered a successful business transaction.
But it was too late to say this now. Zhong Die had already been taken inside the sanctuary hosting the Ceremony of Blood, and her name had been reported to the Raymond Clan, so Lu Xinhuan couldn’t even abduct her anymore.
In reality, Lu Xinhuan also prepared a backup plan in case Stanton couldn’t keep his end of the bargain.
But that backup plan was for the final stage of the selection. Who would’ve thought that Gu Nan would pull the carpet out from right under her feet, turning all of Lu Xinhuan’s preparations into a joke?
When Lu Xinhuan walked out of the sanctuary, her expression was even uglier than Stanton and the others earlier.
She would never allow Zhong Die to just willfully become a vampire.
Not to mention the fact that vampires completely belonged to the ranks of "monsters" in her mind, the mere fact that this kind of race was unique to the World of Gods was utterly unacceptable to her.
This was the daughter of the esteemed Star Ruler of Qinghe Realm!
She wouldn’t even allow Zhong Die to marry into any family here, let alone become a monster that only belonged here!
"Miss Lu." Du Ke stood beside Lu Xinhuan and whispered, "Our main base is in Skeleton City, which isn’t very far from here. Should we…?"
But Lu Xinhuan glared at him. "Don’t tell me you forgot what the rules of our Qinghe Realm are!"
Du Ke’s expression couldn’t help dimming. Of course he knew what rule Lu Xinhuan was referring to. It was a rule personally set by Star Ruler Zhong Qinghe.
When dealing with the outside world, the people from Qinghe Realm could choose to be honorable or sinister, but they mustn’t voluntarily use military force.
Zhong Qinghe's law was business, so he maintained that everything in the world could be solved with money.
If money couldn’t solve something, then it must be because they didn’t spend enough money yet, or the money wasn’t spent cleverly enough.
"After being chosen, it’ll take at least two more months for her to actually receive the siring. We still have a chance," Lu Xinhuan quickly calmed herself and said rationally.
She had already set aside all the matters in Skeleton City and her purpose in coming to the World of Gods. Right now, she was just determined to "rescue" Zhong Die.
"Since we can't stop her from joining the Raymond clan…" A sharp glint appeared in Lu Xinhuan's eyes. "Then we'll buy the Raymond clan!"
……
"Big Brother Gu Nan, I did it!" Zhong Die ran around the room excitedly, occasionally tugging on Gu Nan's sleeves or gulping down a large mouthful of blood drink.
Ever since she came to the Capital of Blood, her blood fetish had been getting worse and worse, and her daily intake of liquids was almost all blood.
"Two months of blood diet—this shouldn’t be a problem for you. Pick Christina for your sire," Gu Nan said as he looked at Zhong Die expressionlessly.
Becoming a noble vampire didn’t just mean finding a random vampire to bite her.
Although vampires were indeed this casual about the development of descendants in the ancient times, when it came to a clan with this much status, they more or less had to be a little more careful with their selection.
This caution was shown in the requirement that after becoming a vampire candidate, Zhong Die needed to go on a blood diet for over two months before she could accept the siring.
The so-called blood diet was to intake all of one’s daily nutrition needs through drinking blood.
At first, nutrients would be put in the blood, then slowly replaced with pure blood until the candidate's body had completely adapted to the blood diet. Only then would they be allowed to accept the siring.
This process varied from person to person, but it would normally take two to four months, which was how the blood diet ritual came to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 356: Knocking
chapters.content:
Blood diet didn’t just exist as a ritual. It did have practical value as well.
Allowing the vampire candidates to adapt to subsisting off of blood in advance not only helped the siring go smoothly, but it also allowed them to quickly adapt to their new physical abilities and habits after the siring.
It was better to get one’s body conditioned first than to rely on genetically-forced habit changes.
But on the other hand, it was a kind of torture for many people to accclimate themselves to a blood diet while they were still human and completely lacked any of the primal desire for blood within their bloodline.
But this couldn’t hinder Zhong Die at all, since this was why she wanted to become a vampire in the first place.
The other matter was regarding the choice of sires.
The sire was the one responsible for conducting the siring. Generally speaking, the relationship between the sire and the sired would be particularly close, just like a parent and child.
"Christina… Who’s that?" Of course Zhong Die heard Gu Nan, but this name that sounded a bit roundabout confused her a little.
"The strongest vampire below the princes, and her reputation is a little obscure. She will advance to Legend Rank in half a year at most," Gu Nan answered casually.
The Capital of Blood and the Raymond vampire clan were also distinguishing features of the Undead Kingdom, so Gu Nan knew a lot about them from his previous life.
Christina was a rather low-profile vampire within the clan. She lived in deep seclusion and practically didn’t participate in any activities hosted by the nobility. Instead, she dedicated herself to combat and cultivation.
If the player didn’t trigger Shana’s quest line, then Christina would be the most suitable puppet leader to use to control the Capital of Blood.
"I understand!" Zhong Die nodded forcefully.
……
Shana had been successfully sent away and Zhong Die had also settled down, so Gu Nan finally had time to pick up that item.
The remnants of a god was sealed inside the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead, but only special items could awaken him.
There were many items capable of this, but considering the difficulty of obtaining them, Gu Nan easily narrowed it down to one target—Cain's Left Hand.
"It’s not easy to get this hand. It has to be fed a large amount of blood…" Gu Nan recalled the method for acquiring Cain's Left Hand.
……
"Cain's Left Hand?" Lu Xinhuan, who was sitting in a temporary villa she just bought, frowned.
"Yes. Cain is the ancestor of the vampires. According to ancient legend, all of the modern vampires are his descendants," Du Ke was obviously more familiar with the Undead Kingdom and explained respectfully.
Lu Xinhuan fell silent. Her fingers drummed the desktop lightly, deep in thought.
Originally, she’d already made up her mind to "buy" the entire Raymond clan and then banish Zhong Die.
Lu Xinhuan wanted to use a very simple method. The Raymond clan was currently undergoing the newest round of elections for clan head. As long as she could put someone loyal to her in that position, then this trivial matter with Zhong Die wouldn’t be difficult to resolve.
Money represents an external resource. As long as this resource was used well, it could absolutely influence a group’s internal politics.
Originally, she was already trying to contact candidates, but things suddenly changed at this juncture.
The original election process was canceled—now, whoever could find "Cain’s Left Hand" would become the clan head!
"Where did they get this information from? How are they so certain?" Lu Xinhuan couldn’t figure out why the Raymond clan changed their attitude so drastically overnight.
No one doubted the truthfulness of this information?
"I heard… that the clue about their ancestor has actually been inside the Raymond sanctuary the whole time and was only discovered by chance a few days ago," Du Ke answered somewhat unnaturally.
A sense of foreboding surfaced in Lu Xinhuan's heart. "Who discovered it?"
"It was our Eldest Miss."
……
Recently, the entire Raymond Clan was in an uproar.
Only four descendants passed this year’s Ceremony of Blood. Originally, this would’ve been a very troubling matter, since it meant they would have to find a way to develop additional descendants from other sources.
But no one expected for one of these four descendants to actually bring them a huge pleasant surprise!
The seal containing information on their ancestor's inheritance was unintentionally opened by a little fellow who wasn't even a vampire yet!
"The Ancestor’s Staff must be retrieved. Whoever can retrieve it will be the next clan head!" This was the consensus that had been reached within the Raymond clan.
Of course the vampires wouldn’t call their ancestor by name, and among the vampires, Cain’s Left Hand had always been believed to be a staff.
But a day later, these vampires’ moods fell once again.
A round table meeting was underway inside the sanctuary of the Ceremony of Blood.
"Who the hell leaked it?!" The current matriarch, Lady Mara, asked with a frosty expression as she slammed her hand onto the table.
Six other vampire powerhouses were sitting around the round table. These seven people were the real top brass of the Raymond Clan. Every single one of them was a Legend Rank powerhouse.
"After the seal was opened, it was the seven of us who viewed it together. Even that little fellow named Zhong Die didn't get to see the content. Who else do you think could’ve leaked it?"
Lady Mara's furious roar echoed continuously throughout the room.
Of course she was angry—because the Ancestor's Staff, which should’ve been top secret, was known by the entire public the next day!
Right now, the entire Capital of Blood was afloat with rumors that the vampire race’s divine weapon would soon appear, and that whoever obtained this divine weapon would be able to quickly achieve Legend Rank and even have hopes of igniting their divine fire.
Only Mara and the others knew that the Ancestor’s Staff could only be considered a divine weapon in the hands of vampires. Outsiders wouldn’t be able to use it at all!
"Calm down, Lady Mara." A handsome middle-aged man spoke from next to her, "You should know that none of us here have a reason to do this."
Leaking information on the Ancestor’s Staff wouldn’t benefit anyone present.
The Ancestor’s Staff would bring benefits to the entire Raymond clan, which was why its ultimate owner would become the next clan head.
Mara gave him a cold glare, still furious. "This better be true!"
This lady clearly didn’t have enough trust in her clan.
"Alright, everyone." The middle-aged man spoke again, "This is not the time to put the blame on people. We must acquire the Ancestor’s Staff before everyone else."
……
Outside Qinghe Pavilion, Du Ke was instructing a few subordinates on work matters when a familiar figure appeared by the gates.
Du Ke looked at Gu Nan in shock and blurted out, "You… You still dare to show your face here?"
Gu Nan gave Du Ke a strange look, then glanced back at himself. "Why wouldn't I dare?"
The tone of his voice really made people feel conflicted. He was clearly the one who abducted Qinghe Realm's Eldest Miss, yet his expression seemed to ask, “Just what kind of grudge do we have?”
Du Ke was in precisely such a conflicted mood. He didn’t know how strong the person in front of him was, but since Gu Nan could throw Noken with his bare hands, he probably wasn’t too weak. Thus, Du Ke concluded that Gu Nan was probably a Void Cutter expert.
However, Du Ke naturally didn’t fear the other party, because he had the backing of the entire Qinghe Realm! ‘If not for that damned rule…’
A secretive glint flashed through Du Ke’s eyes. If the other party made the first move, then there was nothing in Qinghe Realm’s rules stopping him from retaliating in self-defense.
Du Ke asked cautiously, "What are you doing here?"
"Is Lu Xinhuan interested in Cain's Left Hand? I know where it is. I'm here to lead the way," Gu Nan said earnestly.
Du Ke stared blankly, unable to understand Gu Nan's attitude. ‘Could it be that this person realized he’d offended Qinghe Realm and came here to make up for it?’
But Du Ke himself had no intention of forgiving the other party. He was about to find a way to anger Gu Nan.
‘Anger him, so that he’ll make the first move and attack…’
With this thought in mind, Du Ke immediately sneered. "Is Miss Lu someone you can see just because you feel like it? If you want to see Miss Lu, you’ll have to go over there and knock on the door yourself."
Qinghe Pavilion’s gates were closed today due to Lu Xinhuan's preoccupation with the vampire matter, but there were still a few guards from Qinghe Pavilion standing at the entrance.
They instantly understood Du Ke’s intention, and ferocious smiles appeared on their faces.
But Du Ke's voice had just fallen when he saw Gu Nan give a nod, then grab Du Ke with one hand and casually throw him at the Qinghe Pavilion behind him.
Under the terrifying force, Du Ke's entire body turned into a black line and smashed right into Qinghe Pavilion’s gates. The impact collapsed the entire first floor of Qinghe Pavilion.
A white light lit up all the way to the sky. Lu Xinhuan's figure instantly appeared, rushing up to Gu Nan and shouting furiously, "Lord Gu Nan, do you want to start a war with my Qinghe Realm?"
Gu Nan cast a glance at her and shrugged. “I was just knocking on the door."

chapters.title: Chapter 357: Large Net
chapters.content:
Such a big commotion outside Qinghe Pavilion immediately attracted many people’s attention.
Even Gu Nan could sense the several auras that were immediately projected over, as if ready to attack at any time.
But of course Gu Nan didn’t take it to heart—what a joke. He was currently here in his true body. Perhaps if Zhong Qinghe personally came, then Gu Nan might give him some face and be on the alert, but these Tier 4 fellows couldn’t pose any threat to him.
Lu Xinhuan, who also sensed the movement behind her, coldly waved her hand, signaling for them to remain on standby.
She was fully aware of the terrifying thing about Gu Nan. This person had always acted without the slightest scruple, and they were currently in the World of Gods. If they started fighting, they probably wouldn’t even have time to send a rescue signal to Zhong Qinghe.
Lu Xinhuan forcibly restrained her anger and asked, "What did Your Excellency come here for?"
So Gu Nan had to repeat his reason for coming—in fact, he didn’t lie at the beginning. He’d indeed come here to lead the way for Lu Xinhuan and her group.
But since they expressed hostility, leading the way could also be changed to ordering them to go that way instead.
……
A few minutes later, Du Ke, who had a bloody nose, a swollen face, and even several broken ribs, said with a bitter expression, "Miss Lu, that Gu Nan…"
"Don’t even think about revenge. That person is not someone we can afford to provoke." Lu Xinhuan looked indifferent, as if she was talking about something that had nothing to do with her.
As one of Qinghe Realm’s representatives in the outside world, it wasn’t like Lu Xinhuan never compromised before. Sometimes, business was precisely the art of compromise.
Lu Xinhuan looked at Du Ke's still unwilling gaze and suddenly became fed up with him. She waved her hand and had people take him away.
In the end, she didn’t have a personal friendship with Du Ke outside of work. Whether he wanted to sulk or court death by attacking Gu Nan—none of that had anything to do with her.
The only matter Lu Xinhuan was truly concerned about right now was how to "rescue" Zhong Die—if she couldn’t change Zhong Die’s mind for the time being, then she at least had to get her back first.
Zhong Die had already entered the sanctuary hosting the Ceremony of Blood, so it was impossible for Qinghe Pavilion’s people to barge in and kidnap her. Presently, the best method was to help a vampire become the head of the Raymond clan, then have that clan head banish Zhong Die.
"It's a pity the vampire named Mara responds to neither coercion nor bribery, or else things wouldn't have to be so troublesome."
Lu Xinhuan naturally also had contact with Lady Mara, but with the vampire clan’s high status in the Capital of Blood, why would they take a tiny Commerce Association seriously?
In the World of Gods, almost any relatively large force had the protection of a god behind them, or else they wouldn’t be able to survive.
The Undead Kingdom was a main plane that had already been abandoned. It was practically impossible for this plane to provide gods with the power of faith, but this didn’t mean the forces here didn’t have backing.
According to the backstory in the game, the god backing the Raymond clan should be the God of Iron.
His divine authority wasn’t related to vampires in the slightest. On the contrary, it was even somewhat conflicting, but such a situation was all too normal in the Undead Kingdom.
So even if Lu Xinhuan threw out her principles and tried to threaten the Raymond clan with her background, it wouldn’t actually have any effect.
Lu Xinhuan had a splitting headache. She’d never come across such a bizarre situation in all her hundreds of years working for Qinghe Realm.
News had spread throughout the city that the ancestor’s seal in the sanctuary was "accidentally" opened by Zhong Die, and almost simultaneously, everyone learned about information inside the seal pertaining to Cain’s Left Hand.
Lu Xinhuan didn't even need to think about whose handiwork all this was.
But what she couldn't figure out was why Gu Nan actually paid a personal visit to Qinghe Pavilion today and sent her a detailed explanation of the information recorded in the seal.
One should know that the seal’s contents included hundreds of lines of fragmented sentences and esoteric passages, which contained a lot of useless information and misleading wording.
Everyone knew important information regarding the divine weapon was somewhere in this reccord, but it would take an absolutely astronomical amount of time and effort to pick out the correct answer amongst all the misleading information.
The information was so incomprehensible that many people simply threw these passages to the back of their minds and just kept an eye on the sanctuary. As soon as anyone in there made the slightest movement, a large group of people would immediately follow them.
Everyone believed that the Raymond clan, a clan of vampires, would definitely be able to solve the puzzle faster than anyone else.
But Lu Xinhuan was certain that not even the Raymond clan would be able to find the answer as fast as Gu Nan did!
"No matter what, let’s first verify the truthfulness of this information. Additionally…" Lu Xinhuan quickly made a decision, took one last glance at the information on the paper, then burned it to ashes.
And before the paper was completely burned to cinders, the words on it could still be vaguely made out: [Lightless Night, Four Seasons Mountain Valley, three vampire hearts]
At the same time, a gray mark disappeared in front of her, rushing towards the endless void.
After a long time, a mysterious reply fell into her hands. It only had a single word and a signature.
[Received.
—Sylvia]
……
What Lu Xinhuan didn’t know was that at the same time she received the method to open the seal, a similar message also reached the Raymond clan.
No one knew who sent the message. Right at midnight when the moon shone brightest, a parchment scroll of extremely low quality was placed on Lady Mara's desk.
That point in time was when vampires were at their most powerful and their senses were most heightened, yet the other party chose precisely this time to deliver the scroll…
"The other party's strength may be far beyond our imagination." The round table meeting that had just been held appeared again as Lady Mara's expression sank more and more.
The crumpled-looking parchment was just placed in the middle of the round table, surrounded by seven Legend Rank powerhouses, yet none of them reached out to take it.
They didn't even need to take it. The message on it was already visible because there were just a few lines.
[Lightless Night, Four Seasons Mountain Valley… Qinghe Pavilion]
"The time and place match. This person's analysis of the arcane passages is already on par with ours," Lady Mara couldn’t help speaking up when she saw everyone else being silent.
True to the public’s expectations, the Raymond Clan did indeed have a considerable advantage in analyzing the cryptic passages.
While others were still scratching their heads, the Raymond clan had already deciphered two of the three important pieces of information—time and place.
The only thing they still didn't have a clue on was how to awaken the Ancestor's Staff.
It wasn’t that there was no information. Rather, their ancestor actually gave too much information, enough for them to derive hundreds of possibilities from it. However, this matter just happened to be the talk of the town right now, so they couldn’t afford to take their time and slowly try every single possibility.
The group of vampire princes felt as if a large net was slowly closing in on them, blocking every single path they could take, and then… forcing them to take the only path left.
And that remaining path was none other than the one laid out here on this parchment.
"Even if it's a trap, we can only jump headfirst into it."
"It seems that this Qinghe Pavilion is the key."
The middle-aged man named Harrison asked expressionlessly, "Qinghe Pavilion? Does it mean to say this Commerce Association holds the final clue, or is it saying Qinghe Pavilion has what we need to awaken the Ancestor’s Staff?"
"Who knows?" A woman with long blonde hair sitting next to him knocked on the table and was the first to stand up. "Then everyone, let's start with this Qinghe Pavilion first."

chapters.title: Chapter 358: The Goddess of Shadows and the Heaven-God Alliance
chapters.content:
Gu Nan sat in a dark room, his fingers drumming lightly on the table with great regularity.
There was no light at all inside the room. Even the moonlight couldn’t shine in here—everything seemed to be shrouded in shadows, like the darkness from the world’s deepest abyss.
This certainly wasn’t Gu Nan releasing his powers to look cool; neither did he have nothing better to do. In reality, these shadows weren’t created by him at all.
"You don't seem to fear me…" A light, playful female voice rang out faintly in Gu Nan's ears and seemed to be transmitted directly into his mind.
Along with her voice, the shadows in his surroundings grew thicker and thicker, almost to the point of drowning Gu Nan.
But just when Gu Nan's entire body was about to be submerged, he suddenly stood up and took a single step into the shadows before him, his right hand grabbing at a spot in front of him.
"Wandering out for a stroll isn’t a good habit, Sylvia," Gu Nan's voice swam through the darkness, spreading throughout every corner of the shadows, but not a single sound could be heard from the outside.
Such a change came too suddenly, so much so that the “Sylvia” Gu Nan addressed was also caught off guard and was grabbed by his right hand.
The surrounding shadows quickly receded. Gu Nan's figure reappeared, and in his right hand, a girl in a black dress was being lifted like a chicken.
Gu Nan calmly stared at the other party. He truly didn’t expect this. He just wanted to scheme a little to ultimately acquire Cain Left’s Hand, but to think he accidentally baited out this… Mm, a big fish that wasn’t really a big fish.
Sylvia, the Goddess of Shadows.
That’s right—this was the Goddess of Shadows who shared the same source of power as Gu Nan and who wielded divine authority over the shadows.
Sylvia’s actual power wasn’t that strong. She most likely hadn’t even reached Tier 7 yet, so her divine power absolutely fit the description of a “weakling.”
But at the same time, she was also a big fish because she had a good older brother—the undisputed strongest in the entire World of Gods, the Ruler of Light and Justice.
Both siblings were gods, and it was precisely because of them that the saying “light and shadow are two sides of the same coin” began to circulate.
"Your power…" As soon as Gu Nan attacked, his own law was inevitably perceived by Sylvia, so she exclaimed with some pleasant surprise.
Sylvia wasn’t very panicked at all at having been caught by Gu Nan. She, whose divine authority was "shadows," couldn’t be killed this easily.
On the contrary, in the tens of thousands of years she’d been alive, this was the first time she met a god who also controlled shadows just like her—since he was able to catch her, he must naturally be a god too.
"Someone from the Light Faction actually dared to come to the Undead Kingdom. You have a lot of guts." Gu Nan smiled noncommittally and casually tossed her aside.
He didn’t care if Sylvia escaped. A mere Tier 6 god was only worth a few hundred Evil Value at most. Such a measly amount couldn’t even enter Gu Nan’s eyes.
And to offend the Ruler of Light and Justice over something like this, the losses far outweighed the gains.
What Gu Nan really cared about was why Sylvia would appear here—from his memories, this Goddess of Shadows shouldn’t have even the slightest connection to the Undead Kingdom.
Although it was an abandoned main plane, its natural characteristic of being littered with undead made this place more suitable for the development of gods belonging to the Darkness Faction.
"I’m just here for a commission." Sylvia didn't look scared at all and even transformed her shadows into a chair, calmly sitting down.
After a pause, she added with a playful grin, "Someone requested that I keep an eye on you!"
"Who?" Gu Nan already had a guess in his heart, but this wasn’t a guess he was happy to see, so his tone inevitably became harsh.
Sylvia obviously didn’t like this kind of interrogation. She pouted, and her eyes deliberately looked upwards, pretending not to hear Gu Nan's words.
The next instant, a shadow dagger had already stabbed into her stomach, and a large hand clutched on her neck, pressing her entire body to the ground.
"You’d better understand the situation you’re in." Gu Nan's grim voice rang out, his eyes coldly staring at her face. "Other people might fear Austin, I don’t."
Austin was the original name of the Ruler of Light and Justice, but because he was too exalted, there weren’t many gods who even knew his real name nowadays.
It is also because of this that Sylvia experienced an unimaginable shock when Gu Nan uttered this name with a cold expression.
Sharp pain continuously traveled over from her stomach, and the power of shadows that originally should’ve been of the same origin as hers kept surging out, wreaking havoc throughout her body and almost driving her own divine power to the side.
Shadows as far as the eye could see appeared again, but this time they came from Gu Nan, and the aura was completely different from before.
If Sylvia's shadows were mysterious and quiet, with a hint of the coldness of the night, then Gu Nan's shadows could only be described as "wanton and unbridled."
This was a shadow that disregarded all laws, devouring everything around it like a tyrant who slaughtered wantonly.
Sylvia simply couldn’t imagine that it was possible for the power of shadows to also be so overbearing and tyrannical. It was practically… practically the same as the all-oppressive light in her memories.
‘Light and shadow are two sides of the same coin, so this is what it means…’ Inexplicably, this thought emerged in Sylvia's mind.
But Gu Nan's words still reached her ears, so she hurriedly said, "I-I’ll talk… I’ll talk, okay!?"
Gu Nan made no motion to move, nor did the shadows around her have any intention of stopping, which scared Sylvia into hurriedly telling him everything she knew.
The reason she came here at someone’s “request” to keep an eye on Gu Nan was precisely because she received Lu Xinhuan’s letter asking for help.
Since Qinghe Realm was able to expand its business all the way to the World of Gods, of course it couldn’t just rely on smuggling to conduct business. Zhong Qinghe himself came here a long time ago as well.
Not only did he come, but he also joined a special organization. Sylvia was also a member of this organization, which was why she could receive Lu Xinhuan’s request for help.
According to Sylvia, all the members of this organization were either gods or Star Rulers from the Myriad Heavens Universe. Gu Nan even found many familiar names in the members list.
The Goddess of Dawn, the God of Blood, the God of Luxuriant Blossoms… and even a name that surprised Gu Nan—Zuo Zuo.
These gods had more or less all set foot in the Myriad Heavens Universe before, and Gu Nan finally knew why Zuo Zuo knew about the Tier leveling system.
"The Heaven-God Alliance?" Gu Nan repeated the name of this organization and confirmed that it never existed in his past life’s memory.
In other words, this was an organization that didn’t exist in the game, even though Gu Nan had killed many of the members in this organization in his previous life.
The idea that Gu Nan once considered but didn’t think too deeply about finally came true.
The gods and Star Rulers already had considerably close contact since long ago. They, who didn’t have any conflicts of interest, even formed an organization that spanned two worlds.
After all, reality wasn’t a novel, and two connected worlds didn’t necessarily have to go to war. Gods and Star Rulers also had their own interests and goals. They weren’t bosses just waiting for Gu Nan to raid them.
"How interesting." A slight smile appeared on Gu Nan’s face as he dragged Sylvia up and said, "I want to join the Heaven-God Alliance."
The wound in Sylvia's abdomen hadn’t even healed yet. She covered her stomach and said unhappily, "Is this something you can join if you just feel like it?"
Gu Nan glanced at her wound. "You guys will either have one more member or one less member today—your choice."

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Gods and Star Rulers
chapters.content:
The “Heaven-God Alliance,” an organization composed entirely of Star Rulers and gods, was probably named by a Star Ruler.
Based on the conventions of the Myriad Heavens Universe, perhaps the phrase "Heaven-God" represented the Myriad Heavens Universe and the World of Gods respectively.
But in any case, this proved the two sides were already in contact a long time ago.
It was just as well that Gu Nan's plans in the Capital of Blood were wrapping up. All that’s left was to wait for the vampires to start fighting Qinghe Pavilion, thereby awakening Cain's Left Hand.
Now that the matter reached this stage, the rest didn’t actually have much to do with Gu Nan anymore. He could simply watch the show unfold.
Unsealing Cain's Left Hand was a relatively complex multistep process rather than simply having to kill a set number of people. If the latter was true, then Gu Nan wouldn’t have to go through so much trouble and could just capture and kill a group of people.
To awaken Cain's Left Hand, first, at least three vampires needed to kill their opponents and unlock the first seal using the blood of their enemies. Only then would the hearts of three high-level vampires be needed to unlock the second seal.
And the final seal on Cain's Left Hand could only be undone by a mortal. At best, players could only be the oriole behind the mantis.
The reason the mission was designed to be so cumbersome was to make the game experience more interesting and fun.
In fact, the main plane called the Undead Kingdom was no longer a beginner’s village map. Any player who came here would be around Tier 5 or even higher.
So in order to prevent players from directly crushing all missions with brute force, any item with actual value was designed to be more cumbersome to acquire, which stopped players from simply getting drops after killing bosses.
Originally, when he had nothing better to do, Gu Nan didn’t mind staying behind to control the whole situation in case something unexpected happened.
But he had something more interesting now—the mysterious Heaven-God Alliance already attracted Gu Nan's full attention.
As for the vampire race’s divine weapon, Zhong Die, Shana, or the Wu Gui and Zi Dian still waiting in Skeleton City, Gu Nan tossed them all to the back of his mind.
……
The Elemental Plane.
Gu Nan and Sylvia found themselves surrounded by a lightning storm in all directions as soon as they arrived. This was the natural scenery of the Elemental Plane.
This naturally-formed elemental storm was enough to make it hard for Legend Rank powerhouses to take even a single step. Only elemental creatures could walk on the ground as if it was flat.
Of course, with Gu Nan and Sylvia’s power, they could ignore this insignificant elemental storm.
The World of Gods and the Myriad Heavens Universe still had some important differences.
The most typical difference was that none of the main planes in the World of Gods belonged to a particular god. Instead, they were collectively owned by the two major godly factions—the Light Faction and Dark Faction—and there were even neutral main planes like the Undead Kingdom.
This wasn’t like the Myriad Heavens Universe, where all the major planes were the astral worlds of powerhouses. Perhaps neutral planes might exist, but that was only because… they were so small that no Star Ruler wanted them.
The Elemental Plane Gu Nan was on was a typical neutral plane.
The environment here was essentially unsuitable for tangible lifeforms. Only elemental creatures could flourish here, so even gods had no interest in this place.
Sylvia brought Gu Nan here to meet the other members of the Heaven-God Alliance.
Without making them wait too long, an inexplicable aura descended. Sylvia's eyes lit up, but Gu Nan was the first to speak: "Rolensia."
Rolensia, the God of Luxuriant Blossoms, was a powerful Tier 10 god who was only one step away from becoming a greater god.
The appearance of a piece of water attribute Godhead in the Myriad Heavens Universe a while back, followed by the inexplicable appearance of Lan Si and her brother, puzzled Gu Nan for a long time.
How did they get to the Myriad Heavens Universe, and why did they know the Godhead’s whereabouts?
In hindsight, it was probably because Rolensia joined the Heaven-God Alliance and might even have forces that silently infiltrated the Myriad Heavens Universe.
The Myriad Heavens Universe, which naturally had countless planes, was more suitable for infiltration than this side. The gods could just find a random plane to hide their forces in, and in all likelihood, not even the Star Rulers of the Thirteen Heavens would be able to detect them.
A woman wearing a black and white nun robe slowly walked out of the endless storm with a cold expression.
Thunder and lightning crisscrossed all around her, but the elemental storm couldn’t even inch forth at all. And although it was clearly an elemental plane where only the elements could exist, flowers started blooming freely around the woman.
This was the terrifying might of Tier 10 gods, who didn’t even need to use their divine power, but whose presence alone was enough to affect the laws of reality.
"New member?" Rolensia's gaze shifted to Gu Nan, carefully studied him for a while, and frowned. "An astonishingly powerful divine body."
Gu Nan explained with a smile, "I'm from that side."
He didn’t explicitly say what "that side" was, but Rolensia clearly understood and gave a nod.
Gods only differed from each other in their respective divine authorities. There was no such thing as a different path of cultivation, so gods with particularly strong divine bodies didn’t really exist.
Even the deceased God of Strength could only tank two more divine attacks than the average god. He’d still be useless once he lost his divine power.
But the Myriad Heavens Universe was different; there were cultivators who walked the body refining path. In fact, the Rendering Mountain Venerable that Gu Nan previously met could be considered half a body tempering cultivator.
Rolensia then greeted Sylvia and fell silent, having no intention of striking further conversation with the two.
The God of Luxuriant Blossoms had always been this reticent. Gu Nan expected it already, so he didn’t mind.
Not long after Rolensia's arrival, two more people quickly descended. One of them was Cliff, the Sky God, while the other was a Star Ruler.
This Star Ruler revealed a smile as soon as he saw Gu Nan. "I was wondering which one from that side would be able to stop Sylvia from escaping. So it was Your Excellency Gu Nan.”
The person who spoke looked like an immortal, but he was an old man dressed as a Daoist. His long white beard reached his chest.
"This humble one, Clear Profundity Realm’s Daoist Lingyang, greets Daoist Friend." The old Daoist smiled lightly and bowed his head, looking amiable and approachable.
Gu Nan also returned his greetings unhurriedly, but in his mind, he knew very well that this Daoist Lingyang was by no means as good-natured as he seemed.
Clear Profundity Realm was a relatively rare type of astral world in the Myriad Heavens Universe, because the position of its Star Ruler was determined by a sect’s inheritance.
Clear Profundity Realm contained the Clear Profundity Sect, and its sect master would also be the Star Ruler of Clear Profundity Realm.
The fact that this Daoist Lingyang could ultimately win the sect master position from among his fellow sect members of several dozen generations meant he couldn’t possibly be a simple figure.
"Let’s begin now that everyone is here," Rolensia's calm and tranquil voice interrupted the two's courtesies.
According to the Heaven-God Alliance’s internal procedures, the admission of a new member required the recommendation of at least one official member and the completion of one of the organization’s commissions with three other members as witness.
This rule was set during the Heaven-God Alliance’s founding in order to emphasize the purpose of the Heaven-God Alliance, which was to help each other and benefit from each other’s strengths.
Gu Nan already knew about this. He thought about it and suggested, "Sylvia's commission hasn’t been completed yet. Does it count if I help her complete the commission?"

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Cains Left Hand
chapters.content:
Rolensia and the other two didn’t have much of a reaction when Gu Nan brought this up. Cliff, the Sky God, even gave it some serious thought. "It’s possible as long as Sylvia doesn’t mind."
The three of them merely received a message from Sylvia and came to act as witnesses for the new member. They didn’t actually know what had transpired earlier.
Only Sylvia stared at Gu Nan blankly, seemingly stunned by his shamelessness.
Daoist Lingyang on the side noticed her expression and asked curiously, "What was your previous commission?"
Sylvia rolled her eyes as she pointed at Gu Nan. "To keep an eye on him."
"Haha… Technically, it’s possible…” The old Daoist said with a forced smile as his expression turned a bit awkward.
"It’s fine." Cliff still looked deadpan; his expression didn’t even change. This God of the Sky was also considered one of the powerful gods. It’s just that his personality really was strange. Rumor has it that nobody had ever seen him make a different expression before.
The God of Luxuriant Blossoms didn’t even say anything and just silently watched Gu Nan.
In the first place, the three of them had never taken the commission seriously. It was unlikely for any normal god to be stumped by a mere commission.
After all, conflicts between gods were in the minority. The majority of commissions came from requests by people below the gods—such as when Sylvia received Lu Xinhuan's request for help.
If she hadn’t run into an anomaly like Gu Nan, a normal Legend Rank expert probably would’ve been captured by her shadows and would only be released once the matter was over.
To put it bluntly, the so-called commission process was simply a chance for the official members to properly observe the new member and determine his origin and strength.
Gu Nan was quite a famous junior in the Myriad Heavens Universe, so there wasn’t much need for a background check.
So Gu Nan shrugged and asked, "So does this count as me joining?"
Rolensia nodded. "Yes. Sylvia will tell you about some of the rules. When you return to that side, don’t forget to visit…"
"Lord Xue Ren of Extreme Sword Heaven," Daoist Lingyang supplied with a smile from the side.
"Right," Rolensia followed up, clearly not too familiar with the division of planes within the Myriad Heavens Universe. After she said this, she had no intention of lingering and left in a hurry.
Gu Nan also knew about Extreme Sword Heaven. Star Ruler Xue Ren rose abruptly in the last tens of thousands of years. He wasn’t considered a veteran Star Ruler, but his strength was not to be underestimated.
Xue Ren was called "Sword Saint"—and this was the address among Star Rulers, so the weight of that spoke for itself.
