Many in the Myriad Heavens Universe believed that if the Thirteen Heavens eventually became the Fourteen Heavens, then that newest Heaven must be Xue Ren.
With Xue Ren's status, Gu Nan figured he was probably one of the people in charge of the Heaven-God Alliance on the Myriad Heavens Universe’s side.
After Rolensia left, Cliff didn’t stay for long either and said to Gu Nan with a stiff expression, "Welcome, newcomer. If you have the chance, you can visit my Divine Kingdom as a guest."
Although his tone and expression didn’t sound welcoming at all, Gu Nan knew this was already a very sincere invitation.
Daoist Lingyang’s invitation was a bit more simple, "This humble Daoist will return to the Myriad Heavens Universe in a few days. Is Daoist Friend interested in accompanying this one?"
"I still have something to do," Gu Nan refused without even thinking about it, then pointed to himself. "Right, the commission."
At this moment, he remembered it again.
……
Blood had already flowed into a river in the Four Seasons Mountain Valley when Gu Nan returned to the Undead Kingdom. Multiple forces had started fighting, almost triggering a chaotic war in the entire Capital of Blood.
However, everything went as Gu Nan expected. The Raymond clan, which was lurking in the dark, split their troops two ways. One group went to the Capital of Blood to slaughter everyone in Qinghe Pavilion, while the other group made their way to the Four Seasons Mountain Valley.
Since they received the information one step later, of course they arrived later than Lu Xinhuan's group, so again, they didn’t hesitate to ambush and kill the people from Qinghe Pavilion.
However, their ambush just happened to undo the first seal. A burst of power shot up to the sky, exposing both sides at once and attracting the entire city’s attention.
This time, it was the vampires' turn to be out of luck.
The powerhouses from all sides who were attracted by the outburst didn't care what the hell Qinghe Pavilion was. Instead, they were certain that the seal must’ve been opened by the Raymond clan, since the vampires had the greatest advantage here.
Qinghe Pavilion finally got a chance to catch their breath, but Lu Xinhuan didn’t forget the goal of "three vampire hearts."
In the ensuing chaos, the vampires that people normally couldn’t even catch a trace of suddenly seemed to be everywhere.
"The item sealed here is… Cain’s Left Hand?" Even when Sylvia stood in the distant sky overlooking the chaotic battleground, she could still accurately discern the aura inside the seal.
Cain's Left Hand—this vampire clan divine weapon was so famous that even the Goddess of Shadows had heard of it. Legend has it that it was a weapon capable of slaying gods.
"Mm," Gu Nan casually responded, then glanced at her in confusion. "The other three already left. Why are you still following me?"
Sylvia tilted her head and answered, "I have to explain important matters about the organization."
Of course Gu Nan didn’t believe such an excuse, but since she wanted to follow, he wouldn’t care about it too much either. The main thing was that he really wasn't familiar with this Goddess of Shadows, or else it’d be very easy to guess the other party’s thoughts.
The Goddess of Shadows was truly too weak. In his previous life’s game, nobody had time to study this kind of god that players could kill in one hit and who also didn’t have too many good missions on her.
Of course it would never occur to Gu Nan that Sylvia was here because of the law he controlled—she wanted to see him fight using shadows.
After letting her imagination run wild, she decided that the path Gu Nan was taking was the true Shadow Arcana, and the reason she didn’t make much progress all these years was probably because she took the wrong path.
A red light flashed across the ground while the two were talking, and a blood-red coffin slowly emerged, floating in midair.
There was no lid on the coffin, revealing the internal decoration and item—that was an old man dressed in standard knight attire. The strange thing was that half of his left palm had been sliced off.
"Grab his left hand!" Countless shouts came from the surroundings. Everyone stopped at the same time, their gazes fixed on the coffin in midair.
The first to make a move was Lu Xinhuan.
While it was true that she had to use nonviolent business dealings against people, there was no such rule when fighting over treasures!
Lu Xinhuan, who had interacted with Star Rulers for years, revealed astonishing fighting strength at this moment.
She stood alone in front of the coffin, surrounded by a strange field. Any person or attack that neared her would be folded, distorted, and weakened until it was nearly nothing.
Her law wasn’t purely business-related, yet it was also related to it.
The reason Lu Xinhuan dared to make the first move was because of her strength that surpassed most people, as well as…
"Everyone, stop!" Lu Xinhuan grabbed that half of a palm. "Lady Mara, I can give you this divine weapon immediately as long as you agree to one request of mine."
After saying this, she announced to the surroundings: "Everyone, this vampire clan divine weapon must be wielded by a vampire to have the maximum effect. It’s useless even if any of you acquire it. As long as you stop here for today, all losses will be borne by Qinghe Pavilion."
Lu Xinhuan's declaration made the surrounding people fall silent for a while.
These kinds of empty promises couldn’t go so far as to win anyone’s trust, but it could make many people take a wait-and-see approach.
On the other hand, Lady Mara was even more ecstatic and said loudly, "We can agree to any request as long as Your Excellency is willing to return the Ancestor's Staff!"
Lu Xinhuan sighed in relief. Instead of bothering with supporting a clan leader candidate, it was obviously easier to directly exchange Cain's Left Hand for Zhong Die.
However, she suddenly felt the sunlight behind her dim at this moment, as if someone had appeared behind her.
Lu Xinhuan immediately reacted. Her hand flashed with a green light as she crushed a talisman. An unimaginably majestic power gushed out, shielding her whole body.
This power didn’t belong to the mortal world. It was clearly a self-defense treasure bestowed by Zhong Qinghe.
Lu Xinhuan looked back. As expected, she saw Gu Nan’s figure. Her heart sank slightly. ‘To think not even that powerhouse from the organization could stop him…’
However, to her surprise, the other party didn’t seem to have any intention of snatching her prize. Instead, he turned around and headed straight for the coffin.
He was followed by a woman in a long black dress who seemed equally puzzled by his move and asked the question on Lu Xinhuan's mind, "You don’t want Cain’s Left Hand anymore?"
Gu Nan came up to the coffin and ripped off the old man’s entire left arm with a casual tug.
"Now
this
is a left hand." Gu Nan waved the thick arm. "The one in her hand is just a palm at best.

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Mirror God Norris
chapters.content:
Cain's Left Hand could provide a sizable vampire law damage bonus and was very suitable for vampire players. However, it was… a two-handed staff.
That’s right—a two-handed staff. So any player who’d seen pictures of the weapon in the past wouldn’t mistake it, but there were still many beginner players who got it wrong when they first encountered it.
It was also because of this that there were often complaints about Cain's Left Hand in the forum in his previous life. There were even people who deliberately misled newbies to satisfy their own evil delight.
As a veteran player of many years, Gu Nan certainly wouldn’t forget this detail.
Only after Sylvia heard Gu Nan's words did she intentionally study that arm, but she didn’t find anything special about it.
This was very inconceivable to her. After all, she was able to clearly detect the aura inside the seal even from the earlier chaotic battlefield.
Now that the seal was broken and Cain's corpse was right in front of her, how could she still be unable to confirm that there was anything peculiar about his left hand?
Gu Nan, however, knew exactly why this was and casually said, "Take a closer look at this hand. See anything wrong with it?"
Sylvia studied it for a long time but still didn’t find anything. She gave Gu Nan a confused look.
Gu Nan casually beckoned with his hand while expressing concern about this Goddess of Shadow’s intelligence, and the severed half-palm in Lu Xinhuan's hand appeared directly in his hand.
This scene instantly stunned Lu Xinhuan, because the green light around her was clearly still flickering, yet that palm ran into Gu Nan's hand nonetheless.
Since he could take away that half-palm, he could naturally also take away her heart or even her head.
In other words, the protection talisman her Star Ruler left her with was as good as useless in front of this person…
After realizing this, Lu Xinhuan finally understood just what realm the one before her had reached—no wonder he wasn’t the least bit afraid of falling out with her and Qinghe Pavilion.
No wait, that couldn’t be called falling out. At most, it would be an adult bullying a child.
Lu Xinhuan’s complicated mood aside, Sylvia finally realized what was wrong when she saw the severed half-palm.
This half-palm didn’t actually match the arm it was ripped off from!
It wasn’t that someone switched it out with a fake. Both were indeed parts of Cain's body; it’s just that the left and right didn’t quite match.
Sylvia carefully examined it and found that the severed arm was indeed the left arm, but the palm with only four fingers… was clearly the right hand!
The Goddess of Shadows turned her head incredulously towards the corpse inside the coffin, but the hand to the right of the corpse was also a right hand.
Two right hands?
"Cain died at the hands of the Mirror God," Gu Nan used the simplest sentence to convey his meaning when she finally realized what was wrong.
Mirror God Norris!
His strength was only average among Tier 8 gods, but he once stirred up great chaos in the entire World of Gods and was the fuse that set off the Fourth Great War among the gods.
Any god who lived through that period would never forget his name.
As the younger sister of the Ruler of Light and Justice, Sylvia was born almost at the same time as him and was also considered one of the oldest gods, so of course she would know the Mirror God.
Because of this, she deeply understood how uncanny Norris's power was.
Through the law of mirrors, he could map a target into the exact appearance reflected in the mirror and even create a counterpart of it in the Mirror World.
This power worked on objects, people, and even gods.
In the end, the crazy Norris tried to copy the entire world, which brought the entire world’s wrath down upon him. But Norris wasn’t stupid. He pulled a group of gods to his side beforehand, which eventually led to the outbreak of the Fourth Great War among the gods.
Since Cain died by Norris’s hand, it wasn’t so hard to understand why a section of his left hand was reflected by the mirror.
Using her imagination, Sylvia even started to piece together what happened in the past. Back then, a mirror appeared before Cain. He tried to run outside of its range, but ultimately, a part of his left hand was sliced off.
‘But fortunately, Norris has disappeared for tens of thousands of years…’
After her thoughts returned from her imagination, Sylvia sighed in relief but suddenly realized with a start—this fellow called Gu Nan actually knew so much about all this. So then, what did he want to do with Cain’s Left Hand?
An inexplicable fear surfaced in her heart. She looked up sharply, only to find that Gu Nan's figure had already disappeared.
……
"Find Gu Nan. I don't care what method you use." Sylvia sat inside the sanctuary hosting the Ceremony of Blood, while both the vampire princes and the powerhouses from other forces were gathered below her.
But at this moment, they all bowed respectfully. "Yes, Your Highness Sylvia."
When faced with a real god, they had no reason or power to refuse.
Even if Sylvia belonged to the Light Faction and many of the gods backing them belonged to the Dark Faction… Nevertheless, a neutral plane was a neutral plane, and having the protection of those gods wasn’t the same as being their faithful followers.
Moreover, if the gods weren’t at war with each other, then the relationship between the two factions wasn’t actually as tense as one imagined.
Sylvia and the Sky God were both from the Light Faction, while the God of Luxuriant Blossoms belonged to the Dark Faction. But there was a harmonious atmosphere when the three met earlier. None of them had any intention of attacking the other side.
Sitting in the hall, Sylvia's expression was heavy.
She still couldn’t confirm what Gu Nan's goal was, but if she couldn’t find any trace of Gu Nan after a long search, then she would choose to send news back to the Light Faction or even to her older brother.
It wasn’t that she was making a big deal out of it. It was just that Norris, this lunatic, was so terrifying that any information about him must be treated with the utmost seriousness.
But what Sylvia didn't expect was that after just a few days, Gu Nan's whereabouts were reported to her.
This guy had no intention of hiding and strutted into the sanctuary just like that. And he was even… peeping on a siring?!
……
"Pervert!" Sylvia didn’t hesitate to describe Gu Nan as such, and her gaze showed that she believed this in her heart as well.
The vampire clan’s siring was even more secretive than their mating process. After all, mating was only for mutual pleasure, while siring was how they actually developed new descendants—after all, it wasn’t like vampires could get pregnant.
But not only did Gu Nan watch, he even joined in… Please don’t misunderstand, the way he participated was by dropping the golden origin blood into Zhong Die's body.
Zhong Die completed the blood diet process much faster than Gu Nan expected.
When Gu Nan obtained Cain's Left Hand earlier, he didn’t even get to chat with Sylvia for long when he discovered that Zhong Die was already ready to receive the siring.
This extremely special blood fetishist was indeed a natural vampire candidate.
Due to her long-term blood consumption, her digestive system had long since adapted to this diet, even to the point where normal food had to be mixed with blood to be eaten in order to be properly digested and absorbed.
For a human with an ordinary bloodline to torment herself to this point, Zhong Die really wasn’t a normal person.
And precisely because of this, when she found Christina, the latter decided to perform the siring for her without much hesitation.

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Visit
chapters.content:
Christina was a young girl with long coffee-colored hair and soft facial features.
Her face was slightly pale because she’d just finished performing the siring for Zhong Die, but she still regarded Gu Nan warily, along with Sylvia, who suddenly appeared.
"Who are you?" Christina stared at the two but made no move. Anyone who could soundlessly appear before her clearly wasn't simple.
Christina's voice was clear and crisp, as if she really was a young girl. In fact, Gu Nan knew that she actually was very young. She was one of the rare younger generations in the vampire clan.
If the player didn’t interfere, then she would become the future head of the Raymond clan and lead the clan forward, eventually joining the ranks of a powerful god.
She could even be seen in the final war among gods.
But right now, she was just a little fellow who hadn’t even reached Legend Rank yet.
"Don't be nervous. I'm her friend." Gu Nan smiled lightly and pointed to Zhong Die, who was lying in bed drowsily, emitting a thick aura of blood.
Sylvia noticed the vial of blood in Gu Nan's hand and wondered, "Is this… the vampire race’s origin blood?"
The origin of the vampire race naturally referred to the blood of their ancestor.
"Mm." Gu Nan casually nodded, knowing that the other party was curious about this thing’s origin, as well as…
Sylvia took a deep breath and warned, "You'll get her killed. If the vampire race’s origin blood is used on ordinary people… it’s incompatible with their constitution."
Gu Nan cast her a glance but didn’t respond.
He’d heard the phrase "incompatible with their constitution" many times in the game. It wasn’t unfamiliar at all.
Because from the start, the origin blood was an item prepared exclusively for players. Unfortunately, the native NPCs couldn’t enjoy this benefit.
If you ask the gods, you’ll get the answer of "incompatible with their constitution."
In fact, if not for the fact that this quest line was specifically designed for players to change their race to vampires, how could two outsider vampires show up here so coincidentally?
The reason Gu Nan used this on Zhong Die was to see what would happen if Zhong Die took the player’s route.
If this was feasible, then Gu Nan even wanted to use similar methods to create more "protagonist-type NPCs"—he knew many different ways for players to change races or classes.
Of course the natives couldn’t enjoy the benefits given exclusively to players.
But although the natives from the World of Gods couldn’t, what about people from the Myriad Heavens Universe? Gu Nan stared at Zhong Die's face, his gaze deep and even somewhat expectant.
As for how he used a little girl like Zhong Die as an experiment and what kind of risk she was undertaking… Those were outside of Gu Nan's consideration. In any case, he wasn’t the one taking the risk.
After a long time, Zhong Die's breathing remained very even, but she still showed no signs of waking up.
The amount of time she spent unconscious had far exceeded the vampire clan’s normal siring process, and her lips even became a little dry and cracked due to going a long time without food.
Sylvia was sure that it was impossible for a normal person to fuse with origin blood. "It's useless. She’ll die before long."
"She should’ve died a long time ago if this was a normal situation," Gu Nan said with certainty. "Even Legend Rank vampire candidates undergoing the siring wouldn’t last more than half an hour on average."
The phrase "on average" made Sylvia frown, as if she could hear the countless bloodshed behind it.
A few moments later, Zhong Die didn’t let Gu Nan down and actually woke up.
Her gaze was slightly dazed. She looked around in bewilderment, as if confused about where she was.
Wordlessly, Gu Nan waved his hand and had a shadow blade slice open Zhong Die's arm. The latter suddenly started bleeding profusely.
But surprisingly, her blood was actually a dark golden color.
"It's a success!" Gu Nan's heart lifted. It was indeed possible to break through the NPCs’ “physiological limits” by using natives from the Myriad Heavens Universe!
The sharp pain sobered her up. Zhong Die let out a strange scream and hurriedly pulled her hand back.
Immediately, she was surprised to find that the wound on her arm had already stopped bleeding, and the gash was even scabbing over.
"As expected of the vampire race!" Zhong Die marveled. She thought it was because of a vampire’s physique.
But Christina's eyes widened. As a vampire, she knew better than anyone else that a newborn vampire couldn’t possibly possess this kind of ability!
……
In the days that followed, Gu Nan just swaggered into the sanctuary and started living here, training Zhong Die every day and also collecting various data on her new physique.
The conclusion was that Zhong Die's fusion of the origin blood was very successful and had practically the same result as a player—she was just missing an Evil God physique.
On the other hand, since Cain's Left Hand was still in Gu Nan's hands, the Raymond clan was extremely welcoming about him living here.
Of course, if he didn’t display such terrifying power earlier, the vampire clan’s welcome wouldn’t have been this kind of welcome.
In the face of a powerful figure suspected of being a god, even the Raymond clan didn’t dare to threaten him.
They could only hope to use the resources at hand to exchange for the Ancestor’s Staff, or wait until Gu Nan was in a good mood and bestow this divine weapon upon them.
In fact, Gu Nan had already turned away over 20 vampires, all of whom came to his door trying to throw themselves into his arms.
Vampires historically had such a tradition and were adept at taking advantage of their beautiful appearances. Thankfully, over half of those who came to his door were women.
Gu Nan's assessment of Zhong Die was all-encompassing. Her physical strength, recovery ability, speed, sensitivity towards laws, and even beauty—all of them were evaluated one by one.
All these data were strictly recorded, fully demonstrating Zhong Die's current constitution and the entire origin blood modification process.
Two months later, Zhong Die had practically transformed into another person.
The current Zhong Die had long blonde hair. Her skin was fair and flawless, her pupils were an attractive coffee color, and she even grew by several centimeters, making her entire person appear tall and well-proportioned.
He was afraid that not even Lu Xinhuan would recognize her now.
On this day, Gu Nan was still training little Zhong Die as usual when a sudden clamor came from outside.
"What happened?" Gu Nan had little reaction to the commotion, while Zhong Die had already asked impatiently.
After suffering unspeakable misery in Gu Nan's training program, Zhong Die couldn't wait for something to happen right now.
"No matter what happens, it has nothing to do with you," Christina poured a bucket of cold water over Zhong Die’s head and directly extinguished her fantasy.
As Zhong Die's sire, she would also occasionally come to supervise Zhong Die's training.
Zhong Die couldn't help pouting, but Gu Nan said with a smile, "Actually, it really does have something to do with her this time."
……
Outside the sanctuary, Lu Xinhuan glared at Lady Mara with a frosty expression. "I've come to request a meeting with Lord Gu Nan."
Lady Mara didn’t have any good feelings towards Qinghe Pavilion. She revealed a cold smile. "It depends on whether that Lord is willing to see you."
Lu Xinhuan, however, didn’t say anything and just pointed to the two figures behind her.
"For the sake of these two, I believe that Lord will be willing to give me this opportunity."
The two behind her were a man and a woman. The woman was Shana, who’d already advanced to Legend Rank by this point, while the man was Zi Dian, who had a long sword hanging from his waist and a helpless look on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 363: Outcome
chapters.content:
The atmosphere outside the sanctuary had fallen into a strange sort of silence.
No vampire present recognized either Shana or Zi Dian.
Nothing needed to be said about Zi Dian. And although Shana was a member of the Raymond clan, she was listed as a “defector,” and she was also an insignificant nobody within the clan even before she defected.
The inability to identify the two hostages meant they couldn’t make a decision.
Lady Mara was already regretting this a little. Had she known this, she wouldn’t have personally come out to deal with Lu Xinhuan in order to curry favor with that one.
If the vampire who received Lu Xinhuan was just a junior, then they would’ve been able to let Lu Xinhuan in without even having to think. At worst, they would’ve been tricked by Lu Xinhuan once but wouldn’t have lost much face.
But since Mara herself was standing here, she’d lose all her face if she let Lu Xinhuan in, only to have Gu Nan ask, "Who are these two?”
Vampires were a very special race. They could commit unimaginably depraved acts in private, but they also incomparably valued face when in public.
Lu Xinhuan saw the predicament the vampires were in, and a trace of anxiousness flashed through her cold eyes. Without time for further thought, she launched a palm strike directly at Lady Mara’s back.
There was no way she wasn’t anxious—Qinghe Pavilion paid an astronomical price in order to hold up Wu Gui.
To put it bluntly, Lu Xinhuan was currently using the lives of her own people to buy time. How could she have time to waste on Mara?
However, her attack saved Lady Mara from her dilemma—since there was already a commotion, she could just take advantage of the situation to inform Gu Nan, which was also what she intended to do earlier.
"What is it?" Gu Nan arrived sooner than they thought, accompanied by a blonde girl who stood behind him with a reserved expression.
Lu Xinhuan couldn't help taking a deep breath when she saw Gu Nan.
She was well aware that the one before her had the ability to kill her easily, but she had come with the determination to face death, so she didn’t have much fear.
If she didn’t even have the courage to put her life on the line, how could she bring Zhong Die back?
Lu Xinhuan secretly encouraged herself and said in a low voice, "My Lord must surely recognize these two, right? They have already taken the special gu of Qinghe Realm. The gu worm has entered their hearts—they’ll die within two days without the antidote."
Lu Xinhuan said this with confidence.
No one in this world was completely free of weaknesses. Although Gu Nan was certainly powerful to a terrifying extent, as long as there was still something he wanted, then he would have a weakness.
As someone who could become one of Qinghe Realm’s managers, Lu Xinhuan was fully aware of this.
Since she accompanied Gu Nan all the way to the World of Gods, she concluded that he needed Wu Gui and Zi Dian’s help. On the other hand, she also investigated Gu Nan's behavior in the Capital of Blood, from the flower girl to Shana. Thus, it was logical to also capture Shana.
If even these two were unable to "move" Gu Nan, then Lu Xinhuan really would be out of options—she did her best; the rest was up to fate.
Lu Xinhuan recited that sentence in her heart and stared at Gu Nan with a bright gaze. "My Lord, as long as you promise to return Zhong Die to Qinghe Realm, everyone present will be yours to punish, including me."
Lu Xinhuan really was smart. She knew how to get along with Star Rulers. One of the core principles was to use the humblest attitude possible.
But she never could’ve expected for Gu Nan’s response to simply be to turn around and pat the blonde girl’s shoulder.
"Go say hello."
Gu Nan's voice suddenly made Lu Xinhuan feel panicked.
"Big Sis Lu," the blonde girl, Zhong Die, shouted in her familiar crisp voice and even skipped over to Lu Xinhuan's side like nothing had happened.
Zhong Die, who grew slightly, was already a little taller than Lu Xinhuan. With the vampires’ standard high heels, the two’s heights became reversed.
Lu Xinhuan raised her head to stare at the Zhong Die who was already a complete stranger. She could only find a shadow of Zhong Die’s former self from the outline of her face.
"You… already underwent the siring?" She asked, stupefied.
"Yeah!" Zhong Die still had an innocent expression.
Even Gu Nan didn't expect for Zhong Die to be ready for the siring so quickly, so Lu Xinhuan was even less likely to consider it—thus, she screwed herself over.
She came here almost exactly after two months had passed since the Ceremony of Blood. Only with this much time was she able to make sufficient preparations to kidnap Zi Dian.
But now, Zhong Die smashed all her schemes and plans to pieces with only one word, like a thunderbolt from a clear sky.
"How could this be…" Classmate Lu’s mind was a mush. She was completely speechless.
"Let's go, we’ll continue training," Gu Nan's unhurried words traveled over.
Zhong Die, who hadn't had a chance to catch up with Lu Xinhuan, could only pout and walk back obediently.
Ever since she woke up, she never disobeyed Gu Nan's orders. Gu Nan’s orders were even more effective than Christina’s.
This was also very normal. Christina was her direct sire, while Gu Nan was the one who imparted the origin blood to her.
In terms of her origin as a vampire, if Gu Nan was her real father, then Christina would be a surrogate mother at best, or perhaps even a test tube.
"No!" Lu Xinhuan seemed to be startled awake and let out a loud shout.
She grabbed Zhong Die's wrist and said in a heavy voice, "Even if you already accepted the siring, I still have to take you back. Maybe—"
Lu Xinhuan didn’t get to finish before countless black tentacles suddenly lunged out from her shadow and completely wrapped her up.
The hand she used to grab Zhong Die's wrist was also forcibly pried off by those tentacles, and then her entire person quickly fell into her own shadow.
Lu Xinhuan, who was dragged into the ground and whose entire body save half her face was already swallowed up by her shadow, was still able to see this scene.
‘Why…? Does he not care about these two’s lives at all?’
But Lu Xinhuan could no longer see the result, because she had completely fallen into her shadow.
This incomparably eerie scene made everyone present feel their scalps tingle. Not even the vampires had seen such a method of killing people before.
What was even more eerie was that not long after, a ball of black shadow began to churn in the shadow and soon formed a new human figure.
"What’s the method to remove the gu worms?" Gu Nan casually asked.
The shadow began to dutifully report the "recipe": "Blue Heart Grass, Silver Moon White Frost, hind claws of the Great Eagle…"
Gu Nan rarely used the law of resurrection ever since he reached Tier 6, but this didn’t mean he couldn’t use it anymore.
On the contrary, as his strength grew, the law of resurrection also became much more effective than before when used on lower-leveled opponents. The shadow servants were able to retain most of their memories from life.
Of course, it was almost completely useless against gods.
"Is this also an application of shadows?" Sylvia, who had appeared beside Gu Nan at some point, stared at the shadow servant in surprise.
Gu Nan didn’t know how to explain that players had several law slots, so he thought about it and answered, "It might sound unbelievable, but this is called Shadow Resurrection. It’s one the ultimate arcana of our law of shadows."

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Saving Money
chapters.content:
Sylvia was always by Gu Nan’s side recently. She was still worried about Gu Nan's plans for the Mirror God.
After learning that Gu Nan would use Cain's Left Hand soon, she simply started following him to see what he was actually going to use the staff for.
On the other hand, she was also very curious about this other controller of shadows.
Her efforts finally paid off. Classmate Sylvia eventually saw Gu Nan make a move, and his first move was using a power she’d never seen before.
"So the power of shadows can also be used to create life?" Sylvia murmured. Her mind was already filled with "Shadow Resurrection”—a term Gu Nan made up on the spot— there was no room for anything else in her head.
Gu Nan gave a somewhat strange smile. He didn’t mind leading Sylvia astray. Anyhow, regardless of whether it was the right or wrong path, this Goddess of Shadows wouldn’t be able to grow stronger even after tens of thousands of years.
Maybe she could even discover an entirely new path if he directed her down a nonsensical path?
Gu Nan shook his head and threw both Zi Dian and Shana to Lady Mara, asking her to help find the antidote.
The information revealed by the shadow servant of Lu Xinhuan wasn’t completely exact. There were still some vague places in the formula.
But this didn't matter. In any case, Qinghe Pavilion still had lots of these kinds of gu worms lying around, so they could simply find some random people to test the antidote on. Two days was enough time to determine the correct antidote.
Of course Gu Nan didn’t know if the shadow servant’s information was complete or not, but he didn’t care all that much if the two hostages died.
Zi Dian was merely a bonus that came with Wu Gui, and while it would naturally be best if Shana could survive, Gu Nan also had Christina as a substitute if she died, so Shana wasn’t a must-have either.
If not for the fact that he was in a hurry, then a conventional genius like Christina would actually be more suited to being the clan head, both in terms of personality and prestige.
……
Gu Nan didn’t have to wait too long. Just two days later, a perfectly intact Zi Dian and Shana stood in front of Gu Nan.
The Raymond clan was quite competent when it came to handling matters, especially since they wanted to request something from Gu Nan.
And someone else who also arrived at the same time was the maiden Wu Gui, whom Gu Nan hadn’t seen for a long time.
Wu Gui currently looked a little disheveled. Her exquisite kasaya was slightly tattered, and she even put away the lotus pedestal she always sat on, instead electing to rush here on foot.
Indeed, Qinghe Realm’s power couldn’t be underestimated. Just a single Lu Xinhuan could call over a helper of Sylvia’s level and even stall Wu Gui for a while.
"You sure have it easy, leaving us behind in Skeleton City and then arbitrarily falling out with the people from Qinghe Realm." Wu Gui saw Gu Nan’s calm expression and was instantly furious.
With her and Zi Dian's patience, waiting for two months was nothing, but the people of Qinghe Pavilion suddenly turning on them was truly unexpected.
It could be said that Gu Nan's act of abducting Zhong Die indirectly screwed Wu Gui and Zi Dian over.
But Gu Nan shrugged, entirely unconcerned. He’d always acted without regard for what others thought. As long as it didn’t affect his plans, who cares who died?
"You’re just in time. I had these vampires investigate the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead. We’ll leave as soon as there’s a result," Gu Nan told Wu Gui.
In his original plan, he was already planning to have the vampires search the entrance to the Sacred Catacombs. Lu Xinhuan and her group were actually an accident.
"I hope we won't have to wait too long this time," Wu Gui couldn’t do anything about him, so she could only throw down such a sentence.
Gu Nan naturally ignored her. His daily routine continued to be training Zhong Die. Oh, and there was one more task, which was to help Shana run for clan head.
Because the God of Iron was also behind the Raymond clan, Gu Nan couldn’t just kidnap the entire clan—not if he didn’t want to completely expose his existence to this side.
The way he helped Shana was also very simple—he gave her Cain’s Left Hand.
Shana fused her own origin blood with it as soon as she received this staff, turning this divine weapon into her sole possession.
From then on, unless she died, she was the only one who could use this staff.
This was too much of an advantage in the clan leader election!
The Ancestor’s Staff was able to directly enhance the purity of a vampire’s bloodline and indirectly increase the strength of the vampire clan.
Now that it fell into Shana's hands, even if the entire clan could use it, it would only be through Shana.
And since there were so many people in the clan, there had to be a line, right? Who could go first and who would be next, as well as who could use it for a longer time—as the owner of the divine weapon, Shana undoubtedly had an extremely large say in it.
Even if she gave off the impression of treating everyone equally on the surface, it was quite a simple matter for her to tamper with the actual process slightly.
Day by day, Shana stabilized her position in the Raymond clan, and voices supporting her to become the next clan head also grew.
It was at a time like this when they found one of the entrances to the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead.
The Sacred Catacombs of the Undead was indeed a mystical place. Not only did it have nine entrances, but each one’s location was in constant flux.
Almost every once in a while, an entrance would appear in a different place.
Gu Nan's luck was pretty good this time. One of the entrances wasn’t far from the Capital of Blood, and he could get there in two days while traveling on foot.
Three figures slowly appeared at the entrance to Yorktown, the location of the current entrance.
"It's on that mountain," said the white-robed young man among the trio.
Beside him were two women. One was dressed in a gold kasaya, but with an expression as cold as frost. The other one wore a black dress, and her gaze kept wandering around.
The three quickly headed for the mountain peak, but a few people at the foot of the mountain immediately stepped forward, blocking their way.
"Who are you three? Up ahead is—"
Before their voices fell, the white-robed youth had already swallowed them all into the shadows with a gentle wave of his hand.
These three newcomers were naturally Gu Nan and his party. He brought Wu Gui to the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead, and Sylvia also followed them.
"How cruel!" Sylvia shook her head, expressing her distaste of Gu Nan's action.
Wu Gui cast her a puzzled glance. In the former's eyes, this girl in black was clearly also a Star Ruler existence. By all rights, she really shouldn’t be so sentimental.
Gu Nan, however, just smiled. He knew that the gods in the World of Gods had a closer relationship with mortals than Star Rulers did. After all, they still required faith.
Gu Nan and his group clearly weren’t the first to discover the entrance to the Sacred Catacombs. The entire road up the mountain was guarded by people.
But news of a strong enemy attack spread quickly, and no one dared to come up and stop them again after a few waves of people died at Gu Nan's hands.
When the three of them reached the top of the mountain, they saw a faintly fluorescent cave entrance surrounded by groups of powerful figures from various sides.
This was clearly not the one “real” entrance everyone knew how to open, so everyone was blocked outside, while a few who refused to give up were still trying to use their own methods to open it.
Gu Nan merely glanced at the sign outside the cave, then told Wu Gui with a smile, "Your luck isn’t bad."
Wu Gui's luck really was good. The random entrance they found just happened to correspond to the tomb of the Living Dead.
Perhaps some of the surrounding people overheard Gu Nan. Immediately, someone walked over with a smile. "Do you want to try solving the entrance's puzzle? Just pay three hundred divine gold coins each."
Sylvia stared at this person somewhat speechlessly, not expecting that even a Sacred Catacombs they couldn't open could be turned into a means of raking in money.
But she also didn’t care about such a small amount of gold coins. For a place like the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead, it was obviously better to sneak in rather than cause a commotion.
But Gu Nan continued walking forward by himself. The man who came up to talk leisurely blocked Gu Nan’s way, still smiling.
Several commerce guilds joined forces to control the entrance. They were strong enough to bully normal experts, and the truly strong powerhouses wouldn’t care about this meager amount of money anyways.
After all, the fewer people who knew about the Sacred Catacombs, the better. He believed that no one wanted information on this place to be made public.
However, the next moment, his head flew up into the sky and landed heavily to the side, while Gu Nan didn't even spare him a glance.
As far as players were concerned, money that can be saved by killing people definitely should be saved—Gu Nan said so in his heart, making it sound like he actually had any money in the first place.

chapters.title: Chapter 365: Sacred Catacombs of the Undead
chapters.content:
"Who are you three?!"
"The Sacred Catacombs is guarded by our four organizations. What do you intend to do?"
"We are…"
Gu Nan naturally wasn’t interested in knowing who exactly was guarding the Sacred Catacombs. Anyhow, his goal was inside; it had nothing to do with the people guarding it outside.
Gu Nan practically slaughtered everyone who tried to block his way. Finally, Sylvia couldn’t bear to watch this anymore and revealed a trace of her divine aura. From then on, no one dared to trouble them.
But now they were curious about a new question—exactly which Highness would actually be interested in the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead?
No matter how “legendary” Legend Rank necromancers were, they were still mere mortals. How could they be important enough to warrant a god descending here?
In a place like the Undead Kingdom, it was very likely that the god would be using their true bodies to descend rather than just a saint clone!
Gu Nan didn’t pay any attention to these people’s attitude. He reached the entrance of the Sacred Catacombs and created a strange symbol with the power of shadows, which landed on the cave entrance.
This symbol perfectly combined with the original symbol on the entrance, forming a brand new inscription.
Then Gu Nan gently waved his hand and actually divided that inscription in two, sending one to either side of the entrance so that the cave’s luminescence slowly dimmed.
Only when Gu Nan and his two companions entered the cave did he casually close the door.
"Is that the Tatton language?" After entering the Sacred Catacombs, Sylvia searched her memory for that previous inscription and finally remembered. It was the superimposition of the Tatton characters for "life" and "death."
"To be precise, it's the ancient Tatton language," Gu Nan corrected absentmindedly. "The Living Dead, Count Fersen, was a Tattonian. He was the one who left that character at the entrance.”
Fersen was from the Middle Ages, so the language he used was already considered ancient. But in Sylvia's eyes, of course there was no difference between ancient and modern Tatton languages.
She already existed long before the first Tattonians appeared.
Of the nine entrances, the entrance corresponding to the Living Dead’s tomb was considered relatively easy to unlock. To put it bluntly, it was just superimposing two characters, then artificially removing part of the lines.
As long as someone knew Count Fersen was a Tattonian and then guessed this puzzle’s general train of thought, it wasn’t hard to solve.
Wu Gui remained silent, but her gaze gradually turned serious as she looked around cautiously. According to Gu Nan, what she needed was inside here.
But her caution was basically useless because Gu Nan knew this place like his own backyard.
The Tattonians were very famous for their necromantic technology. They were necromancers who specialized in alchemy, so Fersen’s tomb had a large number of alchemical creations.
Traps, stone statues, and even homunculus maids—one after another, a whole bunch of things that couldn’t be seen in the Myriad Heavens Universe appeared in front of Gu Nan and his group.
But these defenses were as useful as a piece of paper. Under Gu Nan's "brilliant leadership," the three didn’t even pause their footsteps and reached the deepest part of the tomb as if they were taking a stroll.
"This is it." Gu Nan pointed to the coffin on the ground.
Fersen’s coffin was very strange. The left and right sides were actually different: the left side was made of dark red wood, while the right side was made of some sort of special crystal.
"Fersen was half-living and half-dead. Half of his body was human, but the other half had already started turning into an undead, and he actually remained in this state for years on end," Gu Nan knew Fersen’s situation like the back of his hand.
Living Dead Fersen was quite a legendary character in the game’s backstory. He wasn’t at all inferior to Sandro, the necromancer people worshiped as a demigod.
When Fersen was alive, he practically conquered the entire plane by himself. His undead empire had already taken control of half the continent. Although he ultimately lost to the Lionheart Queen, it wasn’t entirely his fault.
In contrast, although people made Sandro sound so incredible, the largest territory he ever had was only the size of three dukedoms. Most of his merits were academic in nature.
Merely in terms of pushing forward the progress of necromantic magic, Sandro was indeed number one since time immemorial, with seven or eight different milestones, each in a different field.
Wu Gui had little interest in the history of the World of Gods. Her gaze never left that coffin, while Gu Nan had already opened it with a flourish.
Like he said, a corpse with distinctly different left and right sides was laid out in front of the trio.
"Do I take his origin?" Wu Gui stared at Fersen’s corpse and asked after some thought.
She no longer doubted that this person possessed the law of fusion she wanted, but she still wasn't sure how to extract it.
"The dude has been dead for almost 100,000 years, what origin is there?" Gu Nan rolled his eyes. "You can just take the whole coffin away. But be careful—the corpse will quickly decay after leaving the Sacred Catacombs."
Wu Gui didn't retort and just nodded silently. She wasn’t worried about the corpse rotting away. Since the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead could preserve the corpse, so could she.
After getting Fersen’s corpse, Gu Nan didn't dally any longer and walked directly towards the back of the tomb.
"Norris has slept for so many years. It's time to wake him up," Gu Nan mumbled while walking.
Sylvia was suddenly wide-awake. She pointed at Gu Nan and exclaimed, "So you really do want to wake up Norris!"
Gu Nan turned his head back with a smile. "I never denied it either."
Sylvia's expression sank slightly when she heard that. "Since you know Norris is here, you should’ve informed the public. Norris is the gods’ public enemy. Unless… Unless you want to cooperate with him?!"
This Goddess of Shadows really did have a wild imagination. Gu Nan couldn’t help correcting her, “I’ll kill him.”
In fact, in terms of identity, Gu Nan was more suited to be called the gods’ public enemy rather than the Mirror God—after all, he was the gods’ natural enemy, while Norris only became an enemy later in life.
But for the sake of Gu Nan's Evil Value, he could only wrong the Mirror God a little and have him become exp.
Sylvia didn’t speak again, but her gaze shifted slightly. She clearly didn’t believe Gu Nan, or at least she didn’t believe he had the ability to kill Norris.
She was already mulling over the possibility that if Norris truly was still alive and if Gu Nan died in the other party's hands, then she would escape this place immediately and spread the news.
If it wasn’t for the fact that the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead was a special place, she would’ve gone outside to deliver the news right then and there. But she also knew that Gu Nan most certainly wouldn’t let her go out now.
They didn’t even take two steps further when she saw Gu Nan suddenly stop, take out the Cain’s Left Hand he retrieved from Shana, and stab it into the ground.
Just how terrifying was Gu Nan’s strength? A crack actually appeared in the Sacred Catacombs, which was built from countless mysterious runes, while the somewhat withered Cain’s Left Hand showed signs of fracturing.
But this was already enough.
An inexplicable aura circled around the interior of the Sacred Catacombs, followed by a faint sigh. "I never thought someone would actually find this place…"
"Norris!" Sylvia instantly recognized this voice—young and calm, yet with a hint of madness.

chapters.title: Chapter 366: I’m Sure
chapters.content:
Where was Norris hiding? This was something many gods tried to find out, but no one ever found any results.
Even Sylvia didn’t expect for him to be hiding in an abandoned main plane, and in a place like the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead to boot—a place countless people ventured inside, often overturning everything inside to search for treasures.
Perhaps this was called “the darkest place is directly underneath the lamp
[1]
.”
When too many adventurers were captivated by the treasures in the Sacred Catacombs, they naturally wouldn’t notice the other tombs, much less the space between the tombs.
In fact, Norris hid very well. His hiding place was just a single point in the entire Sacred Catacombs. If one didn’t smash apart the Sacred Catacombs bit by bit, nobody would be able to discover him.
Moreover, the explorers also must’ve guessed at his existence and brought along an item containing the law of mirrors he left behind in the past in order to break through the Mirror World and awaken the remains of his soul ahead of schedule.
Both of these conditions had to be met to awaken him, which practically formed a perfect defense. But what Norris couldn’t imagine was that even with all this, someone still found him.
Of course NPCs wouldn’t understand that there was a group of people called players. When they were bored, they liked to take the whole world apart for fun.
And while dismantling the world, they discovered that there was still a god hidden here. Only then did they start analyzing his origin to look for a way to awaken him.
Norris wore transparent glasses and had a scholarly air about him. His short silver-gray hair covered half of his forehead, and he held a thin book in one hand.
"You’re the one who woke me up." Norris's gaze fell on Gu Nan, looking serene and calm. No semblance of madness could be seen from his face.
Just from appearance alone, no one would ever be able to connect Norris with the impression the world had of him.
Sylvia pursed her lips tightly, having already tensed up. She would immediately take action as soon as Norris made a move.
Norris had long gotten used to eliciting this kind of reaction from people. Rather, Gu Nan’s always-calm expression made him a little curious.
"Why did you awaken me? Oh, no need to answer—let me guess. To borrow my power? To use me to look for some old fellows from back then? Or is it…"
With a charming smile on his face, Norris said it one word at a time, "You want to finish what I started?"
He didn’t even entertain the possibility of "eliminating evil to protect the people.” If this was the goal, then there was no way only three people would come.
Sylvia quickly turned her head, nervously watching Gu Nan, fearful that he’d say, “Yup.”
Gu Nan didn’t let her down. He didn’t even have any intention of responding to Norris. He patted Wu Gui’s shoulder and told her, "You’re up first."
Gu Nan’s attitude stunned both Norris and the Goddess of Shadows.
No matter how detested Norris was and how many disasters he caused, he was once a figure that influenced the entire World of Gods.
Whether he was hated, mocked, or praised, no one could ignore his existence—but Gu Nan did.
It was probably very hard for them to understand that Norris was nothing more than a monster to Gu Nan.
No matter how rich a backstory or how many legendary experiences a monster had, a monster was just a monster, and monsters were meant to be killed.
Like Gu Nan, someone else who could also ignore Norris was Wu Gui—she flat-out didn’t recognize him.
But since she already acquired the coffin of the Living Dead, Wu Gui didn’t mind fulfilling her end of the bargain.
So Wu Gui struck without hesitation. A palm print carrying both demonic and Buddhist intent smashed towards Norris.
Norris laughed involuntarily. He gently raised the book in his hand, and a silver mirror appeared in front of him.
Wu Gui saw her own reflection in the mirror before her. The closer she got to it, the clearer the palm print in the mirror became.
When Wu Gui’s strike finally landed on the silver mirror, almost the exact same power hit her back instantly.
The silver mirror immediately shattered, while Wu Gui herself grunted in pain—anyone who blasted herself once with her full strength wouldn’t feel too good.
However, Norris just chuckled. He’d seen too many such opponents in his ten thousand years of war.
‘Even if I’ve just awakened from the seal, I’m still not someone who… Hm?’
Silver mist once again burst out in front of Norris. Another mirror was blown apart—this time, it was Gu Nan who attacked.
Gu Nan’s fist was covered in blood, and ghastly white bones could even be seen, but he seemed as if he couldn’t feel it at all.
Norris’s eyes narrowed slightly as he placed silver mirrors one after another in front of him, but Gu Nan blasted each of them apart with a punch.
When the two were finally facing each other, Norris suddenly revealed a faint smile as a thin, frameless mirror appeared behind him.
The thin mirror reflected Norris's figure. Gu Nan’s punch landed and shattered Norris's body, but the Norris inside the mirror remained perfectly intact.
Gu Nan didn’t even pause for a second and threw another punch at the mirror.
The sound of impact came again, and the thin mirror was also shattered, while Gu Nan had an additional wound on his hand that quickly started to heal.
But it was clear that Norris couldn’t be killed so easily.
"It's useless." A clear madness began to seep through his voice, "Although you can kill one of me, what about hundreds of me?"
As Norris's words fell, hundreds of mirrors actually appeared in front of Gu Nan, with the Mirror God’s figure in the center of each one.
However, Gu Nan just smiled silently. He instantly rushed into a mirror while telling his companions, "You two guard the center."
Sylvia and Wu Gui didn’t dare to delay and quickly reached the center of the hundreds of mirrors, waiting for further instructions. Only then did they see a scene that made their jaws drop.
Gu Nan, who had entered the mirror, rapidly flew between different mirrors like an agile monkey and quickly killed hundreds of Norris reflections.
"You’re not a god," there was an inexplicable meaning in Norris's crazed voice.
The Mirror World was his foundation. Here, he could alter the laws at will, so any god who fell into this world would inevitably be helpless.
Not even the Ruler of Light and Justice would be able to use half of his original power after entering a world made purely of the law of darkness.
But this was completely meaningless to Gu Nan, because he was only using his physical body to fight, so he wasn’t dependent on any laws at all!
It was precisely because of this that Norris was certain he wasn’t a god—no god would have such a powerful physical body.
Gu Nan smiled wordlessly. If this was in the game, then perhaps his identity as an Evil God would already be seen through by now. But fortunately, the Myriad Heavens Universe existed in this world.
The gods' understanding of the Myriad Heavens Universe was far from deep, not to mention there were indeed body-refining cultivators in the Myriad Heavens Universe.
Norris didn't have time to ponder this too much. He’d just awakened and was already in his weakest state. Faced with an enemy who knew him incomparably well, he could only choose to flee for now.
He instantly vanished from the Mirror World. Sylvia reacted extremely fast and immediately attacked with her shadow divine power, which was boosted with the power of her Divine Kingdom. She was already going all-out from the start.
Wu Gui also materialized her true body. Her half-Buddha and half-demon form had eight arms that carried eight kinds of weapons, which all struck Norris at the same time.
Norris’s expression remained unchanged. Since he dared to leave the Mirror World, he was naturally prepared to deal with these two. ‘A weak god and a mere demigod… Huh?’
Norris suddenly froze as he looked up in astonishment and saw a Buddhist staff hovering horizontally over the top of his head, flickering with a stunning golden light.
"A real god?!"
Even Sylvia couldn’t help glancing at Wu Gui, surprised that this person wasn’t actually much weaker than her… Now that Norris miscalculated, he would have a hard time.
In fact, it wasn’t a matter of having a hard time. Rather, as long as Norris was delayed by even an instant, he would most certainly die.
Norris, who was incomparably mysterious, powerful, and unhinged in the eyes of countless gods, was merely a Tier 8 monster to Gu Nan.
Just like how he crushed Norris’s clones, Gu Nan's extremely plain fist smashed the top of Norris's head, instantly shattering the Godhead of this extremely weakened Tier 8 god.
All the mirrors around them disappeared at once as Gu Nan’s group was returned to the Sacred Catacombs.
Gu Nan glanced at the corpse on the ground and smiled in satisfaction. "All in a day’s work."
"Wait!" Sylvia saw that he was about to leave and rushed up while grumbling, "This is Norris! How can you be sure he’s actually dead?"
"It might sound unbelievable," Gu Nan glanced at his own skyrocketing 2,500 Evil Value and answered, "but I’m sure."
T/N:
[1]
“The darkest place is directly underneath the lamp”
- People often neglect what’s right under their nose

chapters.title: Chapter 367: Return Trip
chapters.content:
The trip to the Sacred Catacombs of the Undead seemed uneventful. In fact, Gu Nan's entire trip after reaching the World of Gods was methodically arranged.
He was way too familiar with this place, so familiar that even if some unexpected events occurred, he could still turn the situation around easily with his experience—and of course, power.
So Gu Nan didn’t feel much about Norris's death and soon left the Sacred Catacombs as usual.
On the contrary, Sylvia was troubled ever since the battle. The Norris who once stirred up such great chaos actually died so quietly. This was a little hard for her to accept.
In a sense, Sylvia didn’t seem like a god who lived for tens of thousands of years, but like a normal adventurer with considerable strength.
There was a reason for this.
Compared to the Star Rulers of the Myriad Heavens Universe, who gradually broke away from the category of humans ever since they entered Star Ruler Realm, the gods here clearly seemed more “human.”
Due to the different laws of space, the Legend Ranks here—which correspond to Void Cutter Realm—didn’t have the ability to break through space, so naturally they couldn’t develop a high-and-mighty mentality.
Legend Rank powerhouses living in the mortal world still had to face the aging, illnesses, and deaths of their loved ones and friends. They still had to endure the distance of space, so how could they be high and mighty?
That was why gods here used the expression "divinity."
But in the Myriad Heavens Universe, all the Star Rulers had long since accepted the gap between themselves and mortals. The reason they climbed step by step from Void Cutter Realm to their current position certainly wasn’t to live together with mortals.
When Gu Nan’s group of three stepped out of the Sacred Catacombs, the onlookers outside had almost dispersed.
The reason was also quite simple. Two men in red robes were standing at the entrance, respectfully waiting for the people inside to come out.
As soon as the three showed themselves, the two red-robed men immediately greeted them while performing an odd salute, "Your Esteemed Highness Sylvia, on behalf of My Lord, I would like to send you the sincerest… Eh?"
Their voices faltered mid-sentence, because they realized the one walking at the head of the trio wasn’t Her Excellency the Goddess of Shadows like they expected, but a young man they didn't recognize.
"Mishra’s apostles?" The youth raised his head to glance at the two, then at the symbol on their chests, and wondered, "Don’t even know how to say a greeting?"
Mishra was the God of Minotaurs and one of the subordinate gods of the Beast God. These two were clearly his apostles.
The two men's faces instantly turned beet red. When an apostle representing a god greets another god, that greeting is naturally of the utmost importance.
The two apostles rushed over to pay their respects when they heard that Sylvia appeared in this place, but they didn’t expect to run headfirst into Gu Nan instead.
"W-Who are you? Why do you address My Lord directly by his name?" One of the apostles came back to his senses and instantly glared at Gu Nan furiously.
Compared to the problem of botching a greeting, referring to a god directly by their actual name was naturally a greater offense. It was normal for this apostle to try to use this as an excuse to change the subject.
Gu Nan didn’t even spare the two another glance and walked forward by himself.
The apostle blocking his way was directly grabbed by his hair and tossed to the side, where not even his shadow could be seen anymore.
The other apostle stared blankly at this scene and just watched as the trio walked past him.
The two apostles were just a brief interlude. Gu Nan's journey wasn’t affected by them at all, and he soon returned to the Capital of Blood.
At this stage, Gu Nan basically achieved all his goals for this trip to the World of Gods.
His Evil Value successfully reached 5,000, and in the process of incorporating the vampire clan into the ranks of his apostles, Cain's Left Hand also came in handy. He even discovered an unexpected pleasant surprise along the way.
He experimented to see whether Zhong Die, a native from the Myriad Heavens Universe, could take the player route, creating player-type NPCs that originally couldn’t have possibly existed.
In the following days, Shana, with Gu Nan's full support, quickly ascended to the position of the Raymond clan’s leader, then set off a wave of bloodshed in the Capital of Blood.
Under Shana's leadership, the Raymond clan suddenly became very aggressive, almost annexing the entire Capital of Blood into their sphere of influence and invading the territories of all other forces.
Such a move allowed the Raymond clan to harvest a large amount of resources at the very start, but it also brought down the wrath of the entire public upon them.
A large number of vampires died in the war. The Raymond clan's former glory could no longer be maintained.
But vampires really were a rule-abiding race. Even in such a situation, Shana still maintained considerable control over the clan.
Of course, this was also thanks to her possession of the Ancestor's Staff.
If not for the existence of this divine weapon, with the vampires’ "wanton" acts during this period, they probably would’ve been wiped out by now.
The chaos in the Capital of Blood lasted only half a month or so. Before the God of Iron could react, Gu Nan had Shana throw out the trump card.
"All clansmen, prepare to move," Shana announced from her seat at the head of the round table, overlooking the crowd below.
Her expression was solemn and unperturbed. After using the power of the Ancestor’s Staff, Shana was no longer a weakling among Legend Rank experts. She was now strong enough to force her clansmen into submission.
"Move to where?" The crowd of vampires revealed a stunned look. For a race that accepted a god’s protection, clan migration was not a trivial matter.
"Of course it's… to My Lord's Divine Kingdom." Shana revealed a faint smile and stood up while Gu Nan slowly walked out from behind her.
……
The migration of the Raymond clan went more smoothly than expected.
This race living in the Undead Kingdom really didn’t have much faith to speak of in any god, so much so that they didn’t even hold much loyalty to the gods.
Shana used only one sentence to convince the vast majority of people: "Stay here and be annihilated by the furious enemies, or come with me and enjoy the blessing of the Ancestor’s Staff."
Gu Nan and the others were originally from the Myriad Heavens Universe, so they wouldn’t feel any obstruction from leaving the dimensional wall of the World of Gods. It was the same for re-entering the Myriad Heavens Universe as well.
But the group of vampires were different. They themselves were natives of the World of Gods, so it wasn't too hard to leave this place, but to enter the Myriad Heavens Universe, they would need to cross the dimensional wall as well.
Crossing the dimensional wall would require space-time crystals, which could be smuggled in if the scale was small. However, the Raymond clan had nearly 200 people that needed to enter, which was a bit of a problem.
In fact, Gu Nan and the others were now staying in the gap between the two worlds, staring at the crystalline dimensional wall somewhat speechlessly.
Gu Nan initially didn’t consider this. Although he was a top player, he wasn’t the kind of genius schemer who could predict everything. There would always be times when he overlooked matters that weren’t as important.
"Do you know where to get space-time crystals?" Gu Nan asked Wu Gui, who was next to him. Right now, Wu Gui was the only person nearby he could discuss this with.
Of course it was impossible for Sylvia to follow him all the way here. Little Zhong Die did follow him, but she might not even know what a space-time crystal was.

chapters.title: Chapter 368: Extreme Sword Heaven
chapters.content:
"It’ll be very difficult if it's on such a large scale." Wu Gui continued hesitantly, "Privately sending so many people into the Myriad Heavens Universe will be tantamount to openly provoking the Thirteen Heavens."
The prestige of the Thirteen Heavens couldn’t be sullied. It was one thing for Gu Nan to privately not give Lu Wen face—not many people knew about it anyways—but if he sent 200 people into the Myriad Heavens Universe, then he was afraid the Thirteen Heavens would send people to hunt him down.
If they didn’t do this, then it wouldn't be long before this ban became as useless as a piece of paper, and the Thirteen Heavens would no longer have any face to speak of.
Gu Nan fell silent. While it was true that he acted unbridled, he wasn't stupid.
Even when killing monsters, there was no reason for a Level 30 player to try to kill a Level 70 monster. The newbies who had nothing better to do and ran to the high-level monster area to hang out had only themselves to blame if a monster one-shotted them.
Gu Nan didn't know why the Thirteenth Heavens restricted travel between the two worlds, but since he was no match for them right now, he couldn’t resolve this using force.
He said after some thought, "If all else fails, I can only leave everyone in the gap first and transport a small group of people back every once in a while."
The Thirteen Heavens mostly turned a blind eye to illegal entries in smaller numbers, or else an organization like the Heaven-God Alliance wouldn’t be able to exist.
‘Wait, the Heaven-God Alliance!’
Gu Nan's eyes lit up when he suddenly remembered that he was now part of the Heaven-God Alliance. Why not try asking someone from the Heaven-God Alliance?
They were bound to have engaged in more human smuggling matters between the two worlds and may even have experience transporting a large number of people.
It just so happened that he needed to pay Extreme Sword Heaven a visit anyways after returning to the Myriad Heavens Universe—he needed to “check in” with Xue Ren, one of the leaders of the Heaven-God Alliance.
"Do you know anything about the situation inside Extreme Sword Heaven or Xue Ren?" Gu Nan turned to Wu Gui and asked.
Since it was one of the top-tier Heaven Level planes, the outside world certainly knew some information regarding the state of affairs and changes in Extreme Sword Heaven.
But this information wouldn’t possibly touch upon Star Ruler Xue Ren himself. Information concerning the major astral worlds’ Star Rulers was top secret and rarely made public.
At most, people knew his name was Xue Ren, he was a swordmaster, and a very powerful swordmaster at that. More detailed information would only be known by someone at Wu Gui’s level.
"Xue Ren… is very young, a few generations younger than me." Wu Gui frowned in contemplation.
She and Xue Ren could barely be considered contemporaries, but that was already her memories from nine thousand lifetimes ago, so it wasn't easy to recall.
"He's not a very typical swordsman. Although he also has a slight obsession with martial arts, he's more like a scholar."
"Scholar?" Gu Nan raised an eyebrow. The distinguished Star Ruler of Extreme Sword Heaven, one of the most powerful swordmasters in the Myriad Heavens Universe, didn’t seem like he’d have anything to do with the word “scholar.”
Wu Gui's expression was also a bit strange. "I don't understand his sword Dao, and neither did anyone else at that time. Other people's sword styles pay attention to the unity of essence, qi, and spirit, but he never cared about those."
"Then what did he care about?"
"I can't explain it very well either, but I still clearly remember the name of the first sword manual he wrote after achieving Star Ruler Realm— ‘The Wave Properties of the Sword’."
……
Nothing seemed to have changed much when Gu Nan re-entered the Myriad Heavens Universe.
It was still a calm situation with violent undercurrents. All the forces were moving towards their respective goals. Gu Nan's Divine Kingdom was naturally no exception.
White Mist was developing well in White Bones Realm. The brand-new White Mist had both a Star Ruler’s backing and its own impressive strength, so naturally it would be able to prosper anywhere.
Several highly promising mission experts even emerged from this side. If Gu Nan activated a new personal dungeon, they would certainly come in handy.
Everything was running smoothly inside the Divine Kingdom. The group of apostles continued to accumulate funds at a steady rate, while the management of the kingdom’s populace also underwent some changes.
After learning about the management system of White Bones Realm, Lan Si and Yan Xiaoxiao started trying to integrate what they learned into Gu Nan’s Divine Kingdom after a few rounds of trial and error.
Gu Nan was aware of this and didn’t intend to oppose it at all. Even in the game, the Divine Kingdom’s administrator would make a similar request after the Divine Kingdom reached a certain level.
All the player needs to do is to enjoy the benefits they brought about.
His Evil Value already satisfied the requirement for advancing to Tier 7. Now, he only needed to slowly accumulate points to successfully level up to Tier 7.
But the accumulation of points also had to be efficient. To only have a supply of points from one personal dungeon was naturally the most inefficient method, and to have an additional supply from the second Crescent Moon World dungeon was the second-most inefficient method.
The only way to further improve efficiency would be to launch a Divine Kingdom War. Evil Value along with points could be earned with this method, but the starting requirements were relatively high.
At the very least, he had to wait until the Divine Servants Institute was leveled up once or even after a few more of those structures were built to reach the best opportunity to launch a Divine Kingdom War.
‘Crescent Moon World’s difficulty level isn’t low. If we can maximize its production capacity, then we’ll be able to afford some small-scale wars.’ Gu Nan calculated in his mind, trying to figure out the most efficient level-up route.
He quickly arrived at the decision to pay Extreme Sword Heaven a visit first and see if there was a way to bring all the vampires over at once.
If that couldn't be done, then he at least wanted to bring over that group of Legend Rank vampires first so that they could start raiding the personal dungeons as soon as possible.
……
Extreme Sword Heaven.
As a large plane that could be ranked firmly within the top twenty planes in the Myriad Heavens Universe, one could imagine how prosperous Extreme Sword Heaven was.
What was a little out of Gu Nan’s expectations was that the buildings in this plane famous for its swordsmanship didn’t actually have an ancient martial arts style. Instead, it looked like a modern city.
A modern city with the sword Dao as the highest pursuit.
"Quite interesting," Gu Nan gave such an evaluation.
"Many people say that!" A young girl walking in front of Gu Nan smiled while pursing her lips.
Gu Nan was on his way to visit Xue Ren, and this young girl was his temporary guide.
Like all large planes, Extreme Sword Heaven monitored every powerful visitor above Void Cutter Realm rather strictly.
Not only would they try to sound out these visitors’ true intentions, but they also wouldn’t let them out of sight easily.
After all, the destructive power of Void Cutters was too great for astral worlds that took the route of peaceful governance.
"We’re here, My Lord." The young girl led Gu Nan to a pavilion facing the sea. "This is Lord Hongye’s residence."
Gu Nan nodded and stepped forward wordlessly.
It’s true that he was here to pay a visit to Xue Ren, but of course the grand Star Ruler of Extreme Sword Heaven wasn’t someone he could meet so easily.
For a visitor like Gu Nan, Extreme Sword Heaven handled it by finding a spokesperson to meet the visitor first, verify the identity and goal of the visitor, and then decide which ones could meet Xue Ren.
The person Gu Nan was going to meet now was Qu Hongye, who was considered Xue Ren's Martial Niece based on seniority and was responsible for receiving a portion of the visitors like Gu Nan.
There were already four or five cultivators sitting inside the seaside pavilion when Gu Nan entered. There were both men and women, and even a young boy with a buzz cut.
Seeing Gu Nan enter, a young man immediately went up to him with a standard smile on his face. "Lord Hongye is currently taking an afternoon nap. Please wait here for a moment."
His tone was very polite, but his expression was extremely calm, clearly having received many guests like Gu Nan and not really taking this seriously.
"She's upstairs?" Gu Nan raised a brow.
The young man stared blankly, then realized the other party’s intentions. This wasn’t the first time he’d seen such a guest either, so he sneered, "Lord Hongye’s whereabouts is not something we can know."
Although he said “we,” his gaze landed straight on Gu Nan. It was obvious that he actually meant "you guys."
To his surprise, the other party’s face didn’t turn angry. Gu Nan just nodded, then gently waved his hand.
The shadows began to spread; the pavilion began to shatter.

chapters.title: Chapter 369: Qu Hongye
chapters.content:
Inside the small seaside pavilion, shadows emerged from under Gu Nan’s feet. Any person or object touched by the shadows was instantly ground into powder.
The youth in front of Gu Nan bore the brunt of the attack and was swept under the shadows. His entire person seemed to shatter inch by inch like glass, ultimately leaving no trace behind.
What also disappeared along with the youth were the floor under everyone’s feet and the surrounding walls, sofas, coffee tables, and other objects.
Fortunately, the shadows didn’t spread so quickly that people couldn’t react in time. The other four or five guests scrambled to get up and retreated backwards at lightning speed.
These guests weren’t normal people either. Almost every single one of them had Void Cutter Realm strength. One person even tried to block the shadows with their own law.
Unfortunately, the person’s law was already crushed to pieces by the shadows before it even had time to leave their body.
This terrifying result scared that guest so much that they didn’t dare linger any longer and fled in the blink of an eye, even abandoning any thought of visiting Xue Ren.
Not every visitor necessarily wanted to meet Xue Ren. Most of them just came to pay their respects to the Sword Sect’s higher-ups, which wasn’t anything urgent.
On the other hand, they were also eager to see what would happen to Gu Nan, the guy who dared to cause trouble in Extreme Sword Heaven.
Completely engulfed in Gu Nan's shadows, most of this pavilion was corroded in the blink of an eye. A few beams on the second floor were also damaged, causing the second floor to collapse.
Miss Qu Hongye, who was supposedly taking a nap, naturally couldn’t continue sleeping any longer.
"You dared to make trouble in my Extreme Sword Heaven. You must be tired of living!" A delicate shout came from above Gu Nan's head, and along with it was a flash of sword light headed straight for him.
Qu Hongye's words carried a martial arts flavor that stood in stark contrast with this obviously modern city, which made Gu Nan feel a little strange.
The first thought he had was: ‘The NPC’s lines are so out of sync with the setting. The game designer for this is going to get his pay docked!’
Then he shook his head again, tossing aside all irrelevant thoughts to observe the sword beam.
Based on the information Wu Gui provided, Xue Ren would probably resemble a physicist disguised as a swordsman, so Qu Hongye, his Martial Niece, should also share this characteristic.
Scientific cultivation didn’t exist in his previous life’s game, so Gu Nan was quite interested in it.
Qu Hongye's sword beam was indeed very strange. It was clearly a direct stab, but it appeared to be a sword cloud in Gu Nan's perception.
There was no mistake. It felt as if her sword scattered and turned into a cloud of fog, all surging towards the enemy.
"So this is the wave properties of the sword?" Gu Nan couldn't help revealing a faint smile.
It looked like Extreme Sword Heaven’s so-called "wave properties" were at least on the level of quantum theory, which maintained that all matter has intrinsic wave properties. The attacks weren’t as basic as the wave crests and troughs of middle school physics.
The next moment, Gu Nan grabbed the sword beam with his hand.
Qu Hongye originally looked very confident, but her smile suddenly froze on her face.
Her wave sword already reached minor attainment, and her own strength was also Void Cutter Realm. Even top-tier Void Cutters would still have to block this carefully, but… ‘This person actually grabbed it with his bare hand?’
If you asked a swordmaster what kind of opponent was the most annoying, then enemies with great speed, strength, or cultivation realm ranked further down. The answer was an opponent whose defense they couldn’t break through.
Gu Nan belonged to this category.
Let alone Qu Hongye, even many enemies in the same realm as Gu Nan found it hard to break through his defense. The Evil God physique of an Evil God who took the pure combat route was too strong.
Gu Nan studied the longsword in his hand but found it to be no different from a normal sword. Of course a sword that was forcibly held could no longer oscillate.
After studying it for a while longer and confirming that he really couldn’t see anything special, Gu Nan lost interest in further observations.
Be it his past or present life, Gu Nan wasn’t someone suited to be the top student. He only knew how to play games.
"I'm looking for Xue Ren," Gu Nan slowly walked up to Qu Hongye and said flatly.
After taking a good look, one would find that Qu Hongye's appearance was very interesting. A small handful of hair on her forehead was dyed red, and her right ear had ear piercings. She looked like a female delinquent.
But she was also wearing an incomparably standard Daoist robe and had a wooden scabbard slung over her back. Her attire and aura were perfectly mismatched.
The Daoist-robed delinquent girl didn’t look scared at all. Rather, she stared at him with an interested look and asked, “Why are you looking for my Martial Uncle?"
Information about the Heaven-God Alliance shouldn’t be revealed to outsiders, and Gu Nan was also too lazy to make up a reason, so he bluntly replied, “Can’t say.”
Qu Hongye’s expression suddenly darkened. She thought about it and asked a new question, "Then what’s your name? Even if I take you to meet Martial Uncle, I still need to give him a name…"
"Just tell me where he is. I’ll find him myself," Gu Nan refused blandly.
He found the entire process of informing someone to inform someone else too troublesome. Even meetings between Star Rulers seldom had use for messengers—because as long as the visiting Star Ruler knew the location, their arrival would quickly alert the local Star Ruler.
