The wrath of the Ruler of Light and Justice wasn’t so easy to withstand, not even if he was hiding in the Myriad Heavens.
But the probability of him being discovered would be much smaller if he merely trapped Sylvia here for a few years. After all, for gods, that was just the blink of an eye.
……
The current Sylvia was very regretful, but also very calm.
As a god who survived for tens of thousands of years, it wasn't like she hadn't experienced dangerous situations before, so she knew that the more dangerous the situation, the more she needed to calm down.
It was as if she was sealed inside boundless shadows, her body unable to move and her mouth unable to speak, but she could still hear the movements of the outside world.
She heard the sound of someone walking into the temple and reporting to Gu Nan, and the content was about the upcoming Divine Kingdom War.
"Divine Kingdom…" At this point, Sylvia was finally able to confirm that Gu Nan was indeed from the World of Gods, or else his subordinates wouldn’t be referring to this place as a Divine Kingdom.
But something about this also didn’t make sense. Since Gu Nan had established a Divine Kingdom instead of an astral world, why didn't he require the power of faith?
‘Could it be that after he reincarnated into the Myriad Heavens, what he re-established was also an astral world and not a Divine Kingdom?’
‘And why did he make a special trip to the World of Gods to kill both Luke and Cliff?’
Although Sylvia couldn’t move, her thoughts were still churning, one question after another surfacing in her mind.
As the god most familiar with Gu Nan, a terrifying thought appeared in Sylvia's mind when she connected all the dots.
It was an ancient legend that already existed long before even the first Great War, and if it hadn't been for her brother offhandedly mentioning it, perhaps Sylvia wouldn't have even known there was such a thing.
But now that she thought about it, Gu Nan seemed to bear an uncanny resemblance to the existence described in that legend.
Sylvia, who knew she had discovered a terrifying secret, suddenly felt a sense of urgency.
"I have to get out of here!"

chapters.title: Chapter 467: Sylvia, Savior Of The World?
chapters.content:
Even in today’s World of Gods, not many people knew about the legend of the Evil God.
In fact, similar legends weren’t uncommon during the ancient era of the World of Gods. All sorts of creatures that were enemies of the gods and even all humanity—with a strong penchant for self-destruction—were said to exist.
But how many people had actually seen such an existence with their own eyes? The answer was zero.
In fact, these legends didn’t really seem realistic. Be it the World of Gods or the Myriad Heavens, the path of development for gods and Star Rulers was essentially the same.
They strengthened themselves by developing their own planes, eventually reaching Unified Dao, merging themselves with the laws of the great world, and from then on, they would exist alongside the world for all eternity.
Since this was the case, how could there be beings in this world who made it their mission to kill gods? What was the meaning of their existence? What benefit would killing gods give them?
There was always a profit motive incentivizing living beings’ actions, and no one had ever heard of someone who benefitted by killing other gods.
But Gu Nan's appearance made Sylvia realize that such a person might actually exist.
Sylvia personally witnessed Gu Nan seeking out the Mirror God in an unheard-of place and then killing him, and this time, he even made a special trip to kill Luke and Cliff.
And it seemed that his power grew every time he killed a god…
As she replayed past scenes in her head, the conjecture in Sylvia's heart grew firmer—Gu Nan was definitely some sort of ancient evil creature that came to the Myriad Heavens for some inexplicable reason and took on a human form.
Not even Sylvia had ever seen such a peculiar existence before, and she suddenly felt as if her heart was gripped by something, feeling like she was duty-bound to save the world.
She was indeed trying to save the world, because those kinds of legendary evil creatures were all bent on destroying the world!
"Escape, I must find a way to escape." Sylvia forced herself to calm down. Despite the fact that most of her senses were sealed, the voices from outside were still coming through.
There was no break in the reports she heard. It seemed that many individuals had already entered and left, and their conversations with Gu Nan were all centered around an upcoming Divine Kingdom War.
The term Divine Kingdom War was one that Sylvia hadn't heard in a long time. This was because most gods in the World of Gods would never casually start a war; they preferred to fight battles as individuals.
This was unlike the Star Rulers of the Myriad Heavens. As long as they defeated other Star Rulers, they could plunder resources from other people’s territories, strengthen their reputation, and attract more powerful subordinates.
If the gods of the World of Gods waged wars, it was basically just for the sake of "doctrine", and there would hardly be any real benefits—believers couldn’t be plundered; they could only be raised.
Sylvia endured the discomfort of not being able to sense the outside world and listened carefully to Gu Nan's conversation with his subordinates, but the more she heard, the more alarmed she became.
Unlike the wars she was familiar with, Gu Nan didn’t seem to care about resources or territory and wanted to send his army out purely to kill people.
All his arrangements were to kill people more efficiently. His targets ranged from mortals to all cultivators weaker than gods, with no exceptions.
Sylvia secretly noted down this detail, then tried to empty her thoughts as much as possible, quietly waiting for a chance to escape.
After a while, she sensed that the outside had been silent for a long time, and Gu Nan seemed to have left long ago.
So this Goddess of Shadows began to cautiously test the waters, mobilizing the divine power in her body bit by bit, seemingly breaking through the shackles from outside.
Unfortunately, the same power of shadows was outside, and her divine power was completely assimilated the moment it left her body, in turn making her restraints even stronger.
"Damn it!"
Sylvia had never hated shadows so much. If not for the fact that the other party also controlled shadows, it would’ve been impossible for anyone else to imprison her like this.
As the goddess who controlled shadows, she was confident in breaking free from her bonds in any situation, as shadows themselves couldn’t be bound—unless the other party also used shadows to bind her.
In the past, Sylvia might have given up hope at this point, praying with all her heart that her brother would quickly realize she was missing and find her.
But now that she believed she was carrying the hopes of the entire world, she was driven by the heavy sense of duty and actually didn’t have the slightest intention of giving up.
"Must… get out!"
The Shadow Goddess launched herself viciously, giving up on the idea of escaping using the power of shadows, and actually started to smash her body against the law of shadows.
Apart from monsters like Gu Nan, the divine bodies of normal gods couldn't be considered powerful, but they weren't weak either. The essence of a god's divine body was stronger than laws, but it was very hard to heal injuries to their physical bodies, so few gods would ever fight with it.
But at this moment, Sylvia couldn't care less.
The power of shadows invaded from the surface of her body, causing Sylvia to feel vague stabs of pain, but she forced herself to endure it and instead became somewhat excited inside.
This was because she could sense the power of the laws binding her outside being worn down slightly as well.
Even if it was just a very tiny bit, these laws that had left Gu Nan would not be replenished. As long as she kept on doing this, sooner or later, she would be able to free herself.
"Hang in there!" Sylvia encouraged herself.
She began to try again and again, pausing for a short rest when her divine body was damaged too seriously, and soon began the repetitive work of "trying to puncture stone with drops of water" once again.
It was only when she heard the sound of footsteps that she hastily stopped moving, fearing that Gu Nan would notice her actions.
Her caution was completely necessary, as Gu Nan's voice soon traveled over.
"Target: Daoist Sect Realm. Set off."
……
Daoist Monarch Wu Tian of Daoist Sect Realm had been tormented miserably by Gu Nan recently.
The thought of Gu Nan specifically targeting the living beings in Daoist Sect Realm never occurred to him; he just believed the invasion was due to the past grudge between them, and Gu Nan came back to seek revenge now that he ascended to a Realm Level Star Ruler.
But he couldn’t even do anything about Gu Nan back in the day, so of course he could only endure the current disaster. Turning the tables and going to Gu Nan's house to wreak havoc was something he could never do.
Who was he kidding? Even Fang Chaoyun suffered a loss in Gu Nan's lair, and now the Star Rulers who had a grudge against Gu Nan all regarded it as a tiger’s den.
Therefore, when a group of divine servants descended from Gu Nan’s Divine Kingdom and landed directly on various parts of Daoist Sect Realm, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian was still in a trance and hadn't regained his senses.
‘Didn’t you just want to vent some anger? How did it turn into an all-out war?’
"The… Lady Sylvia in the Divine Kingdom, do you need me to dispose of her?" In the Divine Kingdom, Yan Xiaoxiao projected a figure next to Gu Nan and asked.
Sylvia probably never imagined that everything she did in the shadows was actually all under Yan Xiaoxiao's watchful eye.
"No need." Gu Nan waved his hand. "If she plans to escape like this, even the monkey would’ve freed himself from Five Elements Mountain before then
[1]
."
T/N:
[1]
Reference to
Journey to the West
, where it took Sun Wukong 500 years to escape the mountain

chapters.title: Chapter 468: Wu Tian Returns To The Sect
chapters.content:
Daoist Sect Realm was finished.
The observers who witnessed Gu Nan's grand army descending knew that Daoist Sect Realm most likely wouldn’t be able to put up much resistance any longer.
Even though Gu Nan's army suffered staggering losses after being ambushed by ten Star Rulers last time and its overall strength still hadn’t recovered, the enemy still couldn’t resist the completion of the player army.
The addition of two fresh troops—Xie Yun and Liang Ruxin—meant the Divine Kingdom wasn’t inferior to any Realm Level plane at all in terms of high-end combat power.
The remaining seven members of the player army were also growing rapidly, with An Tiansheng being the most prominent among them.
This teenager who’d taken the "Bandit" route had a growth curve not much worse than Xie Yun's, and because of the nature of his route, he would enjoy even more flexibility in the future.
Although Pay to Win Experts were indeed incredibly strong at the start, by the time they reached Tier 6 or 7, the amount of gold needed for leveling up would reach a despair-inducing level.
But the Bandit route had no such problems; at worst, he would just steal objects of a higher rank as he leveled up.
In any case, from the Star Rulers to the Void Cutter combat power to the ordinary armies below, Daoist Sect Realm was completely outclassed, with almost no hope of turning the tide.
And due to Gu Nan's earlier actions, none of the Star Rulers, including Fang Chaoyun, dared to come to Wu Tian’s aid anymore.
This was also the case with Daoist Monarch Wu Tian’s friends—whoever helped right now would be the next to suffer.
Gu Nan himself was like a bugged existence. He could casually run into other people's houses to cause trouble, but others didn't dare to throw their lives away by running over to his.
Of course, it wasn't like there were no headstrong people at all. There were always one or two righteous people in this world.
"Old friend Wu Tian, I've come to help you!"
With a loud shout, a burly man holding a double bladed axe appeared as he descended to Daoist Sect Realm.
Daoist Monarch Wu Tian was like someone who’d been in a long drought, so he was extremely touched to receive a helping hand at a time like this.
However, he also knew that this burly man with the double edged axe was, in essence, merely a weak Star Ruler who just obtained an astral world and could never be Gu Nan's match.
Instead of letting him run to his death here, it would be better for him to deal with Gu Nan's army. Having a Star Ruler intervene would undoubtedly buy Wu Tian a lot of time.
Thinking of this, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian hurriedly shouted, "Don't come here, hurry to—"
Bang!
Though he spoke up quickly, Gu Nan reacted even faster. He slammed his fist out without thinking, punching the burly man in the back of his head, and his body slowly collapsed.
"You evil wretch!" Daoist Monarch Wu Tian couldn't help letting out an enraged roar, but Gu Nan turned around and swung another punch at him, knocking down his temper.
Strictly speaking, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian shouldn’t be any weaker than a normal Tier 10 powerhouse when inside Daoist Sect Realm.
The astral world could only strengthen his laws. Even so, he was still unable to deal a fatal blow to Gu Nan, so the scene fell into a stalemate.
As long as the power of his astral world was used up, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian’s defeat would be imminent, and besides, Gu Nan's goal in this battle wasn’t to kill Wu Tian in the first place.
With no external Star Rulers intervening, Daoist Sect Realm's native cultivators were losing ground, and there was absolutely no one who could withstand Gu Nan's army.
Especially Xie Yun, Lan Si, and the others—all of them were the strongest people under Star Ruler Realm, and there was hardly a single enemy who could be their match.
The divine servant army massacred enemies at an extremely swift speed, and in just over a day's time, the entire Daoist Sect Realm had been wiped clean. Even now, Gu Nan and Wu Tian had still yet to decide victory or defeat.
In fact, there was absolutely no need to decide the winner and loser. If Wu Tian was unable to kill Gu Nan in the beginning, then he was already doomed to lose.
And right now, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian was indeed very spent. His attacks seemed mechanical, no longer containing the spirit he seemed to have a day ago.
Anyone who’d been stalled in battle by Gu Nan for a day and a night and had to watch their own astral world being destroyed in the meantime would probably end up like this.
This was the complete destruction of one’s mental state.
What was even more frightening was that Gu Nan didn't seem to have changed at all, as if the previous battle hadn't caused any wear and tear at all.
With ten thousand years of hard work destroyed in a day, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian slipped up and was finally punched squarely in the stomach by Gu Nan, and his entire body immediately flew out.
Of course Gu Nan wouldn’t be polite to him. Since his opponent wasn’t in a good condition, Gu Nan naturally had to give him a thorough thrashing.
However, at this time, a flash of teal light hovered in front of Gu Nan, slowly transforming into human form.
This person was a young man with delicate features and a black Daoist robe, quite similar to the original Daoist Heir Qin Ning.
"Disciple Fang Keming under Void Grotto Heaven’s Radiant Jade Cave Sect Leader greets Senior Gu Nan."
The youth who called himself Fang Keming made his attitude very humble, addressing Gu Nan as “senior” as soon as he appeared.
Contrary to expectations, Gu Nan stopped his attacks in time. The youth in front of him was only around Tier 5, but the person he represented had to be given face.
Void Grotto Heaven’s Daoist Heir Fang Keming, theclosed door disciple
[1]
of Daoist Venerable Yu Lian. He cultivated for less than a hundred years, yet he’d already stepped into Star Ruler Realm.He far surpassed Qin Ning in terms of both talent and status.
Strictly speaking, it really wasn't a problem for him to call Gu Nan his senior—this was a rare occasion where Gu Nan ran into a cultivator younger than himself.
"Yu Lian sent you?" Gu Nan didn't have much intention of chatting with his junior and asked directly.
Fang Keming bowed and saluted. "The Sect Leader said that Daoist Sect Realm is of the same origin as my Void Grotto Heaven, so she asks Senior to please be merciful."
"Sure," Gu Nan seemed to be particularly amenable this time and agreed without any hesitation at all. "I’ll return Wu Tian to you, and my people will withdraw today."
Daoist Sect Realm had gone through a round of massacre, and all the points that could be harvested had pretty much been collected, so it wasn't like there was any benefit to killing Wu Tian.
Fang Keming hurriedly revealed a look of gratitude, shielding Daoist Monarch Wu Tian behind him as he once again saluted and thanked him.
As Daoist Monarch Wu Tian followed behind Fang Keming, he was barely able to recover some of his spirit. At the very least, he was a grand Star Ruler who had weathered great storms.
Although the forces of Daoist Sect Realm had been thoroughly purged, their foundation hadn't been destroyed—Gu Nan hadn't laid his hands on the origin.
Because of this, Daoist Monarch Wu Tian believed that the other party might have done this just to vent some anger and didn’t necessarily want to kill him… It’s just that this venting was a bit extreme.
Wu Tian took a deep breath and took one last look at his tattered Daoist Sect Realm, then helplessly followed Fang Keming to Void Grotto Heaven.
"He's going to rejoin Void Grotto Heaven, congratulations!" Gu Nan revealed a smile and chuckled lightly.
If Daoist Sect Realm wanted to rebuild, it would never happen overnight, and Wu Tian's willingness to follow Fang Keming back represented an attitude in and of itself.
After holding on so stubbornly for so many years, this loser from back then was finally going to bow down to Void Grotto Heaven.
Red Tail was the chief commander of the Divine Kingdom War and finally reached Gu Nan's side at this time. "Then it’ll be hard for us to invade this place again… My Lord, who are we going to fight next?"
Gu Nan glanced at her and laughed involuntarily. "How did you become so belligerent as well?"
Without waiting for Red Tail to respond, he shook his head again. "We’re going to do something big next time."
T/N:
[1]
Closed door disciple
: A master’s final disciple

chapters.title: Chapter 469: Weak Gods Hunting Manual
chapters.content:
After the battle in Daoist Sect Realm ended, Gu Nan immediately checked the losses and gains, and the results somewhat exceeded his expectations.
Perhaps because Gu Nan's earlier actions had indeed frightened many of the Star Rulers, not many dared to intervene, even until the end.
This also resulted in very little casualties to the divine servants, and there was even a 0% casualty rate amongst the apostles, with only a handful of them suffering some injuries.
However, the gains this time were far greater than any other time in the past. Even compared to the earlier attack on Star Realm, this battle still yielded far more points.
After all, Star Realm was merely the weakest of the Realm Level planes, and because of the vastness of its geography and the meddling of other Star Rulers, the war hadn’t been fully successful, so the amount of points gained naturally couldn’t be maximized.
After collecting his thoughts, Gu Nan started considering his next move.
Judging from the current situation, choosing the "reaching heaven in one fell swoop" method by directly advancing to Tier 10 was the more reliable option.
After making such a mess in the World of Gods, it would be inappropriate for him to appear in public again, not unless he was prepared to be interrogated and exposed in front of people.
In that case, rather than making two trips to the World of Gods when advancing to Tier 9 and Tier 10, it would be better to do it all at once.
In terms of points, Gu Nan did some rough calculations. If he followed the simplest route of operating the Divine Kingdom, choosing all structures with the aim of leveling himself up, Tier 10 was actually close at hand.
At most, he would get enough points after slaughtering one more plane with half the population of Daoist Sect Realm.
There were often players who became addicted to the later stages of the Divine Kingdom playstyle after the First Round and couldn't extricate themselves, because there were simply too many structures to choose from from Tier 8 onwards.
They each had their own peculiar uses, and from the perspectives of both appearance and functionality, these structures were all worth building.
Some players even turned their Divine Kingdoms into impenetrable fortresses, so that even a greater god-level powerhouse couldn't easily break in.
For the game's developers, the large variety of structures undoubtedly satisfied the portion of players who loved to build bases while also extending the game's lifespan.
But for a top player like Gu Nan who pursued efficiency, a large number of structures would be of little use; instead, picking out the cheapest structures to meet the upgrade criteria was top priority.
"But even so… the Myriad Heavens is still really efficient in terms of points!" Even Gu Nan couldn't help sighing with emotion.
In the game’s terms, Daoist Sect Realm was only a Tier 8 Divine Kingdom, yet the amount of points that could be harvested surpassed even that of a Tier 9 Divine Kingdom.
In the end, it all came down to the source of points, which mainly came from fanatical worshippers in the World of Gods, so the harvesting—be it efficiency or total amount—was far inferior to directly hunting powerful people in the Myriad Heavens.
The shortfall in terms of points wasn't too large, and it could even be said that because of the characteristics of the Myriad Heavens, he could gather enough without too much difficulty, but there was no possibility of such a loophole when it came to Evil Value.
One needed to kill at least three Tier 10 gods to advance to Tier 10. Of course, the player could also choose to make up for the number with lower level gods, but the number needed would be several times greater.
"It seems like this is the only way." Gu Nan sat calmly inside the Evil God Temple, his gaze falling to the horizon.
……
"What is… this?" Red Tail was slightly surprised when she saw the stack of documents placed in front of her.
The documents detailed a method of cultivating underlings—the Godhead Cultivation Method.
To describe it in the simplest of terms, by using a Godhead as the raw material and a mortal with excellent talent as the culture medium, one could easily cultivate a subordinate who was at least Void Cutter Realm.
Red Tail was perfectly aware that this was by no means false information, as an example was laid out in front of her—Lan Si had been cultivated using a similar method.
More importantly, there was only one Lan Si, but with this cultivation method given by Gu Nan, the Godhead could be utilized over and over again.
Once the subordinate was cultivated to the point of satisfaction, the Godhead could be directly removed. Unlike Lan Si, who became Gu Nan's apostle, this cultivation method merely utilized the sublime laws contained within the Godhead.
Of course, the more the Godhead was used, the less laws would remain within. But in this state where the target semi-fused with the Godhead, it still wasn’t much of a problem to use the Godhead like this ten or so times.
"I know that the birth of a Void Cutter is, in a sense, harder than making a Legend Rank powerhouse." Gu Nan said with a smile, "The level-up route over there is smoother, and they have no need to comprehend the law of space."
"That's why many Star Rulers—especially the weaker ones—have a high demand for Void Cutters."
To a large extent, the number of Void Cutters in an astral world represented the Star Ruler’s overall power, but unfortunately, Void Cutters couldn't be cultivated just because they wanted to and demanded a high level of enlightenment and talent from mortal candidates.
But now, Gu Nan had placed a cultivation plan with an extremely high success rate in front of Red Tail.
Having followed Gu Nan for many years, Red Tail was familiar with his style, so she already realized what Gu Nan was trying to do as soon as she saw this information.
"Are you planning to… publicize this information?"
"Yes." Gu Nan nodded and said with a light smile, "And it can't be openly publicized; it has to be secretly spread around."
He wanted the information to be secretly circulated in the circle of weaker Star Rulers. It wasn’t as if Red Tail hadn't done similar things before, so it wasn’t very hard, and she quickly nodded.
It’s just that her current knowledge was also far superior to the past, so she could see where the real difficulty lay for this plan.
"But the difficulty of obtaining a Godhead is quite high, isn’t it?" Red Tail asked carefully.
Quite many Star Rulers actually knew the situation of the World of Gods, but the two sides had always lived together in harmony. To put it bluntly, it was because there was no conflict of interest. Although Godheads were great, the benefits weren’t really proportional to the effort expended to get them.
Gu Nan smiled and took out another piece of information from the drawer. "This one, on the other hand, can be publicized."
Red Tail hurriedly accepted the document, and when she saw the title alone, she couldn't take her eyes off it anymore.
Clearly written on it were the words: Weak Gods Hunting Manual.
……
Geng Chengyun was a Star Ruler who just broke through not long ago and hadn’t had the chance to take control of an astral world yet.
He did find a suitable target in the Inner World, but because of his own lack of strength, he wasn’t in a hurry to try and instead chose to stabilize his foundation first.
On this day, he was planning to go out for a relaxing stroll after just finishing a round of secluded cultivation when he received a letter from an old friend.
"Extremely urgent, come to Nine Islands World as soon as possible." The sender of the letter was none other than Geng Chengyun's old friend, Nine Islands World’s Star Ruler Mai Cheng.
Geng Chengyun, who was familiar with his old friend's style, felt slightly alarmed. He knew Mai Cheng would never send him such a letter if there wasn’t a genuine emergency, so he hurriedly rushed to Nine Islands World.
Mai Cheng became a Star Ruler about two thousand years ahead of him, so they could barely be considered as the same generation. In the past, Mai Cheng often looked after him.
When Mai Cheng sent out the "extremely urgent" letter, Geng Chengyun had already decided that he would help his old friend in any way he could.
Only when he arrived at Nine Islands World did he realize that the situation wasn’t what he expected.
"Brother Geng is here? Come quickly, come quickly, we were all waiting for you!" As soon as Mai Cheng sensed Geng Chengyun's appearance, he hurriedly guided him down and said excitedly.
Only then did Geng Chengyun realize with surprise that four Star Rulers were already waiting for him inside the tiny Nine Islands World.
Besides Mai Cheng himself, there were two more that he recognized, both of whom were weak Star Rulers at a similar level as himself and the others.
"Brother Mai, what are you guys…?"
Mai Cheng slapped Geng Chengyun's shoulder and laughed. "Brother, our chance has come!"

chapters.title: Chapter 470: Pandora's Box
chapters.content:
Geng Chengyun glanced at Mai Cheng with a baffled expression, incomprehension clear on his face.
The people next to him couldn't help revealing friendly smiles when they saw this. One of the people acquainted with Geng Chengyun asked with a smile, "Old Geng, did you just come out of secluded cultivation? You never even heard about such a major event?"
Geng Chengyun nodded. "I won't hide it from Daoist Friend Xie… This humble one has indeed just left secluded cultivation."
"Then it's no wonder!" A look of realization appeared on Mai Cheng’s face, and he handed a piece of document to Geng Chengyun. "Brother, take a look at this first."
Geng Chengyun took it and realized that a line of large words were written on the first page: Weak Gods Hunting Manual.
Geng Chengyun was naturally aware of the World of Gods and the existence of gods, so he was taken aback on the spot as soon as he saw this name.
Gods were existences on the same level as Star Rulers, yet someone actually dared to talk about hunting gods?
Disdain flickered in his eyes. Geng Chengyun didn’t want to humor this nonsense, but considering that it was information given to him by Mai Cheng, he still patiently flipped open the file.
On the title page, Geng Chengyun saw this sentence: “All methods in this manual are only for weak gods below Tier 7. Remember to choose the correct hunting target when using them.”
‘Yeah right, as if this whole thing isn’t just a huge prank.’ Geng Chengyun secretly bristled, but was then shaken by the long table of contents on the next page.
“Definition of Weak Gods, Common Locations Where Weak Gods Reside, How to Lure Weak Gods Out, Common Areas Weak Gods Frequent…”
Geng Chengyun saw something even more frightening at the end of the manual.
“Example Demonstration: Detailed Steps for Capturing and Killing a Tier 6 God—God of Smoke and Dust Norfetti.”
Geng Chengyun felt his heartbeat speed up as he quickly flipped to the very end, and sure enough, he saw extremely detailed steps written there, telling the reader how to capture and kill Norfetti.
This was a god who had reached Tier 6 and already possessed a Divine Kingdom!
He quickly glanced up at Mai Cheng. "This Norfetti…"
"Dead," Mai Cheng answered lightly. "The method of death was exactly the same as stated in the manual, and the Godhead was also gouged out."
Geng Chengyun only felt a "boom" in his head, as if something had shattered in his heart. He knew that it was the high and mighty status unique to Star Rulers.
Mai Cheng couldn't help chuckling when he saw this. "Don't be nervous. This manual only targets gods—it has no effect on us."
As Mai Cheng and the others recounted what happened, Geng Chengyun soon realized what kind of major event had transpired in the Myriad Heavens during his seclusion.
First, a strange piece of information regarding the use of Godheads to cultivate Void Cutters began to circulate amongst the Star Rulers.
At that time, not many people took it seriously. After all, Godheads weren’t cabbages, and the difficulty of obtaining one might even be higher than cultivating a Void Cutter from scratch, so such information was completely useless.
But then this hunting manual appeared out of nowhere, and it wasn’t even circulated secretly but rather released openly for all Star Rulers and even Void Cutters to read.
"To think such a method exists…" Geng Chengyun muttered under his breath as he finished reading the Godhead Cultivation Method.
Even though he hadn't reached the stage of running an astral world yet, the lack of Void Cutters under his command was a situation every Star Ruler would face. If one could have a Void Cutter underling, it would undoubtedly save a great deal of energy.
Star Rulers like Mai Cheng would have an even greater need for Void Cutters’ assistance and was just short of waving a flag and recruiting Void Cutters from all sides into their own astral worlds.
Moreover, Void Cutters they personally raised would obviously be more dependable than outsiders… Almost without much thought, Geng Chengyun understood the value of these two pieces of information.
His gaze also began to burn with enthusiasm as he looked around him.
According to the manual, the most optimal party for hunting gods was a team of five people. This number could guarantee a fairly high success rate without the loot being poorly distributed due to too many people, making it the most cost-effective configuration.
It occurred to Geng Chengyun that even if the five of them only ended up getting one Godhead, they could still take turns using it…
As long as they found a small plane where time flowed extremely fast, it wouldn't take long at all to cultivate a Void Cutter, and they’d soon be able to squeeze all the value out of a single Godhead.
Seeing Geng Chengyun's expression change, Mai Cheng didn't need to ask much to understand the other party's attitude.
He then spoke again, "There's no time to lose. If Brother Geng is interested in participating in this matter, why don't we set off immediately?"
"Depart immediately? I still want to go back and prepare a little…" Geng Chengyun froze for a second, not expecting Mai Cheng to be in such a hurry.
He originally came out to relax and hadn't prepared too many items suitable for combat.
Daoist Friend Xie next to him said, "Old Geng, you're muddleheaded! This hunting manual is public, so it won't be long before the gods learn about it. How can we have time to wait any longer?"
Geng Chengyun suddenly realized that he’d been so shocked by this series of discoveries that he didn't even consider this. He hurriedly said, "There’s no time to lose. Let’s hurry up and get going!"
This truly was an extremely urgent matter.
……
Motivating people through righteousness would only last for a while, while motivating people through benefits could last for a long time.
Gu Nan didn’t even do anything besides making two pieces of information public and semi-public respectively, and the entire Myriad Heavens completely exploded, with the vast majority of Star Rulers mobilizing.
How could the Star Rulers not be enthusiastic? After all, a single Godhead represented at least ten Void Cutters—and the kind where they could select the candidates themselves. Not even Star Rulers had ever seen such a good thing before.
Those weak Star Rulers who were just starting to develop their astral worlds were definitely grateful from the bottom of their hearts to the person who publicized the information. This really was a timely rain.
As a result, the number of Void Cutters in the entire Myriad Heavens reached its highest peak ever, and after just over half a month, practically every Star Ruler had a Void Cutter attendant in their hands.
The status of independent Void Cutters took a steep dive as a result, and it could be said that because of Gu Nan's actions, the problem of class solidification in the Myriad Heavens worsened severalfold.
Equally unlucky were the weaker gods in the World of Gods. The neutral Void Cutters lost some status at worst, but what these gods lost were their lives.
The sudden death of a large number of gods finally drew the attention of the higher-ups of the World of Gods, and the twelve greater gods sat down together in an unprecedented manner, trying to get to the bottom of the matter—actually, it was thirteen now, since there was an extra Rolensia.
But when the results came out, they could only look at each other speechlessly.
There was no greater god who didn’t know about the Myriad Heavens, so they were well aware of this: the conflict between the two sides had become irreconcilable as soon as Godheads were discovered to greatly benefit Star Rulers’ astral world development.
"Negotiate with that side and have their Unified Dao powers place a ban on Star Rulers coming over here illegally?" The God of Time Valen suggested after some thought.
"It's useless." The Goddess of Darkness Daisy sighed softly. "Even if there is a ban, there will never be a lack of people willing to take risks out of desperation."
The Beast God pressed his greatsword onto the table and looked around. "Everyone, I think it's better to prepare for war."
No one from the crowd of greater gods responded, tacitly acquiescing to his words. No matter how strong the ban, it still wouldn’t be able to stop this kind of behavior that brought huge benefits.
Pandora's box had been opened.

chapters.title: Chapter 471: Response
chapters.content:
The Goddess of Darkness and the Beast God’s words caused the greater gods to fall silent. But not everyone agreed to go to war immediately. Things weren’t quite at that stage yet.
The thirteen greater gods sat around a round table, and in front of them was a list of names provided by Daisy, the Goddess of Darkness.
"Take a look at this first." Daisy said to the greater gods, "In less than half a month, over fifty gods were attacked, and most of them died from it… Especially in the first wave of victims, over 80% of them had their Godheads gouged out."
Due to the suddenness of the incident, even the greater gods didn't have time to count the number of victims.
So when such a shocking statistic was laid out before them, even though all of them were supreme beings, they couldn't help but be moved by it.
While the greater gods were certainly aloof and detached from lower beings, it didn't mean they were truly isolated from the world.
Every single greater god’s Divine Kingdom contained a large number of mortals and cultivators living there, and there were even subordinate gods residing there. It could be said that the Divine Kingdom of each greater god was a huge world.
And in such a situation, of course the greater gods would be concerned about the survival of the gods below them.
In a sense, the normal gods were their foundation. If all the normal gods were killed, then no new greater god would emerge in the future.
If this continued, then sooner or later, the World of Gods would suffer a full-scale invasion from its next-door neighbor.
This list given by Daisy was like the last straw that broke the camel's back, and Austin, who’d remained silent so far, finally spoke up at this moment.
"Even if we have to negotiate with that side, we must first cut off these hands that have stretched too far," Austin's voice didn't hold much emotion, but it contained an indescribable finality.
As soon as this Ruler of Light and Justice opened his mouth, none of the remaining four members of the Light Faction—including Valen—objected any further. Instead, they all acquiesced to Austin's stance in unison.
This was also a long-standing habit. Compared to the Dark Faction, which now had eight greater gods, the Light Faction was much more united—if they weren’t united, they might have been annihilated long ago.
"That's right. Instead of waiting for that side to place a ban, it's better for us to do it," this was Eugene, the Ruler of War and Austin's strongest backer.
The Light Faction already had a clear stance, and on the Dark Faction’s side, the Beast God was even the first one to propose going to war, so it looked like the tone of the response had already been set.
"Arrange for a group of Tier 9 and Tier 10 gods to step in and take care of those illegal trespassers." The Goddess of Darkness Daisy finally nodded, her eyes revealing a deep indifference. "Then… let’s give them a painful beating first."
……
Geng Chengyun followed Mai Cheng and the others and easily arrived at the World of Gods.
The five in their group were all Star Rulers, so it really wasn't difficult to cross over illegally. With the degree of control the Myriad Heavens had over this aspect, even many Void Cutters were able to smuggle themselves in.
On the contrary, because of the popularity of the "God Hunt" operation during this period, the price of space-time crystals had risen significantly, increasing the cost of smuggling, which led to fewer Void Cutters trying to cross the border illegally.
Geng Chengyun and the other Star Rulers weren’t concerned about this insignificant price. The problem in front of them was how to choose the right target.
"We have five Star Rulers, so it won’t be too hard to hunt gods as long as we follow what the manual says." Mai Cheng looked very confident. "The problem is that there are too many monks and not enough porridge right now, and it’ll be troublesome if we accidentally hunt someone else's target."
If there were two parties hunting the same god, of course the god wouldn’t be able to escape, but the distribution of the loot would be a big problem.
Each of the five of them had friendships with each other, and there was a foundation of trust between them, but a rival party was a different story.
For one, a realistic question had to be asked: Who would the Godhead be placed with? Regardless of which party it was placed with, it was impossible for the other party to feel at ease.
Geng Chengyun interjected, "I think we can first poke around and see which gods have already been hunted recently. That way, we can avoid making a trip in vain."
"The manual says that weak gods often create miracles in main planes, so why don't we start by looking in a main plane?"
"That works. As long as they've just created a miracle, they must still be alive."
The party members discussed amongst themselves, while Mai Cheng finally nodded and said, "Then let's split up and scout for information. Everyone should hurry. We'll gather at…"
Just as Mai Cheng was about to set the meeting place, he suddenly felt his heart sink as an inexplicable pressure rose from the depths of his soul.
A white light lit up from behind the crowd, and a silver-haired girl slowly stepped out, her icy gaze sweeping across the several people.
"My name is Quentina." The silver-haired girl held a silvery white longsword, pointing it straight at Mai Cheng and his group. "Are you Star Rulers who crossed over illegally?"
Mai Cheng was a little startled. He didn't expect for them to be so unlucky and be discovered as soon as they reached the World of Gods.
Someone behind him tugged on his sleeve and quickly whispered, "Quentina is the Holy Goddess, Tier 9…"
Before coming to the World of Gods, Mai Cheng had naturally done his homework and instantly realized who Quentina was, feeling his heart sink even further.
A Tier 9 god just came up to them directly. This…
Mai Cheng, who felt like he was caught red-handed, was unable to speak for a moment, so Geng Chengyun behind him hurriedly responded, "Lord Quentina, we are from the Myriad Heavens, but we just came over to collect resources. We didn't commit any evil deeds!"
Only after Geng Chengyun’s reminder did Mai Cheng come to his senses: ‘That's right! We haven’t even done anything yet. Even if the other party is a Tier 9 god, she still can’t just attack like this, can she?’
But in the end, they were still in a foreign land, so Mai Cheng wasn't stupid enough to butt heads with Quentina. He quickly showed a respectful expression and said, "He's right. My Lord, we—"
"No need to say more," Quentina interrupted Mai Cheng, and with a flash of the silver longsword in her hand, a silver colored holy light shone on the five people.
The five of them felt that they were unable to keep any secrets under this holy light, as if they were stripped bare and placed there.
In the next moment, Quentina spoke once again, "No Godhead here. All of you, get lost immediately and run back to that side."
"My Lord, this…" Mai Cheng froze, still wanting to object slightly.
Quentina coldly turned her head to him. "If I still see you loitering around the edge of the world half an hour later, you won't get a second chance."
After saying that, this Holy Goddess had no intention of sparing them a second glance as her figure instantly disappeared.
Mai Cheng took a deep breath and said indignantly, "These gods are really… so overbearing!"
Geng Chengyun, however, looked as if he had just survived a calamity. "Brother Mai, we'd better hurry up and leave… I have a premonition that this is because of the God Hunt."
The rest of the team also nodded. Quentina's words "No Godhead here" was in itself enough to illustrate the problem.
There really was going to be a major change soon.
Geng Chengyun glanced at the place where Quentina had vanished and suddenly felt like he was witnessing history with his very own eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 472: Enmity
chapters.content:
Geng Chengyun and his party were actually very lucky.
They ran into the Holy Goddess Quentina, a Tier 9 god from the Light Faction and a typical clean freak who’d always detested any contact with blood.
Otherwise, a team of five Star Rulers traveling together like them probably would’ve been captured immediately, even if they didn’t have any Godhead on them.
And once the "God Hunting Manual" was found to be in their possession, then nothing more would need to be said.
Moreover, if they ran into some of the more brutal people in the Dark Faction, killing them on the spot wouldn’t be out of the question.
Although Geng Chengyun and his team left in a hurry, a large number of other Star Rulers still lingered in the World of Gods. Their goal naturally didn’t need much elaboration—they all came here for Godheads.
The godly hierarchy also reacted with extreme speed as soon as the thirteen greater gods made their decision, with a group of powerful gods being quickly dispatched to specifically look for Star Rulers who crossed over illegally.
The matter of illegal crossings had previously received little attention from either side.
Star Rulers benefited from this and could easily come to the World of Gods, but on the flip side, they were also easily caught by the gods because they didn't do enough to hide their traces.
Thus, this wave of God Hunts started by Gu Nan was quickly suppressed through overwhelming force.
But as stated earlier, Pandora’s box was already open, and everything had just started.
……
Myriad Heavens.
If it was the gods next door who were on edge earlier, then now, it was the Star Rulers’ turn to voice their grievances.
The greater gods had responded too decisively. A majority of the Star Rulers who sneaked over were killed outright, while half of the remaining ones were searched, and the manuals they carried were discovered. Naturally, those people also suffered the same fate.
Only a very small portion of the luckier ones—or innocents who truly weren't involved in the God Hunt—were repatriated back.
But even then, accidental killings couldn't be avoided, and even some innocent Star Rulers who had gone to the World of Gods a long time ago and didn't even know about the God Hunt were affected by this purge.
More importantly, be it Star Rulers or gods, they weren’t alone and had a huge network of relationships behind them.
This was how enmity was formed.
In a rare moment, Song Fei was feeling a headache as he stared at the disciple standing in front of him inside Academic Heaven.
Song Fei had many direct disciples, but only a handful actually succeeded and became truly powerful Star Rulers.
Graceful Heaven’s Fang Chaoyun naturally counted as one, but Old Fang had always been hot-tempered, even if he cultivated the supposedly calm and composed Dao of Confucianism.
So the disciple Song Fei had the highest hopes for wasn’t Fang Chaoyun, but the person before him.
Phoenix Feather Heaven’s Shi Yeyan. His Tier 9 cultivation was slightly lower than Fang Chaoyun’s, but his mentality and temperament were way better.
Fang Chaoyun ran to Academic Heaven practically everyday, yet besides the routine respects Shi Yeyan came to pay, he had never gone to Academic Heaven for his own matters in almost a hundred years.
Which was why the one time he did come for personal matters, Song Fei had to give him justice, as well as give himself justice.
"Master, you know it too." Shi Yeyan said calmly, "Youngest Martial Brother traveled to the World of Gods six hundred years ago to study the difference between the power of faith and the Shinto path’s incense prayers, so how could he be related to the God Hunt?"
"Just two days ago, Youngest Martial Brother even sent a letter back, saying that he finally had a breakthrough in his research and that he hoped to return within a few decades. He also said he misses the meals in his hometown…"
A trace of anger finally entered Shi Yeyan’s voice as he continued, "Master, Youngest Martial Brother doesn't even know what's happening on this side, so how can he be related to the God Hunt?"
Hearing this, Song Fei already understood what Shi Yeyan wanted to say and sighed softly.
The “Youngest Martial Brother” Shi Yeyan mentioned was none other than Song Fei's closed door disciple, Lu Yang, who’d been interested in all sorts of obscure and esoteric paths ever since he started cultivating.
Six hundred years ago, Lu Yang suddenly became enamored with the Dao of incense prayers, and after studying the relevant spells, he ran to the World of Gods and never returned even now.
Song Fei knew better than anyone else that it was impossible for Lu Yang to be interested in the God Hunt—plenty of Void Cutters in Academic Heaven would be willing to help Song Fei’s direct disciple if he wanted assistance, so why would he need to do such a thing?
But Song Fei also knew that one must remain calm at times like this. If even they—the Unified Dao powerhouses—let emotions affect their decisions, then war between the two sides would be inevitable.
So Song Fei said in a low voice, "I will give him justice, but not now."
Shi Yeyan was silent for a while before he slowly nodded.
……
Song Fei summoned all the Unified Dao cultivators as soon as he sent Shi Yeyan away.
In fact, as a latecomer among the Unified Dao group, not everyone would give him face, but this time was an exception.
Apart from Zi Luo Elder—whose whereabouts were unknown—even the ever-elusive Jiu Po showed up. Every single one of the original Thirteen Heavens was present, with not a single person missing.
"How rare it is to see you!" Weapon Martial Heaven’s Zou Jiming looked to the side and revealed an amused expression.
Beside him stood a bearded man with an average face, wearing plain black clothes. From appearance alone, no one would believe that he ruled over the most mysterious of the Thirteen Heavens, Jiu Po Heaven.
Jiu Po didn't mind the jab at all and also smiled. "If you want to see me so much, how about I pay your Weapon Martial Heaven a visit every day from now on?"
"No way!" Zou Jiming hastily waved his hand. "I can't afford to provide for a great god like you."
It was true that there weren't many opportunities for the Unified Dao powerhouses to meet, but now was clearly not the time for casual greetings. Song Fei coughed lightly and said, "Everyone, let's get down to business."
Zou Jiming turned to Song Fei again. "Old Song, I heard your disciple was also killed? Don't be polite to those gods; let them see what it means to be the most overprotective person in the Myriad Heavens."
In terms of pulling aggro with his words, Classmate Zou Jiming was definitely on a completely different level. The No.1 Aggro Puller in the Myriad Heavens was none other than him.
Song Fei already knew his personality and ignored this person altogether. He redirected the topic back to the official subject, "It’s very likely that this God Hunt movement will lead to the beginning of a war. What is everyone's opinion?"
Lu Wen was the first to speak up, "We need to first catch the person who planned all this, or else who knows what kinds of schemes the mastermind is still hiding?"
"The mastermind should certainly be investigated, but now that things are already like this, finding out won't affect the big picture." Yu Lian said, "Godheads can create Void Cutters—now that this is common knowledge, who can guarantee that the Star Rulers down below won't be swayed?"
Lu Wen didn't say anything else, because he knew what Yu Lian said was true.
Don't be fooled by how the gods were able to hunt down Star Rulers en masse in the World of Gods right now. That was because many people were blinded by greed and weren't careful enough when smuggling themselves in.
After this wave of purging passes, Star Rulers have countless ways to sneak around secretly. They could even ask others to do it for them.
Everyone was a Star Ruler. Who among them was truly dumb?
Faced with such a situation, the thirteen Unified Dao cultivators were truly in a dilemma.

chapters.title: Chapter 473: Meeting Of The Thirteen Heavens
chapters.content:
Star Rulers hunting gods had become an act that concerned the core interests of the weaker Star Rulers, so it was never something that could be stopped as long as a ban was issued.
The thirteen Unified Dao existences were well aware of this.
But then again, judging from the fact that Lu Wen was still in the mood to look for the mastermind, it was clear that they weren’t as anxious as the greater gods next door.
This time, certain gods were hunted down, and some of the Star Rulers were also killed by powerful gods from the World of Gods, so both sides suffered considerable losses.
But the dead couldn’t be brought back to life. Instead, they needed to concern themselves with the future.
Those in the World of Gods had to curb the God Hunt at all costs, or else the gods would be killed off sooner or later, while the Myriad Heavens had no such worries—the weak Star Rulers would get scared as soon as their death count increased. It wasn’t like they would continue to foolishly throw their lives away.
What really gave the Thirteen Heavens a headache was the fact that the greater gods of the Worlds of Gods had such an uncompromising stance on this matter, making them at a loss on how to respond.
Song Fei's youngest disciple dying in the World of Gods was no longer a secret among the Unified Dao figures; they naturally had their own intelligence sources.
They even knew that such situations were by no means few and far between. Perhaps they might even encounter the same situation as Song Fei in the future. So other than someone with a big heart like Zou Jiming, no one would make light of this.
Or rather, by the time more and more Star Rulers were affected, the web of connections would sooner or later implicate them as well.
So by tacit agreement, nobody present brought this up first. They were all waiting for Song Fei to speak up and make a decision. As long as he made a decision, everyone else could just follow suit, and any curses from below would only be directed at Song Fei first.
Song Fei looked around and saw that each and every one of these Unified Dao figures either made it clear that it was none of their business or were filled with righteous indignation but never had any intention of speaking up, so he could only sigh in secret.
"A war cannot be started lightly," after a moment of silence, Song Fei finally provided a response that satisfied the crowd, and the crowd also seemed to let out a collective sigh of relief.
The Unified Dao existences were waiting for precisely this statement!
If the Light Faction in the World of Gods could be described as incomparably united and the Dark Faction slightly less united, then the Myriad Heavens’ leaders were basically scattered sand.
The Thirteen Heavens were all fighting their own battles. At most, two people might have a slightly better relationship, forming an offensive and defensive alliance or something similar, but there had never been any united factions to speak of.
If they truly went to war with the World of Gods, it would definitely be the Myriad Heavens’ side that would have more problems.
What's more, the greater gods over there actually wanted to go to war. On one hand, they wanted to vent some anger, and on the other hand, they also wanted to strike fear into the Star Rulers on this side, turning the "ban" on the God Hunt into a real ban.
For them, stopping a loss was the same as gaining a victory.
But what would the Thirteen Heavens gain by starting a war? Nothing!
The ones who would get the Godheads were the weak Star Rulers just starting out, but the ones who would have to fight the war were the Unified Dao figures. Their victory wouldn’t bring any benefits, and their defeat would just be laughed at, so who would be willing to do such a thing?
But although it would be nice to admit defeat against the gods, they would get a cowardly reputation if word spread, so everyone was waiting for Song Fei to take the lead.
After Song Fei glanced at everyone’s expressions, his face suddenly showed some amusement as he changed the subject, "Indeed, the matter of the God Hunt benefits others at our own detriment, so it shouldn’t be done. But this humble one’s youngest disciple, Lu Yang, was residing in the World of Gods 600 years ago. How could he be related to this matter?"
The Unified Dao cultivators didn't expect him to suddenly change the subject, and while they were still taken aback, Song Fei continued, "This humble one is willing to go to the World of Gods alone to seek justice for my youngest disciple. I would like to ask that all of you please stay at the headquarters to avoid any misunderstandings from that side."
The crowd finally understood Song Fei's intentions this time. He wanted to be the only hero and make everyone else endorse him!
A silver-haired man who’d been silent so far smiled lightly and replied, "Since Daoist Friend Song's disciple was wrongly accused, is there any reason to ignore this injustice? This humble one is willing to go with Daoist Friend."
This was Milky Way Heaven’s Star Ruler Si Yun, the same person who was hiding a Nine Abyss Heavenly Demon in his astral world, the only starry sea-type astral world in the Thirteen Heavens.
Song Fei put on a troubled smile and dissuaded, "That's why this humble one said that a war should not be started lightly—"
"Say no more! How can we let outsiders bully people from our Myriad Heavens? We’re going together!"
"That’s right. Didn’t just a few gods get hunted down? That was due to their lack of ability, but now they’re retaliating by killing innocent people. Do they really think my Myriad Heavens has no one?"
The crowd was so excited that no trace of the previous silence could be seen.
Those not in the know might mistake this for Song Fei's ability to rally supporters. It might even make for a riveting story to pass on to future generations, but only the parties involved knew what was going on.
Song Fei had always urged everyone to focus on the big picture. It was enough for him alone to go; the others shouldn’t casually take action.
How could he be willing to be the first to cause war? Although being the leader would improve his reputation in the eyes of weaker Star Rulers, it might not necessarily be the case in the powerful Star Rulers’ circles.
After all, they also didn’t lack Void Cutters. If they were unable to benefit from the God Hunt but still had to contribute to the war because Song Fei was leading the way, then wouldn’t all the blame fall onto him, Song Fei?
But Song Fei's words had already left his mouth, so the rest of the Unified Dao existences couldn’t possibly let him take them back. Regardless of his intentions, the "pro-war faction" label had already been forced onto Song Fei's head.
……
"Many thanks, Master!"
Shi Yeyan had remained inside Academic Heaven, and when Song Fei returned, he was already greeting him with a deep salute.
Song Fei wasn’t really surprised. He knew that as soon as the words left his mouth, the others would spread them far and wide, cementing his stance as the leader of the pro-war faction.
"You and I are master and disciple, so there's no need to say this." Song Fei was prepared for this and said with a faint smile, "You are coming along with me this time. But remember, we're only there to seek justice for your Youngest Martial Brother."
"Your disciple understands." Shi Yeyan was meticulous and was well aware of what kind of predicament Song Fei was facing. He responded solemnly, "We travel the world with reason and must not rush indiscriminately into war."
Song Fei nodded. "Let’s go."
……
After the meeting of the Thirteen Heavens, Song Fei returned to Academic Heaven alone, but he knew that someone would come over very soon.
"I didn't expect the first visitor to be you." Song Fei looked at the person in front of him with an
I knew it
smile on his face.
Only two figures stood across from each other in the empty hall. After all, Song Fei naturally wouldn’t let his disciples watch his meetings with Unified Dao powerhouses.
The visitor was Weapon Martial Heaven’s Zou Jiming.
This Unified Dao cultivator who was very good at pulling aggro had mocked Song Fei to his face mere hours ago, but now he changed his tune and ran over to see him in private without the slightest hint of embarrassment.
"Our thoughts are the same," Zou Jiming cut straight to the chase, starting with this sentence.
"Oh?" Song Fei was noncommittal.
"You don't want a war." Zou Jiming continued, "As long as a war starts, you’ll be criticized no matter whether you win or lose, and I also don't want a war."
Face didn’t really matter for people at the level of the Thirteen Heavens, but when no concrete benefits were involved, sometimes the fight really was about reputation.
The better their reputation, the easier it was to attract other talents, which was no different from a normal Star Ruler.
"Why?"
Zou Jiming met Song Fei's gaze and said seriously, "Because of the Heaven-God Alliance."

chapters.title: Chapter 474: Nightmare Continent
chapters.content:
Yes, because of the Heaven-God Alliance.
One had to admit that the existence of the Heaven-God Alliance significantly influenced the overall situation of the Myriad Heavens.
Song Fei would inevitably pay attention to the Heaven-God Alliance because it contained his old rival, Zi Luo Elder. And Zou Jiming would also pay attention to the Heaven-God Alliance because it contained his potential rival, Xue Ren.
In a way, both Song Fei and Zou Jiming were threatened by certain members in the Heaven-God Alliance, but the two were different.
Song Fei could directly attack Zi Luo Elder without much scruple since the two of them had a personal vendetta.
But it would be a big problem for Zou Jiming to openly attack Xue Ren—there were too many people who could threaten Zou Jiming, and killing a single Xue Ren would make him the target of criticism in the blink of an eye.
That was why Zou Jiming was relieved when the Heaven-God Alliance appeared.
If Xue Ren could run to the World of Gods to ascend to Unified Dao, then the conflict between him and Zou Jiming would disappear. Instead, there would be one more weapon path Unified Dao cultivator to help Zou Jiming share the pressure. It was a total win-win situation.
Therefore, he didn't want the two sides to go to war. If they did, it would be much more difficult for Xue Ren to break through to Unified Dao on that side.
These two—one a supporter of the Heaven-God Alliance and the other a mortal enemy of the Heaven-God Alliance—shared a common goal regarding whether or not to go to war.
Song Fei stared at him for a long time before finally speaking, "In that case, I’ll have to ask Brother Zou for help."
……
Gu Nan was sitting inside his Divine Kingdom, not in the slightest hurry. He was leisurely sipping tea and reading a light novel.
Ever since the Weak Gods Hunting Manual was published, he’d stayed inside his Divine Kingdom and never stepped foot outside again. At the same time, he also rejected all visits from Star Rulers, acting as if he was in closed-door cultivation until death.
On one hand, it was to avoid suspicion, and on the other hand, it was also because he didn't want to communicate with anyone—at times like these, the more he said, the more he might let something slip.
After all, anyone with a discerning eye could see that the person who wrote the Weak Gods Hunting Manual was bound to be someone who had an extremely thorough understanding of the World of Gods and the gods.
To be precise, when it came to god-slaying techniques, not even the gods themselves were any match for Gu Nan.
It was only until the content from the meeting of the Thirteen Heavens came in that Gu Nan finally put down the light novel in his hands.
"Song Fei is leading?" Gu Nan rubbed his chin, seemingly pondering something.
Gu Nan was already aware of the fact that Song Fei's youngest disciple had been framed and murdered. This wasn’t out of his expectations.
It wasn't that he was great at predicting the future. Rather, he knew that this kind of event would happen sooner or later as time went on—if not with Song Fei, then with someone else.
It’s just that the Thirteen Heavens' determination to go to war was a bit out of his expectations. He’d thought that this group of people wouldn't do such a strenuous and thankless task.
"It's even better if they start fighting; it’ll save me a lot of trouble. But I’m afraid they still have some ulterior motives…" Gu Nan didn't believe figures at the level of the Thirteen Heavens would have such simple plans.
Gu Nan thought for a moment, then said to Red Tail, who’d come over, "Investigate what other information can be used. We can't count on this group of Unified Dao cultivators."
Red Tail seemed already prepared for this and handed over a piece of intelligence.
"Lu Yang still has a wife and son in the World of Gods. His wife used to be a well-known beauty in the Nightmare Continent, and his son just turned fourteen."
Here, Red Tail couldn't help chuckling as she added, "We found out that there’s a God of Lust in the Dark Faction—"
"It's true that Houston is the God of Lust, but that doesn't mean he's a pervert himself," Gu Nan interrupted Red Tail with a wave of his hand.
God of Lust Houston, one of the Tier 8 gods, had a divine authority precisely related to passion and lust.
But just because that was his law didn’t necessarily mean the god himself was lustful; in fact, Houston was an ascetic fellow who usually didn't even touch women.
Red Tail stared blankly, as if she hadn't expected this outcome.
"But your thought process is still very good!" Gu Nan patted Red Tail's shoulder and said with narrowed eyes, "Give me the information on Lu Yang's wife and son. I'll make a personal trip there."
"Yes."
……
Lu Yang's wife and son were a breakthrough—Gu Nan was well aware of that.
Everyone was extremely tense right now. Though the higher-ups on both sides maintained a certain degree of restraint, it was much harder for the Star Rulers and gods under them to have such sensible judgment.
In the end, this was because it concerned their direct interests, while the higher-ups were looking more towards the future.
But in a situation like this, all it takes is one more gentle push, and everything can become irreconcilable.
What? You’re saying one push might not be enough? Then just keep pushing!
Gu Nan, who never harbored expectations of succeeding on the first try, once again came to the World of Gods.
In fact, the residents of the World of Gods already tightened control considerably over visitors from the Myriad Heavens. Every visitor had to be inspected, especially those at Void Cutter Realm or above.
However, these measures obviously couldn’t stump Gu Nan, who was all too familiar with the gods’ abilities and had too many ways to deal with them.
‘Song Fei and the others should be coming over soon, so I need to hurry,’ Gu Nan thought, having already memorized the information Red Tail provided.
Nightmare Continent.
One of the main planes under the control of the Dark Faction. Although the name sounded very sinister, it was essentially a pretty normal main plane.
The reason this place was called Nightmare Continent was simply because the god who first conquered this continent was none other than the original God of Nightmares, now the Ruler of Nightmares.
Of course, because it was under the control of the Ruler of Nightmares for many years, there were still many related traces left on this continent.
For example, Gu Nan was currently standing in front of an inverted garden, a typical Nightmare grotto-heaven.
"This is the 391st Nightmare Land, My Lord," a man in a black suit stood in front of Gu Nan and respectfully explained.
The garden in front of the two hung upside down in the air in a strange state, and all the birds and beasts within it were likewise upside down.
There were many bizarre Nightmare Lands like this on Nightmare Continent, but these types of places often had a strange distribution of laws, making them an excellent place for adventurers to further their training.
Lu Yang's only son on this side, Lu Jialiang, was studying in this particular Nightmare Land.
"I heard those who can study here are all students from well-off families?" Gu Nan asked casually as he looked at this inverted garden.
He knew a little about Nightmare Continent, but it wasn't considered comprehensive, at least not to the extent of knowing it like the back of his hand.
"Yes." The man in a suit nodded with a smile. "The 391st Nightmare Land is a famous aristocratic academy. Ordinary people can't afford the tuition here."
"Has anything strange happened here recently?"
"I don’t think so… Everything is normal—oh right, two days ago, there was a boy who got in a fight and seemed to suffer a head wound, but we haven’t been able to contact his family."
Gu Nan revealed an odd smile and nodded.
And at this moment, within the 391st Nightmare Land, the boy named Lu Jialiang was hiding alone in a corner, bloodstains still lingering on his forehead.
His gaze held a trace of anger. He clenched his fists, then gripped a pendant on his chest.
"Damn you, Brook, you’ll pay for this!"

chapters.title: Chapter 475: Murder Suspect
chapters.content:
Lu Jialiang just celebrated his fourteenth birthday half a month ago.
But this fourteen year old was way too mature for his age. It wasn't because Lu Jialiang matured early, but because reality forced him to grow up.
On his fourteenth birthday, the boy didn't get to meet his father, whom he could only see once a year. His mother came alone, bringing bad news.
Lu Jialiang subconsciously tightened his grip on the pendant.
‘Something has happened to Father… I know it!’ Lu Jialiang thought.
Even though it wasn't explicitly stated, the look on his mother's face at the time clearly told Lu Jialiang this. And the fact that his mother didn't take him away meant an even more terrifying truth.
Even his mother couldn't guarantee her own safety and didn't dare bring him with her, preferring to place him in a safer place like the Nightmare Land.
"Brook must know something…" The teen's gaze was slightly cold, his mind crystal clear.
Brook's uncle was the personal attendant of a powerful god, and even though he wasn't particularly powerful himself, he was definitely well-informed.
If not, Brook wouldn't have dared to deliberately find trouble for Lu Jialiang.
As he thought of this, Lu Jialiang curled in further on himself, trying to keep himself completely hidden in the shadows, his eyes firmly locked on the space in front of him.
This was the path Brook must take to return to the dormitory!
"He’s coming."
Accompanied by the sound of footsteps, Brook's staggering figure appeared in his sight. Brook, who was already over twenty-five years old, was at the age where he couldn’t go without alcohol, and even in Nightmare Land, he still maintained the habit of heavy drinking.
Lu Jialiang stepped forward. The hand gripping his pendant shot out as the pendant instantly transformed into a longsword, pointing directly at Brook.
Brook was still inebriated, so how could he react to this kind of surprise attack? His shoulder was instantly impaled by the sword, which was actually the result of Lu Jialiang avoiding his vitals.
Perhaps not even Lu Jialiang himself expected his attack to land so easily. He, who’d never seen bloodshed before, was also startled.
But the teenager quickly calmed down, putting on a cold expression as he looked at Brook and asked icily, "Brook, do you want to live or die? Tell me exactly what happened!"
The sharp pain coming from his shoulder sobered up Brook, and at the same time, he also saw the face of his attacker.
"Lu! You… You dare to ambush me!" Brook didn’t feel any panic, instead getting angry. Because he knew the other party would never dare kill him, or else it would be impossible for him to leave this place alive.
"Do you believe there are still people who can save you? How ridiculous!" Brook was so furious that he laughed. "It won't be long before you're arrested by those powerful people, you foreigner bastard!"
Lu Jialiang's unique name was a bright beacon that highlighted his origins, and this was his biggest conflict with the natives.
Fire raged in Lu Jialiang's heart. He really wanted to kill this hateful fellow, but in the end, he didn't completely lose his sanity.
There was still hope for escape if he left Nightmare Land now, but killing Brook would immediately trigger the alarm, and he wouldn't be able to leave once that happened!
Having already confirmed his suspicions, was giving up his own life in exchange for this idiot's life worth it?
Lu Jialiang didn't need to think much and made a decision right away.
He pulled out his longsword, then slapped Brook fiercely and added a few more kicks to vent some anger before he quickly turned around and fled.
Brook was dizzy from the beating. It was a while before he came back to his senses and hastily pressed a hand to the wound on his shoulder.
"Damned bastard… W-Who are you?!" He struggled to get up, but then he finally noticed the white-robed youth standing before him.
This person completely ignored him and just lowered his head, studying the wound on Brook’s shoulder.
The next second, a jet black longsword appeared. The sword’s length, width, and sharpness were actually identical to Lu Jialiang's longsword.
Thunk!
The sword instantly pierced Brook's heart, and the latter's eyes widened in disbelief as he slowly collapsed.
……
Lu Jialiang was startled by the blaring of an alarm that resounded throughout the night sky before he even had a chance to leave Nightmare Land.
By the time he wanted to hurry up and leave, it was already too late. The relevant personnel had sealed the entrances and exits of Nightmare Land as soon as the alarm went off, prohibiting anyone from entering or leaving.
"Damn it… Just who the hell triggered the alarm at a time like this?" Lu Jialiang naturally didn't think he caused this, because he hadn't killed Brook.
As for that tiny sword wound, it was just a superficial injury. Nightmare Land wouldn't even care about this kind of thing.
Lu Jialiang had no choice but to return to his dormitory and wait for the alarm to be lifted before trying to sneak out of Nightmare Land.
It wasn't until a slightly imposing middle-aged man with a stiff expression appeared in front of Lu Jialiang with a group of people that the teen realized the turn of events was a little worrying.
"Lord Andy, he is Lu Jialiang," the person in charge of this Nightmare Land respectfully stood to the side and said to the middle-aged man.
Lu Jialiang recognized the other party. He had once seen this person appear together with Brook… He was Brook’s uncle!
Legend had it that he was a god's trusted aide, and his own strength had also reached the peak of Legend Rank…
‘It’s okay! Your father is a legendary Star Ruler!’ Lu Jialiang secretly encouraged himself. Even if something might have happened to his father, he still must not disgrace him!
However, the first sentence from the other party froze Lu Jialiang on the spot.
"Were you the one who killed Brook?" Brook's uncle asked flatly, his expression not even changing for a second.
"No! I didn’t!" Lu Jialiang instantly roared. He couldn't stand the fact that someone else was framing him for a crime he didn’t commit. "I just stabbed him once. He—"
The teen’s voice came to an abrupt halt as he saw Brook's corpse being slowly carried up.
Brook's uncle didn't say anything. He just leveled a cold gaze at Lu Jialiang, then suddenly reached out and grabbed the pendant in front of Lu Jialiang's chest. With a forceful jerk, the silver longsword was once again pulled out.
This middle-aged man named Andy calmly examined the longsword for a couple of moments, then said, "It matches perfectly with those two sword wounds. This sword can be brought back as physical evidence."
"W-What do you mean…?" Lu Jialiang's heart sank slightly. The bad feeling grew stronger, and he gradually started to retreat.
Andy grabbed his shoulder and replied coldly, "It means that you will return with us to the Divine Kingdom to be judged as a murder suspect."
"I didn't kill anyone!" Lu Jialiang's roar became even louder as he bared his teeth, seeing all this as a plot by the other party to frame him.
Andy, however, just said calmly, "Brook became an apostle of our Lord two years ago. Even though he sometimes isn’t pious enough, he cannot be murdered for no reason."
"Now then, please allow me to take him away," he said to the person in charge of this Nightmare Land.

chapters.title: Chapter 476: Shi Yeyan
chapters.content:
Shi Yeyan and his teacher quickly arrived at the World of Gods.
Their arrival wasn’t hidden from anyone; everything was under the watchful eye of gods from the World of Gods. There was also no need to hide it, as they had come to seek justice for Lu Yang.
The only Unified Dao cultivator who ended up accompanying them was Zou Jiming. The others didn't actually come along.
It was enough to force Song Fei to carry the mantle of pro-war leader. It wasn't like they truly wanted to start a war between the two sides.
"Teacher, I'll go retrieve Youngest Martial Brother’s family first," Shi Yeyan said as soon as they reached this side.
"Okay." Song Fei nodded. "I'll meet with Kenneth. Make sure to ensure the safety of your Youngest Martial Brother's wife and son."
Kenneth was precisely the real name of the Ruler of Nightmares. Lu Yang usually resided in Nightmare Continent, and it was also here that he was falsely accused of murder, so of course this blame should be shouldered by Kenneth.
"Yes," Shi Yeyan agreed, then gave a respectful bow to the Zou Jiming beside them before he quickly left.
"What a good upbringing!" Zou Jiming remarked with emotion. Even under such circumstances, Shi Yeyan still remembered to pay him respect. If it was his subordinates instead, they would’ve disappeared without a trace already.
Song Fei replied with a smile, "If you're willing to send a few people to Academic Heaven, I promise to help you discipline them well."
"Forget it." Zou Jiming waved his hand. If he really sent people to Academic Heaven, they might not even be his people anymore after all the brainwashing was done.
……
Shi Yeyan quickly found Lu Yang's wife in the World of Gods. In fact, all this information was semi-public and wasn’t hard to find.
Lu Yang's wife was called Sophia. She wasn’t some amazing bigshot, just a woman native to Nightmare Continent.
Decades ago, Lu Yang's soul was damaged due to an accident during his experiments and even his residence was blown to smithereens, but he also befriended Sophia as a result.
Lu Yang, who was depressed at the time, was only able to overcome his depression with Sophia's advice and encouragement, and at the same time, he also fell in love with this mortal woman, ultimately taking her as his wife.
Later on, he found a way to prolong Sophia's life and also had a son with her, which brought them to the present situation.
"I am Lu Yang's Senior Martial Brother," Shi Yeyan calmly looked at the woman before him and spoke.
The woman standing in front of him looked to only be in her twenties, with an indescribable charm to her features, but her expression was somewhat haggard.
"G-Greetings," Sophia said cautiously, "My Lord, is Lu Yang… really not coming back? "
Sophia, a mortal who wasn’t even Legend Rank, only saw Lu Yang being taken away by those high and mighty gods and still hoped there was a chance her husband could return.
